laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: The God of majesty * hath thundered, ascribe to the Lord glory to his name.

laudes.canticle1.label: Canticum 211
laudes.canticle1.antiphonLat: Laudámus nomen tuum * ínclitum, Deus noster.
laudes.canticle1.antiphonEng: O God of majesty, * we praise thy glorious name.

verses.lat: (Canticum David * 1 Par. 29:10-13)
verses.eng: (Canticle of David * 1 Chron. 29:10-13)

verses.lat: 29:10 Benedíctus es, Dómine, Deus Israël patris nostri, * ab ætérno in ætérnum.
verses.eng: 29:10 Blessed art thou, O Lord the God of Israel, our father * from eternity to eternity.

verses.lat: 29:11 Tua est, Dómine, magnificéntia, et poténtia, * et glória, atque victória:
verses.eng: 29:11 Thine, O Lord, is magnificence, and power, * and glory, and victory:

verses.lat: 29:11 Et tibi laus: * cuncta enim quæ in cælo sunt, et in terra, tua sunt:
verses.eng: 29:11 And to thee is praise: * for all that is in heaven, and in earth, is thine:

verses.lat: 29:11 Tuum, Dómine, regnum, * et tu es super omnes príncipes.
verses.eng: 29:11 Thine is the kingdom, O Lord, * and thou art above all princes.

verses.lat: 29:12 Tuæ divítiæ, et tua est glória: * tu domináris ómnium,
verses.eng: 29:12 Thine are riches, and thine is glory, * thou hast dominion over all,

verses.lat: 29:12 In manu tua virtus et poténtia: * in manu tua magnitúdo, et impérium ómnium.
verses.eng: 29:12 In thy hand is power and might: * in thy hand greatness, and the empire of all things.

verses.lat: 29:13 Nunc ígitur, Deus noster, confitémur tibi, * et laudámus nomen tuum ínclitum.
verses.eng: 29:13 Now therefore our God we give thanks to thee, * and we praise thy glorious name.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Laudámus nomen tuum * ínclitum, Deus noster.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: O God of majesty, * we praise thy glorious name.

laudes.psalm4.label: Psalmus 116
laudes.psalm4.antiphonEng: O praise the Lord, * all ye nations.

verses.lat: 116:1 Laudáte Dóminum, omnes gentes: * laudáte eum, omnes pópuli:
verses.eng: 116:1 Praise the Lord, all ye nations: * praise him, all ye people.

verses.lat: 116:2 Quóniam confirmáta est super nos misericórdia ejus: * et véritas Dómini manet in ætérnum.
verses.eng: 116:2 For his mercy is confirmed upon us: * and the truth of the Lord remaineth for ever.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: O praise the Lord, * all ye nations.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (2 Cor 1:3-4)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Benedíctus Deus, et Pater Dómini nostri Jesu Christi, Pater misericordiárum, et Deus totíus consolatiónis, qui consolátur nos in omni tribulatióne nostra.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort, who comforteth us in all our tribulation.

capitulum_laudes.label: Capitulum (Rom 13:12-13)
capitulum_laudes.lat: Nox præcéssit, dies autem appropinquávit. Abiciámus ergo ópera tenebrárum, et induámur arma lucis. Sicut in die honéste ambulémus.
capitulum_laudes.eng: The night is passed, and the day is at hand. Let us therefore cast off the works of darkness, and put on the armour of light. Let us walk honestly, as in the day.

versum_tertia.label: Versiculus
versum_tertia.lat: ℣. Adjútor meus, esto, ne derelínquas me.
versum_tertia.eng: ℣. Be Thou my helper, forsake me not.
versum_tertia.latR: ℟. Neque despícias me, Deus, salutáris meus.
versum_tertia.engR: ℟. Do not Thou despise me, O God my Saviour.

versum_sexta.label: Versiculus
versum_sexta.lat: ℣. Dóminus regit me, et nihil mihi déerit.
versum_sexta.eng: ℣. The Lord ruleth me: and I shall want nothing.
versum_sexta.latR: ℟. In loco páscuæ ibi me collocávit.
versum_sexta.engR: ℟. He hath set me in a place of pasture.

versum_nona.label: Versiculus
versum_nona.lat: ℣. Ab occúltis meis munda me, Dómine.
versum_nona.eng: ℣. From my secret ones cleanse me, O Lord.
versum_nona.latR: ℟. Et ab aliénis parce servo tuo.
versum_nona.engR: ℟. And from those of others spare Thy servant.

ant_1.label: Antíphona
ant_1.lat: Dóminus de cælo * prospéxit super fílios hóminum.
ant_1.eng: The Lord hath looked down from heaven * upon the children of men.

ant_2.label: Antíphona
ant_2.eng: I will love thee, * O Lord, who art my strength.

ant_3.label: Antíphona
ant_3.lat: Exáudiat te * Dóminus in die tribulatiónis.
ant_3.eng: May the Lord hear * thee in the day of tribulation.

nocturn_1_versum.label: Versicle after Nocturn I
nocturn_1_versum.latR: ℟. Qui salvos facis sperántes in te.
nocturn_1_versum.engR: ℟. Thou who savest them that trust in thee.

nocturn_2_versum.label: Versicle after Nocturn II
nocturn_2_versum.eng: ℣. I will give glory to thee, O Lord, among the nations.
nocturn_2_versum.engR: ℟. And I will sing a psalm to thy name.

nocturn_3_versum.label: Versicle after Nocturn III
nocturn_3_versum.eng: ℣. Sing to the Lord, O ye his saints.
nocturn_3_versum.engR: ℟. And give praise to the memory of his holiness.

hymnus_laudes.label: Hymn
hymnus_laudes.title: Splendor Patérnæ glóriæ
hymnus_laudes.lat:
Splendor Patérnæ glóriæ,
De luce lucem próferens,
Lux lucis, et fons lúminis,
Diem dies illúminans:

Verúsque sol illábere,
Micans nitóre pérpeti:
Jubárque Sancti Spíritus
Infúnde nostris sénsibus.

Votis vocémus et Patrem,
Patrem poténtis grátiæ,
Patrem perénnis glóriæ:
Culpam reléget lúbricam.

Confírmet actus strénuos:
Dentes retúndat ínvidi:
Casus secúndet ásperos:
Agénda recte dírigat.

Mentem gubérnet et regat:
Sit pura nobis cástitas:
Fides calóre férveat,
Fraudis venéna nésciat.

Christúsque nobis sit cibus,
Potúsque noster sit fides:
Læti bibámus sóbriam
Profusiónem Spíritus.

Lætus dies hic tránseat:
Pudor sit ut dilúculum:
Fides velut merídies:
Crepúsculum mens nésciat.

Auróra lucem próvehit,
Cum luce nobis pródeat
In Patre totus Fílius,
Et totus in Verbo Pater.

Deo Patri sit glória,
Ejúsque soli Fílio,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
Nunc et per omne sǽculum.
Amen.
hymnus_laudes.eng:
O splendour of God’s glory bright,
O thou that bringest light from light,
O light of light, light’s living spring,
O day, all days illumining.

O thou true sun, on us thy glance
Let fall in royal radiance,
The Spirit’s sanctifying beam
Upon our earthly senses stream.

The Father too our prayers implore,
Father of glory evermore,
The Father of all grace and might,
To banish sin from our delight:

To guide whate’er we nobly do,
With love all envy to subdue,
To make ill-fortune turn to fair,
And give us grace our wrongs to bear.

Our mind be in his keeping placed,
Our body true to him and chaste,
Where only faith her fire shall feed,
And burn the tares of Satan’s seed.

And Christ to us for food shall be,
From him our drink that welleth free,
The Spirit’s wine, that maketh whole,
And mocking not, exalts the soul.

Rejoicing may this day go hence,
Like virgin dawn our innocence,
Like fiery noon our faith appear,
Nor know the gloom of twilight drear.

Morn in her rosy car is borne;
Let him come forth our perfect morn,
The Word in God the Father One,
The Father perfect in the Son.

All laud to God the Father be;
All praise, Eternal Son, to thee;
All glory, as is ever meet,
To God the Holy Paraclete.
Amen.

hymnus_vespera.label: Hymn
hymnus_vespera.title: Imménse cæli Cónditor
hymnus_vespera.lat:
Imménse cæli Cónditor,
Qui mixta ne confúnderent,
Aquæ fluénta dívidens,
Cælum dedísti límitem.

Firmans locum cæléstibus,
Simúlque terræ rívulis;
Ut unda flammas témperet,
Terræ solum ne díssipent.

Infúnde nunc, piíssime,
Donum perénnis grátiæ:
Fraudis novæ ne cásibus
Nos error átterat vetus.

Lucem fides adáugeat:
Sic lúminis jubar ferat:
Hæc vana cuncta próterat:
Hanc falsa nulla cómprimant.

Præsta, Pater piíssime,
Patríque compar Únice,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito
Regnans per omne sǽculum.
Amen.
hymnus_vespera.eng:
O great Creator of the sky,
Who wouldest not the floods on high
With earthly waters to confound,
But mad’st the firmament their bound;

The floods above thou didst ordain;
The floods below thou didst restrain:
That moisture might attemper heat,
Lest the parched earth should ruin meet.

Upon our souls, good Lord, bestow
Thy gift of grace in endless flow:
Lest some renewed deceit or wile
Of former sin should us beguile.

Let faith discover heav’nly light;
So shall its rays direct us right:
And let this faith each error chase,
And never give to falsehood place.

Grant this, O Father, ever One
With Christ, thy sole-begotten Son,
And Holy Ghost, whom all adore,
Reigning and blest forevermore.
Amen.

ant_laudes.label: Antiphon ad Benedictus
ant_laudes.lat: Benedíctus * Dóminus Deus Israël, quia visitávit et liberávit nos.
ant_laudes.eng: Blessed be the Lord * the God of Israel, because he has visited and redeemed his people.

ant_vespera.label: Antiphon ad Magnificat
ant_vespera.lat: Magníficat * ánima mea Dóminum, quia respéxit Deus humilitátem meam.
ant_vespera.eng: My soul * magnifies the Lord, because God has regarded my lowliness.

versum_1.label: Versicle
versum_1.eng: We are filled in the morning with thy mercy.
versum_1.engR: And we have rejoiced, and are delighted.

matutinum.psalm2.label: Psalmus 34 (1-10)

verses.lat: 34:1 Júdica, Dómine, nocéntes me, * expúgna impugnántes me.
verses.eng: 34:1 Judge thou, O Lord, them that wrong me: * overthrow them that fight against me.

verses.lat: 34:2 Apprehénde arma et scutum: * et exsúrge in adjutórium mihi.
verses.eng: 34:2 Take hold of arms and shield: * and rise up to help me.

verses.lat: 34:3 Effúnde frámeam, et conclúde advérsus eos, qui persequúntur me: * dic ánimæ meæ: Salus tua ego sum.
verses.eng: 34:3 Bring out the sword, and shut up the way against them that persecute me: * say to my soul: I am thy salvation.

verses.lat: 34:4 Confundántur et revereántur, * quæréntes ánimam meam.
verses.eng: 34:4 Let them be confounded and ashamed * that seek after my soul.

verses.lat: 34:4 Avertántur retrórsum, et confundántur * cogitántes mihi mala.
verses.eng: 34:4 Let them be turned back and be confounded * that devise against me.

verses.lat: 34:5 Fiant tamquam pulvis ante fáciem venti: * et Ángelus Dómini coárctans eos.
verses.eng: 34:5 Let them become as dust before the wind: * and let the Angel of the Lord straiten them.

verses.lat: 34:6 Fiat via illórum ténebræ et lúbricum: * et Ángelus Dómini pérsequens eos.
verses.eng: 34:6 Let their way become dark and slippery; * and let the Angel of the Lord pursue them.

verses.lat: 34:7 Quóniam gratis abscondérunt mihi intéritum láquei sui: * supervácue exprobravérunt ánimam meam.
verses.eng: 34:7 For without cause they have hidden their net for me unto destruction: * without cause they have upbraided my soul.

verses.lat: 34:8 Véniat illi láqueus, quem ignórat: et cáptio, quam abscóndit, apprehéndat eum: * et in láqueum cadat in ipsum.
verses.eng: 34:8 Let the snare which he knoweth not come upon him: and let the net which he hath hidden catch him: * and into that very snare let them fall.

verses.lat: 34:9 Ánima autem mea exsultábit in Dómino: * et delectábitur super salutári suo.
verses.eng: 34:9 But my soul shall rejoice in the Lord; * and shall be delighted in his salvation.

verses.lat: 34:10 Ómnia ossa mea dicent: * Dómine, quis símilis tibi?
verses.eng: 34:10 All my bones shall say: * Lord, who is like to thee?

verses.lat: 34:10 Erípiens ínopem de manu fortiórum ejus: * egénum et páuperem a diripiéntibus eum.
verses.eng: 34:10 Who deliverest the poor from the hand of them that are stronger than he; * the needy and the poor from them that strip him.

matutinum.psalm2.antiphonEng: Overthrow, O Lord, * them that fight against me.

matutinum.psalm3.label: Psalmus 34 (11-17)

verses.lat: 34:11 Surgéntes testes iníqui, * quæ ignorábam interrogábant me.
verses.eng: 34:11 Unjust witnesses rising up * have asked me things I knew not.

verses.lat: 34:12 Retribuébant mihi mala pro bonis: * sterilitátem ánimæ meæ.
verses.eng: 34:12 They repaid me evil for good: * to the depriving me of my soul.

verses.lat: 34:13 Ego autem cum mihi molésti essent, * induébar cilício.
verses.eng: 34:13 But as for me, when they were troublesome to me, * I was clothed with haircloth.

verses.lat: 34:13 Humiliábam in jejúnio ánimam meam: * et orátio mea in sinu meo convertétur.
verses.eng: 34:13 I humbled my soul with fasting; * and my prayer shall be turned into my bosom.

verses.lat: 34:14 Quasi próximum, et quasi fratrem nostrum, sic complacébam: * quasi lugens et contristátus, sic humiliábar.
verses.eng: 34:14 As a neighbour and as an own brother, so did I please: * as one mourning and sorrowful so was I humbled.

verses.lat: 34:15 Et advérsum me lætáti sunt, et convenérunt: * congregáta sunt super me flagélla, et ignorávi.
verses.eng: 34:15 But they rejoiced against me, and came together: * scourges were gathered together upon me, and I knew not.

verses.lat: 34:16 Dissipáti sunt, nec compúncti, tentavérunt me, subsannavérunt me subsannatióne: * frenduérunt super me déntibus suis.
verses.eng: 34:16 They were separated, and repented not: they tempted me, they scoffed at me with scorn: * they gnashed upon me with their teeth.

verses.lat: 34:17 Dómine, quando respícies? * restítue ánimam meam a malignitáte eórum, a leónibus únicam meam.
verses.eng: 34:17 Lord, when wilt thou look upon me? * rescue thou my soul from their malice: my only one from the lions.

matutinum.psalm3.antiphonLat: Restítue ánimam meam * a malefáctis eórum, Dómine.
matutinum.psalm3.antiphonEng: Rescue, O Lord, * my soul from their malice.

matutinum.psalm4.label: Psalmus 34 (18-28)

verses.lat: 34:18 Confitébor tibi in ecclésia magna, * in pópulo gravi laudábo te.
verses.eng: 34:18 I will give thanks to thee in a great church; * I will praise thee in a strong people.

verses.lat: 34:19 Non supergáudeant mihi qui adversántur mihi iníque: * qui odérunt me gratis et ánnuunt óculis.
verses.eng: 34:19 Let not them that are my enemies wrongfully rejoice over me: * who have hated me without cause, and wink with the eyes.

verses.lat: 34:20 Quóniam mihi quidem pacífice loquebántur: * et in iracúndia terræ loquéntes, dolos cogitábant.
verses.eng: 34:20 For they spoke indeed peaceably to me; * and speaking in the anger of the earth they devised guile.

verses.lat: 34:21 Et dilatavérunt super me os suum: * dixérunt: Euge, euge, vidérunt óculi nostri.
verses.eng: 34:21 And they opened their mouth wide against me; * they said: Well done, well done, our eyes have seen it.

verses.lat: 34:22 Vidísti, Dómine, ne síleas: * Dómine, ne discédas a me.
verses.eng: 34:22 Thou hast seen, O Lord, be not thou silent: * O Lord, depart not from me.

verses.lat: 34:23 Exsúrge et inténde judício meo: * Deus meus, et Dóminus meus in causam meam.
verses.eng: 34:23 Arise, and be attentive to my judgment: * to my cause, my God, and my Lord.

verses.lat: 34:24 Júdica me secúndum justítiam tuam, Dómine, Deus meus, * et non supergáudeant mihi.
verses.eng: 34:24 Judge me, O Lord my God according to thy justice, * and let them not rejoice over me.

verses.lat: 34:25 Non dicant in córdibus suis: Euge, euge, ánimæ nostræ: * nec dicant: Devorávimus eum.
verses.eng: 34:25 Let them not say in their hearts: It is well, it is well, to our mind: * neither let them say: We have swallowed him up.

verses.lat: 34:26 Erubéscant et revereántur simul, * qui gratulántur malis meis.
verses.eng: 34:26 Let them blush: and be ashamed together, * who rejoice at my evils.

verses.lat: 34:26 Induántur confusióne et reveréntia * qui magna loquúntur super me.
verses.eng: 34:26 Let them be clothed with confusion and shame, * who speak great things against me.

verses.lat: 34:27 Exsúltent et læténtur qui volunt justítiam meam: * et dicant semper: Magnificétur Dóminus qui volunt pacem servi ejus.
verses.eng: 34:27 Let them rejoice and be glad, who are well pleased with my justice, * and let them say always: The Lord be magnified, who delights in the peace of his servant.

verses.lat: 34:28 Et lingua mea meditábitur justítiam tuam, * tota die laudem tuam.
verses.eng: 34:28 And my tongue shall meditate thy justice, * thy praise all the day long.

matutinum.psalm4.antiphonLat: Exsúrge, Dómine, * et inténde judício meo.
matutinum.psalm4.antiphonEng: Arise, O Lord, * and be attentive to my judgment.

matutinum.psalm5.label: Psalmus 36 (1-15)

verses.lat: 36:1 Noli æmulári in malignántibus: * neque zeláveris faciéntes iniquitátem.
verses.eng: 36:1 Be not emulous of evildoers; * nor envy them that work iniquity.

verses.lat: 36:2 Quóniam tamquam fænum velóciter aréscent: * et quemádmodum ólera herbárum cito décident.
verses.eng: 36:2 For they shall shortly wither away as grass, * and as the green herbs shall quickly fall.

verses.lat: 36:3 Spera in Dómino, et fac bonitátem: * et inhábita terram, et pascéris in divítiis ejus.
verses.eng: 36:3 Trust in the Lord, and do good, * and dwell in the land, and thou shalt be fed with its riches.

verses.lat: 36:4 Delectáre in Dómino: * et dabit tibi petitiónes cordis tui.
verses.eng: 36:4 Delight in the Lord, * and he will give thee the requests of thy heart.

verses.lat: 36:5 Revéla Dómino viam tuam, et spera in eo: * et ipse fáciet.
verses.eng: 36:5 Commit thy way to the Lord, and trust in him, * and he will do it.

verses.lat: 36:6 Et edúcet quasi lumen justítiam tuam: et judícium tuum tamquam merídiem: * súbditus esto Dómino, et ora eum.
verses.eng: 36:6 And he will bring forth thy justice as the light, and thy judgment as the noonday: * be subject to the Lord and pray to him.

verses.lat: 36:7 Noli æmulári in eo, qui prosperátur in via sua: * in hómine faciénte injustítias.
verses.eng: 36:7 Envy not the man who prospereth in his way; * the man who doth unjust things.

verses.lat: 36:8 Désine ab ira, et derelínque furórem: * noli æmulári ut malignéris.
verses.eng: 36:8 Cease from anger, and leave rage; * have no emulation to do evil.

verses.lat: 36:9 Quóniam qui malignántur, exterminabúntur: * sustinéntes autem Dóminum, ipsi hereditábunt terram.
verses.eng: 36:9 For the evildoers shall be cut off: * but they that wait upon the Lord shall inherit the land.

verses.lat: 36:10 Et adhuc pusíllum, et non erit peccátor: * et quæres locum ejus et non invénies.
verses.eng: 36:10 For yet a little while, and the wicked shall not be: * and thou shalt seek his place, and shalt not find it.

verses.lat: 36:11 Mansuéti autem hereditábunt terram: * et delectabúntur in multitúdine pacis.
verses.eng: 36:11 But the meek shall inherit the land, * and shall delight in abundance of peace.

verses.lat: 36:12 Observábit peccátor justum: * et stridébit super eum déntibus suis.
verses.eng: 36:12 The sinner shall watch the just man: * and shall gnash upon him with his teeth.

verses.lat: 36:13 Dóminus autem irridébit eum: * quóniam próspicit quod véniet dies ejus.
verses.eng: 36:13 But the Lord shall laugh at him: * for he foreseeth that his day shall come.

verses.lat: 36:14 Gládium evaginavérunt peccatóres: * intendérunt arcum suum,
verses.eng: 36:14 The wicked have drawn out the sword: * they have bent their bow.

verses.lat: 36:14 Ut deíciant páuperem et ínopem: * ut trucídent rectos corde.
verses.eng: 36:14 To cast down the poor and needy, * to kill the upright of heart.

verses.lat: 36:15 Gládius eórum intret in corda ipsórum: * et arcus eórum confringátur.
verses.eng: 36:15 Let their sword enter into their own hearts, * and let their bow be broken.

matutinum.psalm5.antiphonLat: Noli æmulári * in eo qui prosperátur et facit iniquitátem.
matutinum.psalm5.antiphonEng: Envy not * the man who prospereth in his way; the man who doth unjust things.

matutinum.psalm6.label: Psalmus 36 (16-29)

verses.lat: 36:16 Mélius est módicum justo, * super divítias peccatórum multas.
verses.eng: 36:16 Better is a little to the just, * than the great riches of the wicked.

verses.lat: 36:17 Quóniam brácchia peccatórum conteréntur: * confírmat autem justos Dóminus.
verses.eng: 36:17 For the arms of the wicked shall be broken in pieces; * but the Lord strengtheneth the just.

verses.lat: 36:18 Novit Dóminus dies immaculatórum: * et heréditas eórum in ætérnum erit.
verses.eng: 36:18 The Lord knoweth the days of the undefiled; * and their inheritance shall be for ever.

verses.lat: 36:19 Non confundéntur in témpore malo, et in diébus famis saturabúntur: * quia peccatóres períbunt.
verses.eng: 36:19 They shall not be confounded in the evil time; and in the days of famine they shall be filled, * because the wicked shall perish.

verses.lat: 36:20 Inimíci vero Dómini mox ut honorificáti fúerint et exaltáti: * deficiéntes, quemádmodum fumus defícient.
verses.eng: 36:20 And the enemies of the Lord, presently after they shall be honoured and exalted, * shall come to nothing and vanish like smoke.

verses.lat: 36:21 Mutuábitur peccátor, et non solvet: * justus autem miserétur et tríbuet.
verses.eng: 36:21 The sinner shall borrow, and not pay again; * but the just sheweth mercy and shall give.

verses.lat: 36:22 Quia benedicéntes ei hereditábunt terram: * maledicéntes autem ei disperíbunt.
verses.eng: 36:22 For such as bless him shall inherit the land: * but such as curse him shall perish.

verses.lat: 36:23 Apud Dóminum gressus hóminis dirigéntur: * et viam ejus volet.
verses.eng: 36:23 With the Lord shall the steps of a man be directed, * and he shall like well his way.

verses.lat: 36:24 Cum cecíderit non collidétur: * quia Dóminus suppónit manum suam.
verses.eng: 36:24 When he shall fall he shall not be bruised, * for the Lord putteth his hand under him.

verses.lat: 36:25 Júnior fui, étenim sénui: * et non vidi justum derelíctum, nec semen ejus quærens panem.
verses.eng: 36:25 I have been young, and now am old; * and I have not seen the just forsaken, nor his seed seeking bread.

verses.lat: 36:26 Tota die miserétur et cómmodat: * et semen illíus in benedictióne erit.
verses.eng: 36:26 He sheweth mercy, and lendeth all the day long; * and his seed shall be in blessing.

verses.lat: 36:27 Declína a malo, et fac bonum: * et inhábita in sǽculum sǽculi.
verses.eng: 36:27 Decline from evil and do good, * and dwell for ever and ever.

verses.lat: 36:28 Quia Dóminus amat judícium, et non derelínquet sanctos suos: * in ætérnum conservabúntur.
verses.eng: 36:28 For the Lord loveth judgment, and will not forsake his saints: * they shall be preserved for ever.

verses.lat: 36:28 Injústi puniéntur: * et semen impiórum períbit.
verses.eng: 36:28 The unjust shall be punished, * and the seed of the wicked shall perish.

verses.lat: 36:29 Justi autem hereditábunt terram: * et inhabitábunt in sǽculum sǽculi super eam.
verses.eng: 36:29 But the just shall inherit the land, * and shall dwell therein for evermore.

matutinum.psalm6.antiphonLat: Brácchia peccatórum * conteréntur, confírmat autem justos Dóminus.
matutinum.psalm6.antiphonEng: The arms of the wicked * shall be broken in pieces; but the Lord strengtheneth the just.

verses.lat: 36:30 Os justi meditábitur sapiéntiam, * et lingua ejus loquétur judícium.
verses.eng: 36:30 The mouth of the just shall meditate wisdom: * and his tongue shall speak judgment.

verses.lat: 36:31 Lex Dei ejus in corde ipsíus, * et non supplantabúntur gressus ejus.
verses.eng: 36:31 The law of his God is in his heart, * and his steps shall not be supplanted.

verses.lat: 36:32 Consíderat peccátor justum: * et quærit mortificáre eum.
verses.eng: 36:32 The wicked watcheth the just man, * and seeketh to put him to death.

verses.lat: 36:33 Dóminus autem non derelínquet eum in mánibus ejus: * nec damnábit eum, cum judicábitur illi.
verses.eng: 36:33 But the Lord will not leave him in his hands; * nor condemn him when he shall be judged.

verses.lat: 36:34 Exspécta Dóminum, et custódi viam ejus: et exaltábit te ut hereditáte cápias terram: * cum períerint peccatóres vidébis.
verses.eng: 36:34 Expect the Lord and keep his way: and he will exalt thee to inherit the land: * when the sinners shall perish thou shalt see.

verses.lat: 36:35 Vidi ímpium superexaltátum, * et elevátum sicut cedros Líbani.
verses.eng: 36:35 I have seen the wicked highly exalted, * and lifted up like the cedars of Libanus.

verses.lat: 36:36 Et transívi, et ecce non erat: * et quæsívi eum, et non est invéntus locus ejus.
verses.eng: 36:36 And I passed by, and lo, he was not: * and I sought him and his place was not found.

verses.lat: 36:37 Custódi innocéntiam, et vide æquitátem: * quóniam sunt relíquiæ hómini pacífico.
verses.eng: 36:37 Keep innocence, and behold justice: * for there are remnants for the peaceable man.

verses.lat: 36:38 Injústi autem disperíbunt simul: * relíquiæ impiórum interíbunt.
verses.eng: 36:38 But the unjust shall be destroyed together: * the remnants of the wicked shall perish.

verses.lat: 36:39 Salus autem justórum a Dómino: * et protéctor eórum in témpore tribulatiónis.
verses.eng: 36:39 But the salvation of the just is from the Lord, * and he is their protector in the time of trouble.

verses.lat: 36:40 Et adjuvábit eos Dóminus et liberábit eos: * et éruet eos a peccatóribus, et salvábit eos: quia speravérunt in eo.
verses.eng: 36:40 And the Lord will help them and deliver them: * and he will rescue them from the wicked, and save them, because they have hoped in him.

matutinum.psalm8.label: Psalmus 37 (2-11)

verses.lat: 37:2 Dómine, ne in furóre tuo árguas me, * neque in ira tua corrípias me.
verses.eng: 37:2 Rebuke me not, O Lord, in thy indignation; * nor chastise me in thy wrath.

verses.lat: 37:3 Quóniam sagíttæ tuæ infíxæ sunt mihi: * et confirmásti super me manum tuam.
verses.eng: 37:3 For thy arrows are fastened in me: * and thy hand hath been strong upon me.

verses.lat: 37:4 Non est sánitas in carne mea a fácie iræ tuæ: * non est pax óssibus meis a fácie peccatórum meórum.
verses.eng: 37:4 There is no health in my flesh, because of thy wrath: * there is no peace for my bones, because of my sins.

verses.lat: 37:5 Quóniam iniquitátes meæ supergréssæ sunt caput meum: * et sicut onus grave gravátæ sunt super me.
verses.eng: 37:5 For my iniquities are gone over my head: * and as a heavy burden are become heavy upon me.

verses.lat: 37:6 Putruérunt et corrúptæ sunt cicatríces meæ, * a fácie insipiéntiæ meæ.
verses.eng: 37:6 My sores are putrified and corrupted, * because of my foolishness.

verses.lat: 37:7 Miser factus sum, et curvátus sum usque in finem: * tota die contristátus ingrediébar.
verses.eng: 37:7 I am become miserable, and am bowed down even to the end: * I walked sorrowful all the day long.

verses.lat: 37:8 Quóniam lumbi mei impléti sunt illusiónibus: * et non est sánitas in carne mea.
verses.eng: 37:8 For my loins are filled with illusions; * and there is no health in my flesh.

verses.lat: 37:9 Afflíctus sum, et humiliátus sum nimis: * rugiébam a gémitu cordis mei.
verses.eng: 37:9 I am afflicted and humbled exceedingly: * I roared with the groaning of my heart.

verses.lat: 37:10 Dómine, ante te omne desidérium meum: * et gémitus meus a te non est abscónditus.
verses.eng: 37:10 Lord, all my desire is before thee, * and my groaning is not hidden from thee.

verses.lat: 37:11 Cor meum conturbátum est, derelíquit me virtus mea: * et lumen oculórum meórum, et ipsum non est mecum.
verses.eng: 37:11 My heart is troubled, my strength hath left me, * and the light of my eyes itself is not with me.

matutinum.psalm8.antiphonLat: Ne in ira tua * corrípias me, Dómine.
matutinum.psalm8.antiphonEng: O Lord, * do not chastise me in thy wrath.

matutinum.psalm9.label: Psalmus 37 (12-23)

verses.lat: 37:12 Amíci mei, et próximi mei * advérsum me appropinquavérunt, et stetérunt.
verses.eng: 37:12 My friends and my neighbours * have drawn near, and stood against me.

verses.lat: 37:12 Et qui juxta me erant, de longe stetérunt: * et vim faciébant qui quærébant ánimam meam.
verses.eng: 37:12 And they that were near me stood afar off: * and they that sought my soul used violence.

verses.lat: 37:13 Et qui inquirébant mala mihi, locúti sunt vanitátes: * et dolos tota die meditabántur.
verses.eng: 37:13 And they that sought evils to me spoke vain things, * and studied deceits all the day long.

verses.lat: 37:14 Ego autem tamquam surdus non audiébam: * et sicut mutus non apériens os suum.
verses.eng: 37:14 But I, as a deaf man, heard not: * and as a dumb man not opening his mouth.

verses.lat: 37:15 Et factus sum sicut homo non áudiens: * et non habens in ore suo redargutiónes.
verses.eng: 37:15 And I became as a man that heareth not: * and that hath no reproofs in his mouth.

verses.lat: 37:16 Quóniam in te, Dómine, sperávi: * tu exáudies me, Dómine, Deus meus.
verses.eng: 37:16 For in thee, O Lord, have I hoped: * thou wilt hear me, O Lord my God.

verses.lat: 37:17 Quia dixi: Nequándo supergáudeant mihi inimíci mei: * et dum commovéntur pedes mei, super me magna locúti sunt.
verses.eng: 37:17 For I said: Lest at any time my enemies rejoice over me: * and whilst my feet are moved, they speak great things against me.

verses.lat: 37:18 Quóniam ego in flagélla parátus sum: * et dolor meus in conspéctu meo semper.
verses.eng: 37:18 For I am ready for scourges: * and my sorrow is continually before me.

verses.lat: 37:19 Quóniam iniquitátem meam annuntiábo: * et cogitábo pro peccáto meo.
verses.eng: 37:19 For I will declare my iniquity: * and I will think for my sin.

verses.lat: 37:20 Inimíci autem mei vivunt, et confirmáti sunt super me: * et multiplicáti sunt qui odérunt me iníque.
verses.eng: 37:20 But my enemies live, and are stronger than I: * and they that hate me wrongfully are multiplied.

verses.lat: 37:21 Qui retríbuunt mala pro bonis, detrahébant mihi: * quóniam sequébar bonitátem.
verses.eng: 37:21 They that render evil for good, have detracted me, * because I followed goodness.

verses.lat: 37:22 Ne derelínquas me, Dómine, Deus meus: * ne discésseris a me.
verses.eng: 37:22 Forsake me not, O Lord my God: * do not thou depart from me.

verses.lat: 37:23 Inténde in adjutórium meum, * Dómine, Deus, salútis meæ.
verses.eng: 37:23 Attend unto my help, * O Lord, the God of my salvation.

matutinum.psalm9.antiphonLat: Inténde in adjutórium meum, * Dómine, virtus salútis meæ.
matutinum.psalm9.antiphonEng: Attend unto my help, * O Lord, the God of my salvation.

matutinum.psalm10.label: Psalmus 38

verses.lat: 38:2 Dixi: Custódiam vias meas: * ut non delínquam in lingua mea.
verses.eng: 38:2 I said: I will take heed to my ways: * that I sin not with my tongue.

verses.lat: 38:2 Pósui ori meo custódiam, * cum consísteret peccátor advérsum me.
verses.eng: 38:2 I have set guard to my mouth, * when the sinner stood against me.

verses.lat: 38:3 Obmútui, et humiliátus sum, et sílui a bonis: * et dolor meus renovátus est.
verses.eng: 38:3 I was dumb, and was humbled, and kept silence from good things: * and my sorrow was renewed.

verses.lat: 38:4 Concáluit cor meum intra me: * et in meditatióne mea exardéscet ignis.
verses.eng: 38:4 My heart grew hot within me: * and in my meditation a fire shall flame out.

verses.lat: 38:5 Locútus sum in lingua mea: * Notum fac mihi, Dómine, finem meum.
verses.eng: 38:5 I spoke with my tongue: * O Lord, make me know my end.

verses.lat: 38:5 Et númerum diérum meórum quis est: * ut sciam quid desit mihi.
verses.eng: 38:5 And what is the number of my days: * that I may know what is wanting to me.

verses.lat: 38:6 Ecce mensurábiles posuísti dies meos: * et substántia mea tamquam níhilum ante te.
verses.eng: 38:6 Behold thou hast made my days measurable: * and my substance is as nothing before thee.

verses.lat: 38:6 Verúmtamen univérsa vánitas, * omnis homo vivens.
verses.eng: 38:6 And indeed all things are vanity: * every man living.

verses.lat: 38:7 Verúmtamen in imágine pertránsit homo: * sed et frustra conturbátur.
verses.eng: 38:7 Surely man passeth as an image: * yea, and he is disquieted in vain.

verses.lat: 38:7 Thesaurízat: * et ignórat cui congregábit ea.
verses.eng: 38:7 He storeth up: * and he knoweth not for whom he shall gather these things.

verses.lat: 38:8 Et nunc quæ est exspectátio mea? Nonne Dóminus? * Et substántia mea apud te est.
verses.eng: 38:8 And now what is my hope? Is it not the Lord? * And my substance is with thee.

verses.lat: 38:9 Ab ómnibus iniquitátibus meis érue me: * oppróbrium insipiénti dedísti me.
verses.eng: 38:9 Deliver thou me from all my iniquities: * thou hast made me a reproach to the fool.

verses.lat: 38:10 Obmútui, et non apérui os meum, quóniam tu fecísti: * ámove a me plagas tuas.
verses.eng: 38:10 I was dumb, and I opened not my mouth, because thou hast done it: * remove thy scourges from me.

verses.lat: 38:12 A fortitúdine manus tuæ ego deféci in increpatiónibus: * propter iniquitátem corripuísti hóminem.
verses.eng: 38:12 The strength of thy hand hath made me faint in rebukes: * thou hast corrected man for iniquity.

verses.lat: 38:12 Et tabéscere fecísti sicut aráneam ánimam ejus: * verúmtamen vane conturbátur omnis homo.
verses.eng: 38:12 And thou hast made his soul to waste away like a spider: * surely in vain is any man disquieted.

verses.lat: 38:13 Exáudi oratiónem meam, Dómine, et deprecatiónem meam: * áuribus pércipe lácrimas meas.
verses.eng: 38:13 Hear my prayer, O Lord, and my supplication: * give ear to my tears.

verses.lat: 38:13 Ne síleas: quóniam ádvena ego sum apud te, et peregrínus, * sicut omnes patres mei.
verses.eng: 38:13 Be not silent: for I am a stranger with thee, * and a sojourner as all my fathers were.

verses.lat: 38:14 Remítte mihi, ut refrígerer priúsquam ábeam, * et ámplius non ero.
verses.eng: 38:14 O forgive me, that I may be refreshed, before I go hence, * and be no more.

matutinum.psalm10.antiphonLat: Ámove, Dómine, * a me plagas tuas.
matutinum.psalm10.antiphonEng: Remove, O Lord, * thy scourges from me.

vesperae.psalm1.label: Psalmus 122
vesperae.psalm1.antiphonLat: Qui hábitas in cælis, * miserére nobis.
vesperae.psalm1.antiphonEng: Thou who dwellest in heaven, * have mercy on us.

verses.lat: 122:1 Ad te levávi óculos meos, * qui hábitas in cælis.
verses.eng: 122:1 To thee have I lifted up my eyes, * who dwellest in heaven.

verses.lat: 122:2a Ecce, sicut óculi servórum * in mánibus dominórum suórum,
verses.eng: 122:2y Behold as the eyes of servants * are on the hands of their masters,

verses.lat: 122:2b Sicut óculi ancíllæ in mánibus dóminæ suæ: * ita óculi nostri ad Dóminum, Deum nostrum, donec misereátur nostri.
verses.eng: 122:2b As the eyes of the handmaid are on the hands of her mistress: * so are our eyes unto the Lord our God, until he have mercy on us.

verses.lat: 122:3 Miserére nostri, Dómine, miserére nostri: * quia multum repléti sumus despectióne:
verses.eng: 122:3 Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us: * for we are greatly filled with contempt.

verses.lat: 122:4 Quia multum repléta est ánima nostra: * oppróbrium abundántibus, et despéctio supérbis.
verses.eng: 122:4 For our soul is greatly filled: * we are a reproach to the rich, and contempt to the proud.

vesperae.psalm2.label: Psalmus 123
vesperae.psalm2.antiphonEng: Our help is * in the name of the Lord.

verses.lat: 123:1 Nisi quia Dóminus erat in nobis, dicat nunc Israël: * (2a) nisi quia Dóminus erat in nobis,
verses.eng: 123:1 If it had not been that the Lord was with us, let Israel now say: * (2a) If it had not been that the Lord was with us,

verses.lat: 123:2b Cum exsúrgerent hómines in nos, * (3a) forte vivos deglutíssent nos:
verses.eng: 123:2b When men rose up against us, * (3a) perhaps they had swallowed us up alive.

verses.lat: 123:3b Cum irascerétur furor eórum in nos, * (4) fórsitan aqua absorbuísset nos.
verses.eng: 123:3b When their fury was enkindled against us, * (4) perhaps the waters had swallowed us up.

verses.lat: 123:5 Torréntem pertransívit ánima nostra: * fórsitan pertransísset ánima nostra aquam intolerábilem.
verses.eng: 123:5 Our soul hath passed through a torrent: * perhaps our soul had passed through a water insupportable.

verses.lat: 123:6 Benedíctus Dóminus * qui non dedit nos in captiónem déntibus eórum.
verses.eng: 123:6 Blessed be the Lord, * who hath not given us to be a prey to their teeth.

verses.lat: 123:7a Ánima nostra sicut passer erépta est * de láqueo venántium:
verses.eng: 123:7a Our soul hath been delivered as a sparrow * out of the snare of the fowlers.

verses.lat: 123:7b Láqueus contrítus est, * et nos liberáti sumus.
verses.eng: 123:7b The snare is broken, * and we are delivered.

verses.lat: 123:8 Adjutórium nostrum in nómine Dómini, * qui fecit cælum et terram.
verses.eng: 123:8 Our help is in the name of the Lord, * who made heaven and earth.

vesperae.psalm3.label: Psalmus 124
vesperae.psalm3.antiphonLat: In circúitu pópuli sui * Dóminus, ex hoc nunc et usque in sǽculum.
vesperae.psalm3.antiphonEng: The Lord standeth round his people * from this time forth and for evermore.

verses.lat: 124:1 Qui confídunt in Dómino, sicut mons Sion: * non commovébitur in ætérnum, qui hábitat (2a) in Jerúsalem.
verses.eng: 124:1 They that trust in the Lord shall be as mount Sion: * he shall not be moved for ever that dwelleth (2a) in Jerusalem.

verses.lat: 124:2b Montes in circúitu ejus: ‡ et Dóminus in circúitu pópuli sui, * ex hoc nunc et usque in sǽculum.
verses.eng: 124:2b Mountains are round about it: ‡ so the Lord is round about his people * from henceforth now and for ever.

verses.lat: 124:3 Quia non relínquet Dóminus virgam peccatórum super sortem justórum: * ut non exténdant justi ad iniquitátem manus suas.
verses.eng: 124:3 For the Lord will not leave the rod of sinners upon the lot of the just: * that the just may not stretch forth their hands to iniquity.

verses.lat: 124:4 Bénefac, Dómine, bonis, * et rectis corde.
verses.eng: 124:4 Do good, O Lord, to those that are good, * and to the upright of heart.

verses.lat: 124:5 Declinántes autem in obligatiónes addúcet Dóminus cum operántibus iniquitátem: * pax super Israël.
verses.eng: 124:5 But such as turn aside into bonds, the Lord shall lead out with the workers of iniquity: * peace upon Israel.

vesperae.psalm4.label: Psalmus 125
vesperae.psalm4.antiphonLat: Magnificávit Dóminus * fácere nobíscum: facti sumus lætántes.
vesperae.psalm4.antiphonEng: The Lord hath * done great things for us, whereof we rejoice.

verses.lat: 125:1 In converténdo Dóminus captivitátem Sion: * facti sumus sicut consoláti:
verses.eng: 125:1 When the Lord brought back the captivity of Sion, * we became like men comforted.

verses.lat: 125:2a Tunc replétum est gáudio os nostrum: * et lingua nostra exsultatióne.
verses.eng: 125:2a Then was our mouth filled with gladness; * and our tongue with joy.

verses.lat: 125:2b Tunc dicent inter gentes: * Magnificávit Dóminus fácere cum eis.
verses.eng: 125:2b Then shall they say among the Gentiles: * The Lord hath done great things for them.

verses.lat: 125:3 Magnificávit Dóminus fácere nobíscum: * facti sumus lætántes.
verses.eng: 125:3 The Lord hath done great things for us: * we are become joyful.

verses.lat: 125:4 Convérte, Dómine, captivitátem nostram, * sicut torrens in Austro.
verses.eng: 125:4 Turn again our captivity, O Lord, * as a stream in the south.

verses.lat: 125:5 Qui séminant in lácrimis, * in exsultatióne metent.
verses.eng: 125:5 They that sow in tears * shall reap in joy.

verses.lat: 125:6a Eúntes ibant et flebant, * mitténtes sémina sua.
verses.eng: 125:6a Going they went and wept, * casting their seeds.

verses.lat: 125:6b Veniéntes autem vénient cum exsultatióne, * portántes manípulos suos.
verses.eng: 125:6b But coming they shall come with joyfulness, * carrying their sheaves.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Qui hábitas in cælis, * miserére nobis.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Thou who dwellest in heaven, * have mercy on us.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Our help is * in the name of the Lord.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.lat: In circúitu pópuli sui * Dóminus, ex hoc nunc et usque in sǽculum.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.eng: The Lord standeth round his people * from this time forth and for evermore.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Magnificávit Dóminus * fácere nobíscum: facti sumus lætántes.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.eng: The Lord hath * done great things for us, whereof we rejoice.

vesperae.psalm5.label: Psalmus 126
vesperae.psalm5.antiphonLat: Dóminus ædíficet * nobis domum, et custódiat civitátem.
vesperae.psalm5.antiphonEng: The Lord builds * the house and keeps the city.

verses.lat: 126:1a Nisi Dóminus ædificáverit domum, * in vanum laboravérunt qui ædíficant eam.
verses.eng: 126:1a Unless the Lord build the house, * they labour in vain that build it.

verses.lat: 126:1b Nisi Dóminus custodíerit civitátem, * frustra vígilat qui custódit eam.
verses.eng: 126:1b Unless the Lord keep the city, * he watcheth in vain that keepeth it.

verses.lat: 126:2a Vanum est vobis ante lucem súrgere: * súrgite postquam sedéritis, qui manducátis panem dolóris.
verses.eng: 126:2a It is vain for you to rise before light, * rise ye after you have sitten, you that eat the bread of sorrow.

verses.lat: 126:2b Cum déderit diléctis suis somnum: * (3) ecce heréditas Dómini fílii: merces, fructus ventris.
verses.eng: 126:2b When he shall give sleep to his beloved, * (3) behold the inheritance of the Lord are children: the reward, the fruit of the womb.

verses.lat: 126:4 Sicut sagíttæ in manu poténtis: * ita fílii excussórum.
verses.eng: 126:4 As arrows in the hand of the mighty, * so the children of them that have been shaken.

verses.lat: 126:5 Beátus vir, qui implévit desidérium suum ex ipsis: * non confundétur cum loquétur inimícis suis in porta.
verses.eng: 126:5 Blessed is the man that hath filled the desire with them; * he shall not be confounded when he shall speak to his enemies in the gate.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Dóminus ædíficet * nobis domum, et custódiat civitátem.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.eng: The Lord builds * the house and keeps the city.

ant_prima.label: Antíphona
ant_prima.lat: Deus meus * in te confído non erubéscam.
ant_prima.eng: In thee, O my God, * I put my trust; let me not be ashamed.

verses.lat: 24:1 Ad te, Dómine, levávi ánimam meam: * Deus meus, in te confído, non erubéscam.
verses.eng: 24:1 To thee, O Lord, have I lifted up my soul: * In thee, O my God, I put my trust; let me not be ashamed.

verses.lat: 24:3 Neque irrídeant me inimíci mei: * étenim univérsi, qui sústinent te, non confundéntur.
verses.eng: 24:3 Neither let my enemies laugh at me: * for none of them that wait on thee shall be confounded.

verses.lat: 24:4 Confundántur omnes iníqua agéntes * supervácue.
verses.eng: 24:4 Let all them be confounded that act unjust things * without cause.

verses.lat: 24:4 Vias tuas, Dómine, demónstra mihi: * et sémitas tuas édoce me.
verses.eng: 24:4 Shew, O Lord, thy ways to me, * and teach me thy paths.

verses.lat: 24:5 Dírige me in veritáte tua, et doce me: * quia tu es, Deus, salvátor meus, et te sustínui tota die.
verses.eng: 24:5 Direct me in thy truth, and teach me; * for thou art God my Saviour; and on thee have I waited all the day long.

verses.lat: 24:6 Reminíscere miseratiónum tuárum, Dómine, * et misericordiárum tuárum, quæ a sǽculo sunt.
verses.eng: 24:6 Remember, O Lord, thy bowels of compassion; * and thy mercies that are from the beginning of the world.

verses.lat: 24:7 Delícta juventútis meæ, * et ignorántias meas ne memíneris.
verses.eng: 24:7 The sins of my youth * and my ignorances do not remember.

verses.lat: 24:7 Secúndum misericórdiam tuam meménto mei tu: * propter bonitátem tuam, Dómine.
verses.eng: 24:7 According to thy mercy remember thou me: * for thy goodness’ sake, O Lord.

verses.lat: 24:8 Dulcis et rectus Dóminus: * propter hoc legem dabit delinquéntibus in via.
verses.eng: 24:8 The Lord is sweet and righteous: * therefore he will give a law to sinners in the way.

verses.lat: 24:9 Díriget mansuétos in judício: * docébit mites vias suas.
verses.eng: 24:9 He will guide the mild in judgment: * he will teach the meek his ways.

verses.lat: 24:10 Univérsæ viæ Dómini, misericórdia et véritas, * requiréntibus testaméntum ejus et testimónia ejus.
verses.eng: 24:10 All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth, * to them that seek after his covenant and his testimonies.

verses.lat: 24:11 Propter nomen tuum, Dómine, propitiáberis peccáto meo: * multum est enim.
verses.eng: 24:11 For thy name’s sake, O Lord, thou wilt pardon my sin: * for it is great.

verses.lat: 24:12 Quis est homo qui timet Dóminum? * legem státuit ei in via, quam elégit.
verses.eng: 24:12 Who is the man that feareth the Lord? * He hath appointed him a law in the way he hath chosen.

verses.lat: 24:13 Ánima ejus in bonis demorábitur: * et semen ejus hereditábit terram.
verses.eng: 24:13 His soul shall dwell in good things: * and his seed shall inherit the land.

verses.lat: 24:14 Firmaméntum est Dóminus timéntibus eum: * et testaméntum ipsíus ut manifestétur illis.
verses.eng: 24:14 The Lord is a firmament to them that fear him: * and his covenant shall be made manifest to them.

verses.lat: 24:15 Óculi mei semper ad Dóminum: * quóniam ipse evéllet de láqueo pedes meos.
verses.eng: 24:15 My eyes are ever towards the Lord: * for he shall pluck my feet out of the snare.

verses.lat: 24:16 Réspice in me, et miserére mei: * quia únicus et pauper sum ego.
verses.eng: 24:16 Look thou upon me, and have mercy on me; * for I am alone and poor.

verses.lat: 24:17 Tribulatiónes cordis mei multiplicátæ sunt: * de necessitátibus meis érue me.
verses.eng: 24:17 The troubles of my heart are multiplied: * deliver me from my necessities.

verses.lat: 24:18 Vide humilitátem meam, et labórem meum: * et dimítte univérsa delícta mea.
verses.eng: 24:18 See my abjection and my labour; * and forgive me all my sins.

verses.lat: 24:19 Réspice inimícos meos quóniam multiplicáti sunt, * et ódio iníquo odérunt me.
verses.eng: 24:19 Consider my enemies for they are multiplied, * and have hated me with an unjust hatred.

verses.lat: 24:20 Custódi ánimam meam, et érue me: * non erubéscam quóniam sperávi in te.
verses.eng: 24:20 Keep thou my soul, and deliver me: * I shall not be ashamed, for I have hoped in thee.

verses.lat: 24:21 Innocéntes et recti adhæsérunt mihi: * quia sustínui te.
verses.eng: 24:21 The innocent and the upright have adhered to me: * because I have waited on thee.

verses.lat: 24:22 Líbera, Deus, Israël, * ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus suis.
verses.eng: 24:22 Deliver Israel, O God, * from all his tribulations.

ant_tertia.label: Antíphona
ant_tertia.lat: Respéxit me * et exaudívit deprecatiónem meam Dóminus.
ant_tertia.eng: The Lord hath heard * my supplication: the Lord hath received my prayer.

verses.lat: 39:2 Exspéctans exspectávi Dóminum, * et inténdit mihi.
verses.eng: 39:2 With expectation I have waited for the Lord, * and he was attentive to me.

verses.lat: 39:3 Et exaudívit preces meas: * et edúxit me de lacu misériæ, et de luto fæcis.
verses.eng: 39:3 And he heard my prayers, * and brought me out of the pit of misery and the mire of dregs.

verses.lat: 39:3 Et státuit super petram pedes meos: * et diréxit gressus meos.
verses.eng: 39:3 And he set my feet upon a rock, * and directed my steps.

verses.lat: 39:4 Et immísit in os meum cánticum novum, * carmen Deo nostro.
verses.eng: 39:4 And he put a new canticle into my mouth, * a song to our God.

verses.lat: 39:4 Vidébunt multi, et timébunt: * et sperábunt in Dómino.
verses.eng: 39:4 Many shall see, and shall fear: * and they shall hope in the Lord.

verses.lat: 39:5 Beátus vir, cujus est nomen Dómini spes ejus: * et non respéxit in vanitátes et insánias falsas.
verses.eng: 39:5 Blessed is the man whose trust is in the name of the Lord; * and who hath not had regard to vanities, and lying follies.

verses.lat: 39:6 Multa fecísti tu, Dómine, Deus meus, mirabília tua: * et cogitatiónibus tuis non est qui símilis sit tibi.
verses.eng: 39:6 Thou hast multiplied thy wonderful works, O Lord my God: * and in thy thoughts there is no one like to thee.

verses.lat: 39:6 Annuntiávi et locútus sum: * multiplicáti sunt super númerum.
verses.eng: 39:6 I have declared and I have spoken * they are multiplied above number.

verses.lat: 39:7 Sacrifícium et oblatiónem noluísti: * aures autem perfecísti mihi.
verses.eng: 39:7 Sacrifice and oblation thou didst not desire; * but thou hast pierced ears for me.

verses.lat: 39:7 Holocáustum et pro peccáto non postulásti: * tunc dixi: Ecce, vénio.
verses.eng: 39:7 Burnt offering and sin offering thou didst not require: * then said I, Behold I come.

verses.lat: 39:8 In cápite libri scriptum est de me ut fácerem voluntátem tuam: * Deus meus, vólui, et legem tuam in médio cordis mei.
verses.eng: 39:8 In the head of the book it is written of me that I should do thy will: * O my God, I have desired it, and thy law in the midst of my heart.

verses.lat: 39:10 Annuntiávi justítiam tuam in ecclésia magna, * ecce, lábia mea non prohibébo: Dómine, tu scisti.
verses.eng: 39:10 I have declared thy justice in a great church, * lo, I will not restrain my lips: O Lord, thou knowest it.

verses.lat: 39:11 Justítiam tuam non abscóndi in corde meo: * veritátem tuam et salutáre tuum dixi.
verses.eng: 39:11 I have not hid thy justice within my heart: * I have declared thy truth and thy salvation.

verses.lat: 39:11 Non abscóndi misericórdiam tuam et veritátem tuam * a concílio multo.
verses.eng: 39:11 I have not concealed thy mercy and thy truth * from a great council.

verses.lat: 39:12 Tu autem, Dómine, ne longe fácias miseratiónes tuas a me: * misericórdia tua et véritas tua semper suscepérunt me.
verses.eng: 39:12 Withhold not thou, O Lord, thy tender mercies from me: * thy mercy and thy truth have always upheld me.

verses.lat: 39:13 Quóniam circumdedérunt me mala, quorum non est númerus: * comprehendérunt me iniquitátes meæ, et non pótui ut vidérem.
verses.eng: 39:13 For evils without number have surrounded me; * my iniquities have overtaken me, and I was not able to see.

verses.lat: 39:13 Multiplicátæ sunt super capíllos cápitis mei: * et cor meum derelíquit me.
verses.eng: 39:13 They are multiplied above the hairs of my head: * and my heart hath forsaken me.

verses.lat: 39:14 Compláceat tibi, Dómine, ut éruas me: * Dómine, ad adjuvándum me réspice.
verses.eng: 39:14 Be pleased, O Lord to deliver me: * look down, O Lord, to help me.

verses.lat: 39:15 Confundántur et revereántur simul, qui quærunt ánimam meam, * ut áuferant eam.
verses.eng: 39:15 Let them be confounded and ashamed together, that seek after my soul * to take it away.

verses.lat: 39:15 Convertántur retrórsum, et revereántur, * qui volunt mihi mala.
verses.eng: 39:15 Let them be turned backward and be ashamed * that desire evils to me.

verses.lat: 39:16 Ferant conféstim confusiónem suam, * qui dicunt mihi: Euge, euge.
verses.eng: 39:16 Let them immediately bear their confusion, * that say to me: ’T is well, ’t is well.

verses.lat: 39:17 Exsúltent et læténtur super te omnes quæréntes te: * et dicant semper: Magnificétur Dóminus: qui díligunt salutáre tuum.
verses.eng: 39:17 Let all that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee: * and let such as love thy salvation say always: The Lord be magnified.

verses.lat: 39:18 Ego autem mendícus sum, et pauper: * Dóminus sollícitus est mei.
verses.eng: 39:18 But I am a beggar and poor: * the Lord is careful for me.

verses.lat: 39:18 Adjútor meus, et protéctor meus tu es: * Deus meus, ne tardáveris.
verses.eng: 39:18 Thou art my helper and my protector: * O my God, be not slack.

ant_sexta.label: Antíphona
ant_sexta.lat: Suscepísti me, Dómine: * et confirmásti me in conspéctu tuo.
ant_sexta.eng: But thou hast upheld me, O Lord, * and hast established me in thy sight for ever.

verses.lat: 40:2 Beátus qui intéllegit super egénum, et páuperem: * in die mala liberábit eum Dóminus.
verses.eng: 40:2 Blessed is he that understandeth concerning the needy and the poor: * the Lord will deliver him in the evil day.

verses.lat: 40:3 Dóminus consérvet eum, et vivíficet eum, et beátum fáciat eum in terra: * et non tradat eum in ánimam inimicórum ejus.
verses.eng: 40:3 The Lord preserve him and give him life, and make him blessed upon the earth: * and deliver him not up to the will of his enemies.

verses.lat: 40:4 Dóminus opem ferat illi super lectum dolóris ejus: * univérsum stratum ejus versásti in infirmitáte ejus.
verses.eng: 40:4 The Lord help him on his bed of sorrow: * thou hast turned all his couch in his sickness.

verses.lat: 40:5 Ego dixi: Dómine, miserére mei: * sana ánimam meam, quia peccávi tibi.
verses.eng: 40:5 I said: O Lord, be thou merciful to me: * heal my soul, for I have sinned against thee.

verses.lat: 40:6 Inimíci mei dixérunt mala mihi: * Quando moriétur, et períbit nomen ejus?
verses.eng: 40:6 My enemies have spoken evils against me: * when shall he die and his name perish?

verses.lat: 40:7 Et si ingrediebátur ut vidéret, vana loquebátur: * cor ejus congregávit iniquitátem sibi.
verses.eng: 40:7 And if he came in to see me, he spoke vain things: * his heart gathered together iniquity to itself.

verses.lat: 40:7 Egrediebátur foras, * et loquebátur in idípsum.
verses.eng: 40:7 He went out * and spoke to the same purpose.

verses.lat: 40:8 Advérsum me susurrábant omnes inimíci mei: * advérsum me cogitábant mala mihi.
verses.eng: 40:8 All my enemies whispered together against me: * they devised evils to me.

verses.lat: 40:9 Verbum iníquum constituérunt advérsum me: * Numquid qui dormit non adíciet ut resúrgat?
verses.eng: 40:9 They determined against me an unjust word: * shall he that sleepeth rise again no more?

verses.lat: 40:10 Étenim homo pacis meæ, in quo sperávi: * qui edébat panes meos, magnificávit super me supplantatiónem.
verses.eng: 40:10 For even the man of my peace, in whom I trusted, * who ate my bread, hath greatly supplanted me.

verses.lat: 40:11 Tu autem, Dómine, miserére mei, et resúscita me: * et retríbuam eis.
verses.eng: 40:11 But thou, O Lord, have mercy on me, and raise me up again: * and I will requite them.

verses.lat: 40:12 In hoc cognóvi quóniam voluísti me: * quóniam non gaudébit inimícus meus super me.
verses.eng: 40:12 By this I know, that thou hast had a good will for me: * because my enemy shall not rejoice over me.

verses.lat: 40:13 Me autem propter innocéntiam suscepísti: * et confirmásti me in conspéctu tuo in ætérnum.
verses.eng: 40:13 But thou hast upheld me by reason of my innocence: * and hast established me in thy sight for ever.

verses.lat: 40:14 Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël, a sǽculo et usque in sǽculum: * fiat, fiat.
verses.eng: 40:14 Blessed be the Lord the God of Israel from eternity to eternity. * So be it. So be it.

verses.lat: 41:2 Quemádmodum desíderat cervus ad fontes aquárum: * ita desíderat ánima mea ad te, Deus.
verses.eng: 41:2 As the hart panteth after the fountains of water; * so my soul panteth after thee, O God.

verses.lat: 41:3 Sitívit ánima mea ad Deum fortem vivum: * quando véniam, et apparébo ante fáciem Dei?
verses.eng: 41:3 My soul hath thirsted after the strong living God; * when shall I come and appear before the face of God?

verses.lat: 41:4 Fuérunt mihi lácrimæ meæ panes die ac nocte: * dum dícitur mihi cotídie: Ubi est Deus tuus?
verses.eng: 41:4 My tears have been my bread day and night, * whilst it is said to me daily: Where is thy God?

verses.lat: 41:5 Hæc recordátus sum, et effúdi in me ánimam meam: * quóniam transíbo in locum tabernáculi admirábilis, usque ad domum Dei.
verses.eng: 41:5 These things I remembered, and poured out my soul in me: * for I shall go over into the place of the wonderful tabernacle, even to the house of God:

verses.lat: 41:5 In voce exsultatiónis, et confessiónis: * sonus epulántis.
verses.eng: 41:5 With the voice of joy and praise; * the noise of one feasting.

verses.lat: 41:6 Quare tristis es, ánima mea? * et quare contúrbas me?
verses.eng: 41:6 Why art thou sad, O my soul? * and why dost thou trouble me?

verses.lat: 41:6 Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
verses.eng: 41:6 Hope in God, for I will still give praise to him: * the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

verses.lat: 41:7 Ad meípsum ánima mea conturbáta est: * proptérea memor ero tui de terra Jordánis, et Hermóniim a monte módico.
verses.eng: 41:7 My soul is troubled within myself: * therefore will I remember thee from the land of Jordan and Hermoniim, from the little hill.

verses.lat: 41:8 Abýssus abýssum ínvocat, * in voce cataractárum tuárum.
verses.eng: 41:8 Deep calleth on deep, * at the noise of thy flood-gates.

verses.lat: 41:8 Ómnia excélsa tua, et fluctus tui * super me transiérunt.
verses.eng: 41:8 All thy heights and thy billows * have passed over me.

verses.lat: 41:9 In die mandávit Dóminus misericórdiam suam: * et nocte cánticum ejus.
verses.eng: 41:9 In the daytime the Lord hath commanded his mercy; * and a canticle to him in the night.

verses.lat: 41:9 Apud me orátio Deo vitæ meæ, * dicam Deo: Suscéptor meus es.
verses.eng: 41:9 With me is prayer to the God of my life. * I will say to God: Thou art my support.

verses.lat: 41:10 Quare oblítus es mei? * et quare contristátus incédo, dum afflígit me inimícus?
verses.eng: 41:10 Why hast thou forgotten me? * and why go I mourning, whilst my enemy afflicteth me?

verses.lat: 41:11 Dum confringúntur ossa mea, * exprobravérunt mihi qui tríbulant me inimíci mei.
verses.eng: 41:11 Whilst my bones are broken, * my enemies who trouble me have reproached me;

verses.lat: 41:11 Dum dicunt mihi per síngulos dies: Ubi est Deus tuus? * quare tristis es, ánima mea? et quare contúrbas me?
verses.eng: 41:11 Whilst they say to me day by day: Where is thy God? * Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why dost thou disquiet me?

verses.lat: 41:12 Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
verses.eng: 41:12 Hope thou in God, for I will still give praise to him: * the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

ant_nona.label: Antíphona
ant_nona.lat: Salvásti nos, * Dómine, et in nómine tuo confitébimur in sǽcula.
ant_nona.eng: Thou hast saved us, O Lord, * and in thy name we will give praise for ever.

verses.lat: 43:2 Deus áuribus nostris audívimus: * patres nostri annuntiavérunt nobis.
verses.eng: 43:2 We have heard, O God, with our ears: * our fathers have declared to us,

verses.lat: 43:2 Opus, quod operátus es in diébus eórum, * et in diébus antíquis.
verses.eng: 43:2 The work thou hast wrought in their days, * and in the days of old.

verses.lat: 43:3 Manus tua gentes dispérdidit, et plantásti eos: * afflixísti pópulos, et expulísti eos.
verses.eng: 43:3 Thy hand destroyed the Gentiles, and thou plantedst them: * thou didst afflict the people and cast them out.

verses.lat: 43:4 Nec enim in gládio suo possedérunt terram, * et brácchium eórum non salvávit eos:
verses.eng: 43:4 For they got not the possession of the land by their own sword: * neither did their own arm save them.

verses.lat: 43:4 Sed déxtera tua, et brácchium tuum, et illuminátio vultus tui: * quóniam complacuísti in eis.
verses.eng: 43:4 But thy right hand and thy arm, and the light of thy countenance: * because thou wast pleased with them.

verses.lat: 43:5 Tu es ipse Rex meus et Deus meus: * qui mandas salútes Jacob.
verses.eng: 43:5 Thou art thyself my king and my God, * who commandest the saving of Jacob.

verses.lat: 43:6 In te inimícos nostros ventilábimus cornu: * et in nómine tuo spernémus insurgéntes in nobis.
verses.eng: 43:6 Through thee we will push down our enemies with the horn: * and through thy name we will despise them that rise up against us.

verses.lat: 43:7 Non enim in arcu meo sperábo: * et gládius meus non salvábit me.
verses.eng: 43:7 For I will not trust in my bow: * neither shall my sword save me.

verses.lat: 43:8 Salvásti enim nos de affligéntibus nos: * et odiéntes nos confudísti.
verses.eng: 43:8 But thou hast saved us from them that afflict us: * and hast put them to shame that hate us.

verses.lat: 43:9 In Deo laudábimur tota die: * et in nómine tuo confitébimur in sǽculum.
verses.eng: 43:9 In God shall we glory all the day long: * and in thy name we will give praise for ever.

verses.lat: 43:10 Nunc autem repulísti et confudísti nos: * et non egrediéris, Deus, in virtútibus nostris.
verses.eng: 43:10 But now thou hast cast us off, and put us to shame: * and thou, O God, wilt not go out with our armies.

verses.lat: 43:11 Avertísti nos retrórsum post inimícos nostros: * et qui odérunt nos, diripiébant sibi.
verses.eng: 43:11 Thou hast made us turn our back to our enemies: * and they that hated us plundered for themselves.

verses.lat: 43:12 Dedísti nos tamquam oves escárum: * et in géntibus dispersísti nos.
verses.eng: 43:12 Thou hast given us up like sheep to be eaten: * thou hast scattered us among the nations.

verses.lat: 43:13 Vendidísti pópulum tuum sine prétio: * et non fuit multitúdo in commutatiónibus eórum.
verses.eng: 43:13 Thou hast sold thy people for no price: * and there was no reckoning in the exchange of them.

verses.lat: 43:14 Posuísti nos oppróbrium vicínis nostris, * subsannatiónem et derísum his, qui sunt in circúitu nostro.
verses.eng: 43:14 Thou hast made us a reproach to our neighbours, * a scoff and derision to them that are round about us.

verses.lat: 43:15 Posuísti nos in similitúdinem géntibus: * commotiónem cápitis in pópulis.
verses.eng: 43:15 Thou hast made us a byword among the Gentiles: * a shaking of the head among the people.

verses.lat: 43:16 Tota die verecúndia mea contra me est, * et confúsio faciéi meæ coopéruit me.
verses.eng: 43:16 All the day long my shame is before me: * and the confusion of my face hath covered me.

verses.lat: 43:17 A voce exprobrántis, et obloquéntis: * a fácie inimíci, et persequéntis.
verses.eng: 43:17 At the voice of him that reproacheth and detracteth me: * at the face of the enemy and persecutor.

verses.lat: 43:18 Hæc ómnia venérunt super nos, nec oblíti sumus te: * et iníque non égimus in testaménto tuo.
verses.eng: 43:18 All these things have come upon us, yet we have not forgotten thee: * and we have not done wickedly in thy covenant.

verses.lat: 43:19 Et non recéssit retro cor nostrum: * et declinásti sémitas nostras a via tua:
verses.eng: 43:19 And our heart hath not turned back: * neither hast thou turned aside our steps from thy way.

verses.lat: 43:20 Quóniam humiliásti nos in loco afflictiónis, * et coopéruit nos umbra mortis.
verses.eng: 43:20 For thou hast humbled us in the place of affliction: * and the shadow of death hath covered us.

verses.lat: 43:21 Si oblíti sumus nomen Dei nostri, * et si expándimus manus nostras ad deum aliénum:
verses.eng: 43:21 If we have forgotten the name of our God, * and if we have spread forth our hands to a strange god:

verses.lat: 43:22 Nonne Deus requíret ista? * ipse enim novit abscóndita cordis.
verses.eng: 43:22 Shall not God search out these things: * for he knoweth the secrets of the heart.

verses.lat: 43:22 Quóniam propter te mortificámur tota die: * æstimáti sumus sicut oves occisiónis.
verses.eng: 43:22 Because for thy sake we are killed all the day long: * we are counted as sheep for the slaughter.

verses.lat: 43:23 Exsúrge, quare obdórmis, Dómine? * exsúrge, et ne repéllas in finem.
verses.eng: 43:23 Arise, why sleepest thou, O Lord? * arise, and cast us not off to the end.

verses.lat: 43:24 Quare fáciem tuam avértis, * oblivísceris inópiæ nostræ, et tribulatiónis nostræ?
verses.eng: 43:24 Why turnest thou thy face away? * and forgettest our want and our trouble?

verses.lat: 43:25 Quóniam humiliáta est in púlvere ánima nostra: * conglutinátus est in terra venter noster.
verses.eng: 43:25 For our soul is humbled down to the dust: * our belly cleaveth to the earth.

verses.lat: 43:26 Exsúrge, Dómine, ádjuva nos: * et rédime nos propter nomen tuum.
verses.eng: 43:26 Arise, O Lord, help us * and redeem us for thy name’s sake.

completorium.antiphon.label: Antíphona
completorium.antiphon.lat: Tu, Dómine, * servábis nos: et custódies nos in ætérnum.
completorium.antiphon.eng: Thou, O Lord, * wilt preserve us: and keep us for ever.

verses.lat: 11:2 Salvum me fac, Dómine, quóniam defécit sanctus: * quóniam diminútæ sunt veritátes a fíliis hóminum.
verses.eng: 11:2 Save me, O Lord, for there is now no saint: * truths are decayed from among the children of men.

verses.lat: 11:3 Vana locúti sunt unusquísque ad próximum suum: * lábia dolósa, in corde et corde locúti sunt.
verses.eng: 11:3 They have spoken vain things every one to his neighbour: * with deceitful lips, and with a double heart have they spoken.

verses.lat: 11:4 Dispérdat Dóminus univérsa lábia dolósa, * et linguam magníloquam.
verses.eng: 11:4 May the Lord destroy all deceitful lips, * and the tongue that speaketh proud things.

verses.lat: 11:5 Qui dixérunt: Linguam nostram magnificábimus, † lábia nostra a nobis sunt, * quis noster Dóminus est?
verses.eng: 11:5 Who have said: We will magnify our tongue; † our lips are our own; * who is Lord over us?

verses.lat: 11:6a Propter misériam ínopum, et gémitum páuperum, * nunc exsúrgam, dicit Dóminus.
verses.eng: 11:6a By reason of the misery of the needy, and the groans of the poor, * now will I arise, saith the Lord.

verses.lat: 11:6b Ponam in salutári: * fiduciáliter agam in eo.
verses.eng: 11:6b I will set him in safety; * I will deal confidently in his regard.

verses.lat: 11:7 Elóquia Dómini, elóquia casta: * argéntum igne examinátum, probátum terræ purgátum séptuplum.
verses.eng: 11:7 The words of the Lord are pure words: * as silver tried by the fire, purged from the earth, refined seven times.

verses.lat: 11:8 Tu, Dómine, servábis nos: et custódies nos * a generatióne hac in ætérnum.
verses.eng: 11:8 Thou, O Lord, wilt preserve us: and keep us * from this generation for ever.

verses.lat: 11:9 In circúitu ímpii ámbulant: * secúndum altitúdinem tuam multiplicásti fílios hóminum.
verses.eng: 11:9 The wicked walk round about: * according to thy highness, thou hast multiplied the children of men.

verses.lat: 12:1 Úsquequo, Dómine, obliviscéris me in finem? * Úsquequo avértis fáciem tuam a me?
verses.eng: 12:1 How long, O Lord, wilt thou forget me unto the end? * how long dost thou turn away thy face from me?

verses.lat: 12:2 Quámdiu ponam consília in ánima mea, * dolórem in corde meo per diem?
verses.eng: 12:2 How long shall I take counsels in my soul, * sorrow in my heart all the day?

verses.lat: 12:3 Úsquequo exaltábitur inimícus meus super me? * (4a) réspice, et exáudi me, Dómine, Deus meus.
verses.eng: 12:3 How long shall my enemy be exalted over me? * (4a) Consider, and hear me, O Lord my God.

verses.lat: 12:4b Illúmina óculos meos ne umquam obdórmiam in morte: * (5a) nequándo dicat inimícus meus: Præválui advérsus eum.
verses.eng: 12:4b Enlighten my eyes that I never sleep in death: * (5a) lest at any time my enemy say: I have prevailed against him.

verses.lat: 12:5b Qui tríbulant me, exsultábunt si motus fúero: * (6a) ego autem in misericórdia tua sperávi.
verses.eng: 12:5b They that trouble me will rejoice when I am moved: * (6a) but I have trusted in thy mercy.

verses.lat: 12:6b Exsultábit cor meum in salutári tuo: † cantábo Dómino qui bona tríbuit mihi: * et psallam nómini Dómini altíssimi.
verses.eng: 12:6b My heart shall rejoice in thy salvation: † I will sing to the Lord, who giveth me good things: * yea, I will sing to the name of the Lord the most High.

verses.lat: 15:1 Consérva me, Dómine, quóniam sperávi in te. ‡ (2) Dixi Dómino: Deus meus es tu, * quóniam bonórum meórum non eges.
verses.eng: 15:1 Preserve me, O Lord, for I have put my trust in thee. ‡  (2) I have said to the Lord, thou art my God, * for thou hast no need of my goods.

verses.lat: 15:3 Sanctis, qui sunt in terra ejus, * mirificávit omnes voluntátes meas in eis.
verses.eng: 15:3 To the saints, who are in his land, * he hath made wonderful all my desires in them.

verses.lat: 15:4a Multiplicátæ sunt infirmitátes eórum: * póstea acceleravérunt.
verses.eng: 15:4a Their infirmities were multiplied: * afterwards they made haste.

verses.lat: 15:4b Non congregábo conventícula eórum de sanguínibus, * nec memor ero nóminum eórum per lábia mea.
verses.eng: 15:4b I will not gather together their meetings for blood offerings: * nor will I be mindful of their names by my lips.

verses.lat: 15:5 Dóminus pars hereditátis meæ, et cálicis mei: * tu es, qui restítues hereditátem meam mihi.
verses.eng: 15:5 The Lord is the portion of my inheritance and of my cup: * it is thou that wilt restore my inheritance to me.

verses.lat: 15:6 Funes cecidérunt mihi in præcláris: * étenim heréditas mea præclára est mihi.
verses.eng: 15:6 The lines are fallen unto me in goodly places: * for my inheritance is goodly to me.

verses.lat: 15:7 Benedícam Dóminum, qui tríbuit mihi intelléctum: * ínsuper et usque ad noctem increpuérunt me renes mei.
verses.eng: 15:7 I will bless the Lord, who hath given me understanding: * moreover my reins also have corrected me even till night.

verses.lat: 15:8 Providébam Dóminum in conspéctu meo semper: * quóniam a dextris est mihi, ne commóvear.
verses.eng: 15:8 I set the Lord always in my sight: * for he is at my right hand, that I be not moved.

verses.lat: 15:9 Propter hoc lætátum est cor meum, et exsultávit lingua mea: * ínsuper et caro mea requiéscet in spe.
verses.eng: 15:9 Therefore my heart hath been glad, and my tongue hath rejoiced: * moreover my flesh also shall rest in hope.

verses.lat: 15:10 Quóniam non derelínques ánimam meam in inférno: * nec dabis sanctum tuum vidére corruptiónem.
verses.eng: 15:10 Because thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; * nor wilt thou give thy holy one to see corruption.

verses.lat: 15:11 Notas mihi fecísti vias vitæ, † adimplébis me lætítia cum vultu tuo: * delectatiónes in déxtera tua usque in finem.
verses.eng: 15:11 Thou hast made known to me the ways of life, † thou shalt fill me with joy with thy countenance: * at thy right hand are delights even to the end.

tertia.capitulum.label: Capitulum
tertia.capitulum.lat: Sana me, Dómine, et sanábor: salvum me fac, et salvus ero: quóniam laus mea tu es.
tertia.capitulum.eng: Heal me, O Lord, and I shall be healed: save me, and I shall be saved, for Thou art my praise.

responsory_breve_tertia.label: Responsory
responsory_breve_tertia.lat:
℟.br. Sana ánimam meam, * quia peccávi tibi.
℣. Ego dixi: Dómine, miserére mei.
℟. Quia peccávi tibi.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Sana ánimam meam, * quia peccávi tibi.
responsory_breve_tertia.eng:
℟.br. Heal my soul, * for I have sinned against Thee.
℣. I said: O Lord, be Thou merciful to me.
℟. For I have sinned against Thee.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. Heal my soul, * for I have sinned against Thee.

capitulum_sexta.label: Capitulum
capitulum_sexta.lat: Némini quidquam debeátis, nisi ut ínvicem diligátis: qui enim díligit próximum, legem implévit.
capitulum_sexta.eng: Owe no man any thing, but to love one another. For he that loveth his neighbour, hath fulfilled the law.

responsory_breve_sexta.label: Responsory
responsory_breve_sexta.lat:
℟.br. Benedícam Dóminum * in omni témpore.
℣. Semper laus ejus in ore meo.
℟. In omni témpore.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Benedícam Dóminum * in omni témpore.
responsory_breve_sexta.eng:
℟.br. I will bless the Lord * at all times.
℣. His praise shall be always in my mouth.
℟. At all times.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. I will bless the Lord * at all times.

capitulum_nona.label: Capitulum
capitulum_nona.lat: In timóre incolátus vestri témpore conversámini: sciéntes quod non corruptibílibus auro vel argénto redémpti estis, sed pretióso sánguine quasi Agni immaculáti Christi.
capitulum_nona.eng: Converse in fear during the time of your sojourning here. Knowing that you were not redeemed with corruptible things as gold or silver, but with the precious blood of Christ.

responsory_breve_nona.label: Responsory
responsory_breve_nona.lat:
℟.br. Rédime me, Dómine, * et miserére mei.
℣. Pes enim meus stetit in via recta.
℟. Et miserére mei.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Rédime me, Dómine, * et miserére mei.
responsory_breve_nona.eng:
℟.br. Redeem me, O Lord, * and have mercy on me.
℣. For my feet stood in the right way.
℟. And have mercy on me.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. Redeem me, O Lord, * and have mercy on me.

laudes.psalm1.label: Psalmus 95
laudes.psalm1.antiphonLat: Cantáte * Dómino et benedícite nómini ejus.
laudes.psalm1.antiphonEng: Sing ye * to the Lord and bless his name.

verses.lat: 95:1 Cantáte Dómino cánticum novum: * cantáte Dómino, omnis terra.
verses.eng: 95:1 Sing ye to the Lord a new canticle: * sing to the Lord, all the earth.

verses.lat: 95:2 Cantáte Dómino, et benedícite nómini ejus: * annuntiáte de die in diem salutáre ejus.
verses.eng: 95:2 Sing ye to the Lord and bless his name: * shew forth his salvation from day to day.

verses.lat: 95:3 Annuntiáte inter gentes glóriam ejus, * in ómnibus pópulis mirabília ejus.
verses.eng: 95:3 Declare his glory among the Gentiles: * his wonders among all people.

verses.lat: 95:4 Quóniam magnus Dóminus, et laudábilis nimis: * terríbilis est super omnes deos.
verses.eng: 95:4 For the Lord is great, and exceedingly to be praised: * he is to be feared above all gods.

verses.lat: 95:5 Quóniam omnes dii géntium dæmónia: * Dóminus autem cælos fecit.
verses.eng: 95:5 For all the gods of the Gentiles are devils: * but the Lord made the heavens.

verses.lat: 95:6 Conféssio, et pulchritúdo in conspéctu ejus: * sanctimónia et magnificéntia in sanctificatióne ejus.
verses.eng: 95:6 Praise and beauty are before him: * holiness and majesty in his sanctuary.

verses.lat: 95:7 Afférte Dómino, pátriæ géntium, afférte Dómino glóriam et honórem: * afférte Dómino glóriam nómini ejus.
verses.eng: 95:7 Bring ye to the Lord, O ye kindreds of the Gentiles, bring ye to the Lord glory and honour: * bring to the Lord glory unto his name.

verses.lat: 95:8 Tóllite hóstias, et introíte in átria ejus: * adoráte Dóminum in átrio sancto ejus.
verses.eng: 95:8 Bring up sacrifices, and come into his courts: * adore ye the Lord in his holy court.

verses.lat: 95:9 Commoveátur a fácie ejus univérsa terra: * dícite in géntibus quia Dóminus regnávit.
verses.eng: 95:9 Let all the earth be moved at his presence. * Say ye among the Gentiles, the Lord hath reigned.

verses.lat: 95:10 Étenim corréxit orbem terræ qui non commovébitur: * judicábit pópulos in æquitáte.
verses.eng: 95:10 For he hath corrected the world, which shall not be moved: * he will judge the people with justice.

verses.lat: 95:11 Læténtur cæli, et exsúltet terra: commoveátur mare, et plenitúdo ejus: * gaudébunt campi, et ómnia quæ in eis sunt.
verses.eng: 95:11 Let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth be glad, let the sea be moved, and the fulness thereof: * the fields and all things that are in them shall be joyful.

verses.lat: 95:12 Tunc exsultábunt ómnia ligna silvárum a fácie Dómini, quia venit: * quóniam venit judicáre terram.
verses.eng: 95:12 Then shall all the trees of the woods rejoice before the face of the Lord, because he cometh: * because he cometh to judge the earth.

verses.lat: 95:13 Judicábit orbem terræ in æquitáte, * et pópulos in veritáte sua.
verses.eng: 95:13 He shall judge the world with justice, * and the people with his truth.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Cantáte * Dómino et benedícite nómini ejus.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Sing ye * to the Lord and bless his name.

laudes.psalm2.label: Psalmus 42
laudes.psalm2.antiphonEng: The salvation of my countenance * and my God.

verses.lat: 42:1 Júdica me, Deus, et discérne causam meam de gente non sancta, * ab hómine iníquo, et dolóso érue me.
verses.eng: 42:1 Judge me, O God, and distinguish my cause from the nation that is not holy: * deliver me from the unjust and deceitful man.

verses.lat: 42:2 Quia tu es, Deus, fortitúdo mea: * quare me repulísti? et quare tristis incédo, dum afflígit me inimícus?
verses.eng: 42:2 For thou art God my strength: * why hast thou cast me off? and why do I go sorrowful whilst the enemy afflicteth me?

verses.lat: 42:3 Emítte lucem tuam et veritátem tuam: * ipsa me deduxérunt, et adduxérunt in montem sanctum tuum, et in tabernácula tua.
verses.eng: 42:3 Send forth thy light and thy truth: * they have conducted me, and brought me unto thy holy hill, and into thy tabernacles.

verses.lat: 42:4 Et introíbo ad altáre Dei: * ad Deum, qui lætíficat juventútem meam.
verses.eng: 42:4 And I will go in to the altar of God: * to God who giveth joy to my youth.

verses.lat: 42:5 Confitébor tibi in cíthara, Deus, Deus meus: * quare tristis es, ánima mea? et quare contúrbas me?
verses.eng: 42:5 To thee, O God my God, I will give praise upon the harp: * why art thou sad, O my soul? and why dost thou disquiet me?

verses.lat: 42:6 Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
verses.eng: 42:6 Hope in God, for I will still give praise to him: * the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: The salvation of my countenance * and my God.

laudes.psalm3.label: Psalmus 66
laudes.psalm3.antiphonLat: Illúmina, Dómine, * vultum tuum super nos.
laudes.psalm3.antiphonEng: May the Lord shine the light * of his countenance upon us.

verses.lat: 66:2 Deus misereátur nostri, et benedícat nobis: * illúminet vultum suum super nos, et misereátur nostri.
verses.eng: 66:2 May God have mercy on us, and bless us: * may he cause the light of his countenance to shine upon us, and may he have mercy on us.

verses.lat: 66:3 Ut cognoscámus in terra viam tuam, * in ómnibus géntibus salutáre tuum.
verses.eng: 66:3 That we may know thy way upon earth: * thy salvation in all nations.

verses.lat: 66:4 Confiteántur tibi pópuli, Deus: * confiteántur tibi pópuli omnes.
verses.eng: 66:4 Let people confess to thee, O God: * let all people give praise to thee.

verses.lat: 66:5 Læténtur et exsúltent gentes: * quóniam júdicas pópulos in æquitáte, et gentes in terra dírigis.
verses.eng: 66:5 Let the nations be glad and rejoice: * for thou judgest the people with justice, and directest the nations upon earth.

verses.lat: 66:6 Confiteántur tibi pópuli, Deus, confiteántur tibi pópuli omnes: * (7a) terra dedit fructum suum.
verses.eng: 66:6 Let the people, O God, confess to thee: * (7a) let all the people give praise to thee: the earth hath yielded her fruit.

verses.lat: 66:7b Benedícat nos Deus, Deus noster, (8) benedícat nos Deus: * et métuant eum omnes fines terræ.
verses.eng: 66:7b May God, our God bless us, (8) may God bless us: * and all the ends of the earth fear him.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Illúmina, Dómine, * vultum tuum super nos.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: May the Lord shine the light * of his countenance upon us.

laudes.canticle1.label: Canticum 212
laudes.canticle1.antiphonLat: Exaltáte * Regem sæculórum in opéribus vestris.
laudes.canticle1.antiphonEng: Give ye glory to him * in your works.

verses.lat: (Canticum Tobiæ * Tob. 13:1-11)
verses.eng: (Canticle of_Tobias * Tob. 13:1-11)

verses.lat: 13:1 Magnus es, Dómine, in ætérnum, * et in ómnia sǽcula regnum tuum:
verses.eng: 13:1 Thou art great, O Lord, for ever, * and thy kingdom is unto all ages:

verses.lat: 13:2 Quóniam tu flagéllas, et salvas: dedúcis ad ínferos, et redúcis: * et non est qui effúgiat manum tuam.
verses.eng: 13:2 For thou scourgest, and thou savest: thou leadest down to hell, and bringest up again: * and there is none that can escape thy hand.
