verses.lat: 13:3 Confitémini Dómino, fílii Israël, * et in conspéctu géntium laudáte eum:
verses.eng: 13:3 Give glory to the Lord, ye children of Israel, * and praise him in the sight of the Gentiles:

verses.lat: 13:4 Quóniam ídeo dispérsit vos inter gentes, quæ ignórant eum, * ut vos enarrétis mirabília ejus,
verses.eng: 13:4 Because he hath therefore scattered you among the Gentiles, who know not him, * that you may declare his wonderful works,

verses.lat: 13:5 Et faciátis scire eos, * quia non est álius Deus omnípotens præter eum.
verses.eng: 13:5 And make them know * that there is no other almighty God besides him.

verses.lat: 13:6 Ipse castigávit nos propter iniquitátes nostras: * et ipse salvábit nos propter misericórdiam suam.
verses.eng: 13:6 He hath chastised us for our iniquities: * and he will save us for his own mercy.

verses.lat: 13:7 Aspícite ergo quæ fecit nobíscum, et cum timóre et tremóre confitémini illi: * Regémque sæculórum exaltáte in opéribus vestris.
verses.eng: 13:7 See then what he hath done with us, and with fear and trembling give ye glory to him: * and extol the eternal King of worlds in your works.

verses.lat: 13:8 Ego autem in terra captivitátis meæ confitébor illi: * quóniam osténdit majestátem suam in gentem peccatrícem.
verses.eng: 13:8 As for me, I will praise him in the land of my captivity: * because he hath shewn his majesty toward a sinful nation.

verses.lat: 13:9 Convertímini ítaque, peccatóres, et fácite justítiam coram Deo, * credéntes quod fáciat vobíscum misericórdiam suam:
verses.eng: 13:9 Be converted therefore, ye sinners, and do justice before God, * believing that he will shew his mercy to you.

verses.lat: 13:10 Ego autem, et ánima mea * in eo lætábimur.
verses.eng: 13:10 And I and my soul * will rejoice in him.

verses.lat: 13:11 Benedícite Dóminum, omnes elécti ejus: * ágite dies lætítiæ, et confitémini illi.
verses.eng: 13:11 Bless ye the Lord, all his elect, * keep days of joy, and give glory to him.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Exaltáte * Regem sæculórum in opéribus vestris.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: Give ye glory to him * in your works.

laudes.psalm4.label: Psalmus 134
laudes.psalm4.antiphonLat: Laudáte * nomen Dómini, qui statis in domo Dómini.
laudes.psalm4.antiphonEng: Praise * the name of the Lord, ye who stand in the house of the Lord.

verses.lat: 134:1 Laudáte nomen Dómini, * laudáte, servi, Dóminum.
verses.eng: 134:1 Praise ye the name of the Lord: * O you his servants, praise the Lord:

verses.lat: 134:2 Qui statis in domo Dómini, * in átriis domus Dei nostri.
verses.eng: 134:2 You that stand in the house of the Lord, * in the courts of the house of our God.

verses.lat: 134:3 Laudáte Dóminum, quia bonus Dóminus: * psállite nómini ejus, quóniam suáve.
verses.eng: 134:3 Praise ye the Lord, for the Lord is good: * sing ye to his name, for it is sweet.

verses.lat: 134:4 Quóniam Jacob elégit sibi Dóminus, * Israël in possessiónem sibi.
verses.eng: 134:4 For the Lord hath chosen Jacob unto himself: * Israel for his own possession.

verses.lat: 134:5 Quia ego cognóvi quod magnus est Dóminus, * et Deus noster præ ómnibus diis.
verses.eng: 134:5 For I have known that the Lord is great, * and our God is above all gods.

verses.lat: 134:6 Ómnia quæcúmque vóluit, Dóminus fecit in cælo, et in terra, * in mari, et in ómnibus abýssis.
verses.eng: 134:6 Whatsoever the Lord pleased he hath done, in heaven, in earth, * in the sea, and in all the deeps.

verses.lat: 134:7 Edúcens nubes ab extrémo terræ: * fúlgura in plúviam fecit.
verses.eng: 134:7 He bringeth up clouds from the end of the earth: * he hath made lightnings for the rain.

verses.lat: 134:8 Qui prodúcit ventos de thesáuris suis: * qui percússit primogénita Ægýpti ab hómine usque ad pecus.
verses.eng: 134:8 He bringeth forth winds out of his stores: * He slew the firstborn of Egypt from man even unto beast.

verses.lat: 134:9 Et misit signa, et prodígia in médio tui, Ægýpte: * in Pharaónem, et in omnes servos ejus.
verses.eng: 134:9 He sent forth signs and wonders in the midst of thee, O Egypt: * upon Pharao, and upon all his servants.

verses.lat: 134:10 Qui percússit gentes multas: * et occídit reges fortes:
verses.eng: 134:10 He smote many nations, * and slew mighty kings:

verses.lat: 134:11 Sehon, regem Amorrhæórum, et Og, regem Basan, * et ómnia regna Chánaan.
verses.eng: 134:11 Sehon king of the Amorrhites, and Og king of Basan, * and all the kingdoms of Chanaan.

verses.lat: 134:12 Et dedit terram eórum hereditátem, * hereditátem Israël, pópulo suo.
verses.eng: 134:12 And gave their land for an inheritance, * for an inheritance to his people Israel.

verses.lat: 134:13 Dómine, nomen tuum in ætérnum: * Dómine, memoriále tuum in generatiónem et generatiónem.
verses.eng: 134:13 Thy name, O Lord, is for ever: * thy memorial, O Lord, unto all generations.

verses.lat: 134:14 Quia judicábit Dóminus pópulum suum: * et in servis suis deprecábitur.
verses.eng: 134:14 For the Lord will judge his people, * and will be entreated in favour of his servants.

verses.lat: 134:15 Simulácra géntium argéntum, et aurum, * ópera mánuum hóminum.
verses.eng: 134:15 The idols of the Gentiles are silver and gold, * the works of men’s hands.

verses.lat: 134:16 Os habent, et non loquéntur: * óculos habent, et non vidébunt.
verses.eng: 134:16 They have a mouth, but they speak not: * they have eyes, but they see not.

verses.lat: 134:17 Aures habent, et non áudient: * neque enim est spíritus in ore ipsórum.
verses.eng: 134:17 They have ears, but they hear not: * neither is there any breath in their mouths.

verses.lat: 134:18 Símiles illis fiant qui fáciunt ea: * et omnes qui confídunt in eis.
verses.eng: 134:18 Let them that make them be like to them: * and every one that trusteth in them.

verses.lat: 134:19 Domus Israël, benedícite Dómino: * domus Aaron, benedícite Dómino.
verses.eng: 134:19 Bless the Lord, O house of Israel: * bless the Lord, O house of Aaron.

verses.lat: 134:20 Domus Levi, benedícite Dómino: * qui timétis Dóminum, benedícite Dómino.
verses.eng: 134:20 Bless the Lord, O house of Levi: * you that fear the Lord, bless the Lord.

verses.lat: 134:21 Benedíctus Dóminus ex Sion, * qui hábitat in Jerúsalem.
verses.eng: 134:21 Blessed be the Lord out of Sion, * who dwelleth in Jerusalem.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Laudáte * nomen Dómini, qui statis in domo Dómini.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Praise * the name of the Lord, ye who stand in the house of the Lord.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (2 Cor 1:3-4)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Benedíctus Deus, et Pater Dómini nostri Jesu Christi, Pater misericordiárum, et Deus totíus consolatiónis, qui consolátur nos in omni tribulatióne nostra.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort, who comforteth us in all our tribulation.

capitulum_laudes.label: Capitulum (Rom 13:12-13)
capitulum_laudes.lat: Nox præcéssit, dies autem appropinquávit. Abiciámus ergo ópera tenebrárum, et induámur arma lucis. Sicut in die honéste ambulémus.
capitulum_laudes.eng: The night is passed, and the day is at hand. Let us therefore cast off the works of darkness, and put on the armour of light. Let us walk honestly, as in the day.

versum_tertia.label: Versiculus
versum_tertia.lat: ℣. Adjútor meus, esto, ne derelínquas me.
versum_tertia.eng: ℣. Be Thou my helper, forsake me not.
versum_tertia.latR: ℟. Neque despícias me, Deus, salutáris meus.
versum_tertia.engR: ℟. Do not Thou despise me, O God my Saviour.

versum_sexta.label: Versiculus
versum_sexta.lat: ℣. Dóminus regit me, et nihil mihi déerit.
versum_sexta.eng: ℣. The Lord ruleth me: and I shall want nothing.
versum_sexta.latR: ℟. In loco páscuæ ibi me collocávit.
versum_sexta.engR: ℟. He hath set me in a place of pasture.

versum_nona.label: Versiculus
versum_nona.lat: ℣. Ab occúltis meis munda me, Dómine.
versum_nona.eng: ℣. From my secret ones cleanse me, O Lord.
versum_nona.latR: ℟. Et ab aliénis parce servo tuo.
versum_nona.engR: ℟. And from those of others spare Thy servant.

ant_1.label: Antíphona
ant_1.eng: Overthrow, O Lord, * them that fight against me.

ant_2.label: Antíphona
ant_2.lat: Noli æmulári * in eo qui prosperátur et facit iniquitátem.
ant_2.eng: Envy not * the man who prospereth in his way; the man who doth unjust things.

ant_3.label: Antíphona
ant_3.lat: Ne in ira tua * corrípias me, Dómine.
ant_3.eng: O Lord, * do not chastise me in thy wrath.

nocturn_1_versum.label: Versicle after Nocturn I
nocturn_1_versum.eng: ℣. And my tongue shall meditate thy justice.
nocturn_1_versum.engR: ℟. Thy praise all the day long, O Lord.

nocturn_2_versum.label: Versicle after Nocturn II
nocturn_2_versum.lat: ℣. Exspécta Dóminum, et custódi viam ejus.
nocturn_2_versum.latR: ℟. Exaltábit te, ut hereditáte cápias terram.
nocturn_2_versum.eng: ℣. Expect the Lord and keep his way.
nocturn_2_versum.engR: ℟. He will exalt thee to inherit the land.

nocturn_3_versum.label: Versicle after Nocturn III
nocturn_3_versum.lat: ℣. Deus, ne síleas a me, remítte mihi.
nocturn_3_versum.latR: ℟. Quóniam íncola ego sum apud te et peregrínus.
nocturn_3_versum.eng: ℣. O Lord, be not thou silent, forgive me.
nocturn_3_versum.engR: ℟. For I am a stranger with thee, and a sojourner.

hymnus_laudes.label: Hymn
hymnus_laudes.title: Ales diéi núntius
hymnus_laudes.lat:
Ales diéi núntius
Lucem propínquam prǽcinit:
Nos excitátor méntium
Jam Christus ad vitam vocat.

Auférte, clamat, léctulos,
Ægro sopóre désides:
Castíque, recti, ac sóbrii
Vigiláte, jam sum próximus.

Jesum ciámus vócibus,
Flentes, precántes, sóbrii:
Inténta supplicátio
Dormíre cor mundum vetat.

Tu, Christe, somnum díscute:
Tu rumpe noctis víncula:
Tu solve peccátum vetus,
Novúmque lumen íngere.

Deo Patri sit glória,
Ejúsque soli Fílio,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
Nunc et per omne sǽculum.
Amen.
hymnus_laudes.eng:
As the bird, whose clarion gay
Sounds before the dawn is grey,
Christ, who brings the spirit’s day,
Calls us, close at hand:

Wake! he cries, and for my sake,
From your eyes dull slumbers shake!
Sober, righteous, chaste, awake!
At the door I stand!

Lord, to thee we lift on high
Fervent prayer and bitter cry:
Hearts aroused to pray and sigh
May not slumber more:

Break the sleep of death and time,
Forged by Adam’s ancient crime;
And the light of Eden’s prime
To the world restore!

Unto God the Father, Son,
Holy Spirit, Three in One,
One in Three, be glory done,
Now and evermore.
Amen.

hymnus_vespera.label: Hymn
hymnus_vespera.title: Tellúris alme Cónditor
hymnus_vespera.lat:
Tellúris alme Cónditor,
Mundi solum qui séparans,
Pulsis aquæ moléstiis,
Terram dedísti immóbilem:

Ut germen aptum próferens,
Fulvis decóra flóribus,
Fecúnda fructu sísteret,
Pastúmque gratum rédderet.

Mentis perústæ vúlnera
Munda viróre grátiæ:
Ut facta fletu díluat,
Motúsque pravos átterat.

Jussis tuis obtémperet:
Nullis malis appróximet:
Bonis repléri gáudeat,
Et mortis ictum nésciat.

Præsta, Pater piíssime,
Patríque compar Únice,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito
Regnans per omne sǽculum.
Amen.
hymnus_vespera.eng:
Earth's mighty Maker, whose command
Raised from the sea the solid land;
And drove each billowy heap away,
And bade the earth stand firm for aye:

That so, with flowers of golden hue,
The seeds of each it might renew;
And fruit-trees bearing fruit might yield,
And pleasant pasture of the field:

Our spirit’s rankling wounds efface
With dewy freshness of thy grace:
That grief may cleanse each deed of ill,
And o’er each lust may triumph still.

Let every soul thy law obey,
And keep from every evil way;
Rejoice each promised good to win,
And flee from every mortal sin.

Hear thou our prayer, Almighty King!
Hear thou our praises, while we sing,
Adoring with the heavenly host,
The Father, Son, and Holy Ghost!
Amen.

ant_laudes.label: Antiphon ad Benedictus
ant_laudes.lat: Eréxit nobis * Dóminus cornu salútis in domo David púeri sui.
ant_laudes.eng: The Lord has raised up * a horn of salvation for us in the house of David his servant.

ant_vespera.label: Antiphon ad Magnificat
ant_vespera.lat: Exsultávit * spíritus meus in Deo salutári meo.
ant_vespera.eng: My spirit rejoices * in God, in my Saviour.

versum_1.label: Versicle
versum_1.eng: We are filled in the morning with thy mercy.
versum_1.engR: And we have rejoiced, and are delighted.

matutinum.psalm2.label: Psalmus 44 (2a-10b)

verses.lat: 44:2a Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum: * dico ego ópera mea Regi.
verses.eng: 44:2a My heart hath uttered a good word; * I speak my works to the King.

verses.lat: 44:2b Lingua mea cálamus scribæ: * velóciter scribéntis.
verses.eng: 44:2b My tongue is the pen of a scrivener * that writeth swiftly.

verses.lat: 44:3 Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, † diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis: * proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.
verses.eng: 44:3 Thou art beautiful above the sons of men: † grace is poured abroad in thy lips; * therefore hath God blessed thee for ever.

verses.lat: 44:4 Accíngere gládio tuo super femur tuum, * potentíssime.
verses.eng: 44:4 Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, * O thou most mighty.

verses.lat: 44:5a Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua: * inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
verses.eng: 44:5a With thy comeliness and thy beauty * set out, proceed prosperously, and reign.

verses.lat: 44:5b Propter veritátem, et mansuetúdinem, et justítiam: * et dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua.
verses.eng: 44:5b Because of truth and meekness and justice: * and thy right hand shall conduct thee wonderfully.

verses.lat: 44:6 Sagíttæ tuæ acútæ, pópuli sub te cadent: * in corda inimicórum Regis.
verses.eng: 44:6 Thy arrows are sharp: under thee shall people fall, * into the hearts of the king’s enemies.

verses.lat: 44:7 Sedes tua, Deus, in sǽculum sǽculi: * virga directiónis virga regni tui.
verses.eng: 44:7 Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: * the sceptre of thy kingdom is a sceptre of uprightness.

verses.lat: 44:8 Dilexísti justítiam, et odísti iniquitátem: * proptérea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, óleo lætítiæ præ consórtibus tuis.
verses.eng: 44:8 Thou hast loved justice, and hated iniquity: * therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.

verses.lat: 44:9 Myrrha, et gutta, et cásia a vestiméntis tuis, a dómibus ebúrneis: * ex quibus delectavérunt te (10a) fíliæ regum in honóre tuo.
verses.eng: 44:9 Myrrh and stacte and cassia perfume thy garments, from the ivory houses: * out of which (10a) the daughters of kings have delighted thee in thy glory.

verses.lat: 44:10b Ástitit regína a dextris tuis in vestítu deauráto: * circúmdata varietáte.
verses.eng: 44:10b The queen stood on thy right hand, in gilded clothing; * surrounded with variety.

matutinum.psalm2.antiphonLat: Speciósus forma * præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis.
matutinum.psalm2.antiphonEng: Thou art beautiful * above the sons of men: grace is poured abroad in thy lips.

matutinum.psalm3.label: Psalmus 44 (11-18b)

verses.lat: 44:11 Audi fília, et vide, et inclína aurem tuam: * et oblivíscere pópulum tuum et domum patris tui.
verses.eng: 44:11 Hearken, O daughter, and see, and incline thy ear: * and forget thy people and thy father’s house.

verses.lat: 44:12 Et concupíscet Rex decórem tuum: * quóniam ipse est Dóminus Deus tuus, et adorábunt eum.
verses.eng: 44:12 And the king shall greatly desire thy beauty; * for he is the Lord thy God, and him they shall adore.

verses.lat: 44:13 Et fíliæ Tyri in munéribus * vultum tuum deprecabúntur: omnes dívites plebis.
verses.eng: 44:13 And the daughters of Tyre with gifts, * yea, all the rich among the people, shall entreat thy countenance.

verses.lat: 44:14 Omnis glória ejus fíliæ Regis ab intus, * in fímbriis áureis (15a) circumamícta varietátibus.
verses.eng: 44:14 All the glory of the king’s daughter is within, * in golden borders, (15a) clothed round about with varieties.

verses.lat: 44:15b Adducéntur Regi vírgines post eam: * próximæ ejus afferéntur tibi.
verses.eng: 44:15b After her shall virgins be brought to the king: * her neighbours shall be brought to thee.

verses.lat: 44:16 Afferéntur in lætítia et exsultatióne: * adducéntur in templum Regis.
verses.eng: 44:16 They shall be brought with gladness and rejoicing: * they shall be brought into the temple of the king.

verses.lat: 44:17 Pro pátribus tuis nati sunt tibi fílii: * constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram.
verses.eng: 44:17 Instead of thy fathers, sons are born to thee: * thou shalt make them princes over all the earth.

verses.lat: 44:18a Mémores erunt nóminis tui: * in omni generatióne et generatiónem.
verses.eng: 44:18a They shall remember thy name * throughout all generations.

verses.lat: 44:18b Proptérea pópuli confitebúntur tibi in ætérnum: * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
verses.eng: 44:18b Therefore shall people praise thee for ever; yea, * for ever and ever.

matutinum.psalm3.antiphonLat: Confitebúntur tibi * pópuli Deus in ætérnum.
matutinum.psalm3.antiphonEng: Let people confess to thee, * O God, forever.

matutinum.psalm4.label: Psalmus 45

verses.lat: 45:2 Deus noster refúgium, et virtus: * adjútor in tribulatiónibus, quæ invenérunt nos nimis.
verses.eng: 45:2 Our God is our refuge and strength: * a helper in troubles, which have found us exceedingly.

verses.lat: 45:3 Proptérea non timébimus dum turbábitur terra: * et transferéntur montes in cor maris.
verses.eng: 45:3 Therefore we will not fear, when the earth shall be troubled; * and the mountains shall be removed into the heart of the sea.

verses.lat: 45:4 Sonuérunt, et turbátæ sunt aquæ eórum: * conturbáti sunt montes in fortitúdine ejus.
verses.eng: 45:4 Their waters roared and were troubled: * the mountains were troubled with his strength.

verses.lat: 45:5 Flúminis ímpetus lætíficat civitátem Dei: * sanctificávit tabernáculum suum Altíssimus.
verses.eng: 45:5 The stream of the river maketh the city of God joyful: * the most High hath sanctified his own tabernacle.

verses.lat: 45:6 Deus in médio ejus, non commovébitur: * adjuvábit eam Deus mane dilúculo.
verses.eng: 45:6 God is in the midst thereof, it shall not be moved: * God will help it in the morning early.

verses.lat: 45:7 Conturbátæ sunt gentes, et inclináta sunt regna: * dedit vocem suam, mota est terra.
verses.eng: 45:7 Nations were troubled, and kingdoms were bowed down: * he uttered his voice, the earth trembled.

verses.lat: 45:8 Dóminus virtútum nobíscum: * suscéptor noster Deus Jacob.
verses.eng: 45:8 The Lord of armies is with us: * the God of Jacob is our protector.

verses.lat: 45:9 Veníte, et vidéte ópera Dómini, quæ pósuit prodígia super terram: * áuferens bella usque ad finem terræ.
verses.eng: 45:9 Come and behold ye the works of the Lord: what wonders he hath done upon earth, * making wars to cease even to the end of the earth.

verses.lat: 45:10 Arcum cónteret, et confrínget arma: * et scuta combúret igni.
verses.eng: 45:10 He shall destroy the bow, and break the weapons: * and the shield he shall burn in the fire.

verses.lat: 45:11 Vacáte, et vidéte quóniam ego sum Deus: * exaltábor in géntibus, et exaltábor in terra.
verses.eng: 45:11 Be still and see that I am God; * I will be exalted among the nations, and I will be exalted in the earth.

verses.lat: 45:12 Dóminus virtútum nobíscum: * suscéptor noster Deus Jacob.
verses.eng: 45:12 The Lord of armies is with us: * the God of Jacob is our protector.

matutinum.psalm4.antiphonEng: Our God * is our helper in troubles.

matutinum.psalm5.label: Psalmus 47

verses.lat: 47:2 Magnus Dóminus, et laudábilis nimis * in civitáte Dei nostri, in monte sancto ejus.
verses.eng: 47:2 Great is the Lord, and exceedingly to be praised * in the city of our God, in his holy mountain.

verses.lat: 47:3 Fundátur exsultatióne univérsæ terræ mons Sion, * látera Aquilónis, cívitas Regis magni.
verses.eng: 47:3 With the joy of the whole earth is mount Sion founded, * on the sides of the north, the city of the great king.

verses.lat: 47:4 Deus in dómibus ejus cognoscétur: * cum suscípiet eam.
verses.eng: 47:4 In her houses shall God be known, * when he shall protect her.

verses.lat: 47:5 Quóniam ecce reges terræ congregáti sunt: * convenérunt in unum.
verses.eng: 47:5 For behold the kings of the earth assembled themselves: * they gathered together.

verses.lat: 47:6 Ipsi vidéntes sic admiráti sunt, conturbáti sunt, commóti sunt: * tremor apprehéndit eos.
verses.eng: 47:6 So they saw, and they wondered, they were troubled, they were moved: * trembling took hold of them.

verses.lat: 47:7 Ibi dolóres ut parturiéntis: * in spíritu veheménti cónteres naves Tharsis.
verses.eng: 47:7 There were pains as of a woman in labour; * with a vehement wind thou shalt break in pieces the ships of Tharsis.

verses.lat: 47:9 Sicut audívimus, sic vídimus in civitáte Dómini virtútum, in civitáte Dei nostri: * Deus fundávit eam in ætérnum.
verses.eng: 47:9 As we have heard, so have we seen, in the city of the Lord of hosts, in the city of our God: * God hath founded it for ever.

verses.lat: 47:10 Suscépimus, Deus, misericórdiam tuam, * in médio templi tui.
verses.eng: 47:10 We have received thy mercy, O God, * in the midst of thy temple.

verses.lat: 47:11 Secúndum nomen tuum, Deus, sic et laus tua in fines terræ: * justítia plena est déxtera tua.
verses.eng: 47:11 According to thy name, O God, so also is thy praise unto the ends of the earth: * thy right hand is full of justice.

verses.lat: 47:12 Lætétur mons Sion, et exsúltent fíliæ Judæ: * propter judícia tua, Dómine.
verses.eng: 47:12 Let mount Sion rejoice, and the daughters of Juda be glad; * because of thy judgments, O Lord.

verses.lat: 47:13 Circúmdate Sion, et complectímini eam: * narráte in túrribus ejus.
verses.eng: 47:13 Surround Sion, and encompass her: * tell ye in her towers.

verses.lat: 47:14 Pónite corda vestra in virtúte ejus: * et distribúite domos ejus, ut enarrétis in progénie áltera.
verses.eng: 47:14 Set your hearts on her strength; and distribute her houses, * that ye may relate it in another generation.

verses.lat: 47:15 Quóniam hic est Deus, Deus noster in ætérnum et in sǽculum sǽculi: * ipse reget nos in sǽcula.
verses.eng: 47:15 For this is God, our God unto eternity, and for ever and ever: * he shall rule us for evermore.

matutinum.psalm5.antiphonLat: Magnus Dóminus * et laudábilis nimis in civitáte Dei nostri.
matutinum.psalm5.antiphonEng: Great is the Lord * and exceedingly to be praised in the city of our God.

matutinum.psalm6.label: Psalmus 48 (2-13)

verses.lat: 48:2 Audíte hæc, omnes gentes: * áuribus percípite omnes, qui habitátis orbem:
verses.eng: 48:2 Hear these things, all ye nations: * give ear, all ye inhabitants of the world.

verses.lat: 48:3 Quique terrígenæ, et fílii hóminum: * simul in unum dives et pauper.
verses.eng: 48:3 All you that are earthborn, and you sons of men: * both rich and poor together.

verses.lat: 48:4 Os meum loquétur sapiéntiam: * et meditátio cordis mei prudéntiam.
verses.eng: 48:4 My mouth shall speak wisdom: * and the meditation of my heart understanding

verses.lat: 48:5 Inclinábo in parábolam aurem meam: * apériam in psaltério propositiónem meam.
verses.eng: 48:5 I will incline my ear to a parable; * I will open my proposition on the psaltery.

verses.lat: 48:6 Cur timébo in die mala? * iníquitas calcánei mei circúmdabit me:
verses.eng: 48:6 Why shall I fear in the evil day? * the iniquity of my heel shall encompass me.

verses.lat: 48:7 Qui confídunt in virtúte sua: * et in multitúdine divitiárum suárum gloriántur.
verses.eng: 48:7 They that trust in their own strength, * and glory in the multitude of their riches,

verses.lat: 48:8 Frater non rédimit, rédimet homo: * non dabit Deo placatiónem suam.
verses.eng: 48:8 No brother can redeem, nor shall man redeem: * he shall not give to God his ransom,

verses.lat: 48:9 Et prétium redemptiónis ánimæ suæ: * et laborábit in ætérnum, et vivet adhuc in finem.
verses.eng: 48:9 Nor the price of the redemption of his soul: * and shall labour for ever, and shall still live unto the end.

verses.lat: 48:11 Non vidébit intéritum, cum víderit sapiéntes moriéntes: * simul insípiens, et stultus períbunt.
verses.eng: 48:11 He shall not see destruction, when he shall see the wise dying: * the senseless and the fool shall perish together:

verses.lat: 48:11 Et relínquent aliénis divítias suas: * et sepúlcra eórum domus illórum in ætérnum.
verses.eng: 48:11 And they shall leave their riches to strangers: * and their sepulchres shall be their houses for ever.

verses.lat: 48:12 Tabernácula eórum in progénie et progénie: * vocavérunt nómina sua in terris suis.
verses.eng: 48:12 Their dwelling places to all generations: * they have called their lands by their names.

verses.lat: 48:13 Et homo, cum in honóre esset, non intelléxit: * comparátus est juméntis insipiéntibus, et símilis factus est illis.
verses.eng: 48:13 And man when he was in honour did not understand; * he is compared to senseless beasts, and is become like to them.

matutinum.psalm6.antiphonLat: Os meum loquétur * sapiéntiam: et meditátio cordis mei prudéntiam.
matutinum.psalm6.antiphonEng: My mouth shall speak * wisdom: and the meditation of my heart understanding.

matutinum.psalm7.label: Psalmus 48 (14-21)

verses.lat: 48:14 Hæc via illórum scándalum ipsis: * et póstea in ore suo complacébunt.
verses.eng: 48:14 This way of theirs is a stumbling block to them: * and afterwards they shall delight in their mouth.

verses.lat: 48:15 Sicut oves in inférno pósiti sunt: * mors depáscet eos.
verses.eng: 48:15 They are laid in hell like sheep: * death shall feed upon them.

verses.lat: 48:15 Et dominabúntur eórum justi in matutíno: * et auxílium eórum veteráscet in inférno a glória eórum.
verses.eng: 48:15 And the just shall have dominion over them in the morning; * and their help shall decay in hell from their glory.

verses.lat: 48:16 Verúmtamen Deus rédimet ánimam meam de manu ínferi: * cum accéperit me.
verses.eng: 48:16 But God will redeem my soul from the hand of hell, * when he shall receive me.

verses.lat: 48:17 Ne timúeris, cum dives factus fúerit homo: * et cum multiplicáta fúerit glória domus ejus.
verses.eng: 48:17 Be not thou afraid, when a man shall be made rich, * and when the glory of his house shall be increased.

verses.lat: 48:18 Quóniam cum interíerit, non sumet ómnia: * neque descéndet cum eo glória ejus.
verses.eng: 48:18 For when he shall die he shall take nothing away; * nor shall his glory descend with him.

verses.lat: 48:19 Quia ánima ejus in vita ipsíus benedicétur: * confitébitur tibi cum beneféceris ei.
verses.eng: 48:19 For in his lifetime his soul will be blessed: * and he will praise thee when thou shalt do well to him.

verses.lat: 48:20 Introíbit usque in progénies patrum suórum: * et usque in ætérnum non vidébit lumen.
verses.eng: 48:20 He shall go in to the generations of his fathers: * and he shall never see light.

verses.lat: 48:21 Homo, cum in honóre esset, non intelléxit: * comparátus est juméntis insipiéntibus, et símilis factus est illis.
verses.eng: 48:21 Man when he was in honour did not understand: * he hath been compared to senseless beasts, and made like to them.

matutinum.psalm7.antiphonLat: Ne timúeris * cum dívite non descéndet in sepúlcrum glória ejus.
matutinum.psalm7.antiphonEng: Be not thou afraid * the things which made him rich, or his glory shall not descend with him to the sepulchre.

matutinum.psalm8.label: Psalmus 49 (1-15)

verses.lat: 49:1 Deus deórum, Dóminus locútus est: * et vocávit terram,
verses.eng: 49:1 The God of gods, the Lord hath spoken: * and he hath called the earth.

verses.lat: 49:1 A solis ortu usque ad occásum: * ex Sion spécies decóris ejus.
verses.eng: 49:1 From the rising of the sun, to the going down thereof: * out of Sion the loveliness of his beauty.

verses.lat: 49:3 Deus maniféste véniet: * Deus noster et non silébit.
verses.eng: 49:3 God shall come manifestly: our God shall come, * and shall not keep silence.

verses.lat: 49:3 Ignis in conspéctu ejus exardéscet: * et in circúitu ejus tempéstas válida.
verses.eng: 49:3 A fire shall burn before him: * and a mighty tempest shall be round about

verses.lat: 49:4 Advocábit cælum desúrsum: * et terram discérnere pópulum suum.
verses.eng: 49:4 He shall call heaven from above, * and the earth, to judge his people.

verses.lat: 49:5 Congregáte illi sanctos ejus: * qui órdinant testaméntum ejus super sacrifícia.
verses.eng: 49:5 Gather ye together his saints to him: * who set his covenant before sacrifices.

verses.lat: 49:6 Et annuntiábunt cæli justítiam ejus: * quóniam Deus judex est.
verses.eng: 49:6 And the heavens shall declare his justice: * for God is judge.

verses.lat: 49:7 Audi, pópulus meus, et loquar: Israël, et testificábor tibi: * Deus, Deus tuus ego sum.
verses.eng: 49:7 Hear, O my people, and I will speak: O Israel, and I will testify to thee: * I am God, thy God.

verses.lat: 49:8 Non in sacrifíciis tuis árguam te: * holocáusta autem tua in conspéctu meo sunt semper.
verses.eng: 49:8 I will not reprove thee for thy sacrifices: * and thy burnt offerings are always in my sight.

verses.lat: 49:9 Non accípiam de domo tua vítulos: * neque de grégibus tuis hircos.
verses.eng: 49:9 I will not take calves out of thy house: * nor he goats out of thy flocks.

verses.lat: 49:10 Quóniam meæ sunt omnes feræ silvárum: * juménta in móntibus et boves.
verses.eng: 49:10 For all the beasts of the woods are mine: * the cattle on the hills, and the oxen.

verses.lat: 49:11 Cognóvi ómnia volatília cæli: * et pulchritúdo agri mecum est.
verses.eng: 49:11 I know all the fowls of the air: * and with me is the beauty of the field.

verses.lat: 49:12 Si esuríero, non dicam tibi: * meus est enim orbis terræ, et plenitúdo ejus.
verses.eng: 49:12 If I should be hungry, I would not tell thee: * for the world is mine, and the fulness thereof.

verses.lat: 49:13 Numquid manducábo carnes taurórum? * aut sánguinem hircórum potábo?
verses.eng: 49:13 Shall I eat the flesh of bullocks? * or shall I drink the blood of goats?

verses.lat: 49:14 Ímmola Deo sacrifícium laudis: * et redde Altíssimo vota tua.
verses.eng: 49:14 Offer to God the sacrifice of praise: * and pay thy vows to the most High.

verses.lat: 49:15 Et ínvoca me in die tribulatiónis: * éruam te, et honorificábis me.
verses.eng: 49:15 And call upon me in the day of trouble: * I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify me.

matutinum.psalm8.antiphonEng: The God of gods, * the Lord hath spoken.

matutinum.psalm9.label: Psalmus 49 (16-23)

verses.lat: 49:16 Peccatóri autem dixit Deus: * Quare tu enárras justítias meas, et assúmis testaméntum meum per os tuum?
verses.eng: 49:16 But to the sinner God hath said: * Why dost thou declare my justices, and take my covenant in thy mouth?

verses.lat: 49:17 Tu vero odísti disciplínam: * et projecísti sermónes meos retrórsum:
verses.eng: 49:17 Seeing thou hast hated discipline: * and hast cast my words behind thee.

verses.lat: 49:18 Si vidébas furem, currébas cum eo: * et cum adúlteris portiónem tuam ponébas.
verses.eng: 49:18 If thou didst see a thief thou didst run with him: * and with adulterers thou hast been a partaker.

verses.lat: 49:19 Os tuum abundávit malítia: * et lingua tua concinnábat dolos.
verses.eng: 49:19 Thy mouth hath abounded with evil, * and thy tongue framed deceits.

verses.lat: 49:20 Sedens advérsus fratrem tuum loquebáris, et advérsus fílium matris tuæ ponébas scándalum: * hæc fecísti, et tácui.
verses.eng: 49:20 Sitting thou didst speak against thy brother, and didst lay a scandal against thy mother’s son: * these things hast thou done, and I was silent.

verses.lat: 49:21 Existimásti, iníque, quod ero tui símilis: * árguam te, et státuam contra fáciem tuam.
verses.eng: 49:21 Thou thoughtest unjustly that I should be like to thee: * but I will reprove thee, and set before thy face.

verses.lat: 49:22 Intellégite hæc, qui obliviscímini Deum: * nequándo rápiat, et non sit qui erípiat.
verses.eng: 49:22 Understand these things, you that forget God; * lest he snatch you away, and there be none to deliver you.

verses.lat: 49:23 Sacrifícium laudis honorificábit me: * et illic iter, quo osténdam illi salutáre Dei.
verses.eng: 49:23 The sacrifice of praise shall glorify me: * and there is the way by which I will shew him the salvation of God.

matutinum.psalm9.antiphonEng: Understand these things, * you that forget God.

matutinum.psalm10.label: Psalmus 50

verses.lat: 50:3a Miserére mei, Deus, * secúndum magnam misericórdiam tuam.
verses.eng: 50:3a Have mercy on me, O God, * according to thy great mercy.

verses.lat: 50:3b Et secúndum multitúdinem miseratiónum tuárum, * dele iniquitátem meam.
verses.eng: 50:3b And according to the multitude of thy tender mercies * blot out my iniquity.

verses.lat: 50:4 Ámplius lava me ab iniquitáte mea: * et a peccáto meo munda me.
verses.eng: 50:4 Wash me yet more from my iniquity, * and cleanse me from my sin.

verses.lat: 50:5 Quóniam iniquitátem meam ego cognósco: * et peccátum meum contra me est semper.
verses.eng: 50:5 For I know my iniquity, * and my sin is always before me.

verses.lat: 50:6 Tibi soli peccávi, et malum coram te feci: * ut justificéris in sermónibus tuis, et vincas cum judicáris.
verses.eng: 50:6 To thee only have I sinned, and have done evil before thee: * that thou mayst be justified in thy words, and mayst overcome when thou art judged.

verses.lat: 50:7 Ecce enim, in iniquitátibus concéptus sum: * et in peccátis concépit me mater mea.
verses.eng: 50:7 For behold I was conceived in iniquities; * and in sins did my mother conceive me.

verses.lat: 50:8 Ecce enim, veritátem dilexísti: * incérta et occúlta sapiéntiæ tuæ manifestásti mihi.
verses.eng: 50:8 For behold thou hast loved truth: * the uncertain and hidden things of thy wisdom thou hast made manifest to me.

verses.lat: 50:9 Aspérges me hyssópo, et mundábor: * lavábis me, et super nivem dealbábor.
verses.eng: 50:9 Thou shalt sprinkle me with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed: * thou shalt wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow.

verses.lat: 50:10 Audítui meo dabis gáudium et lætítiam: * et exsultábunt ossa humiliáta.
verses.eng: 50:10 To my hearing thou shalt give joy and gladness: * and the bones that have been humbled shall rejoice.

verses.lat: 50:11 Avérte fáciem tuam a peccátis meis: * et omnes iniquitátes meas dele.
verses.eng: 50:11 Turn away thy face from my sins, * and blot out all my iniquities.

verses.lat: 50:12 Cor mundum crea in me, Deus: * et spíritum rectum ínnova in viscéribus meis.
verses.eng: 50:12 Create a clean heart in me, O God: * and renew a right spirit within my bowels.

verses.lat: 50:13 Ne proícias me a fácie tua: * et spíritum sanctum tuum ne áuferas a me.
verses.eng: 50:13 Cast me not away from thy face; * and take not thy holy spirit from me.

verses.lat: 50:14 Redde mihi lætítiam salutáris tui: * et spíritu principáli confírma me.
verses.eng: 50:14 Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation, * and strengthen me with a perfect spirit.

verses.lat: 50:15 Docébo iníquos vias tuas: * et ímpii ad te converténtur.
verses.eng: 50:15 I will teach the unjust thy ways: * and the wicked shall be converted to thee.

verses.lat: 50:16 Líbera me de sanguínibus, Deus, Deus salútis meæ: * et exsultábit lingua mea justítiam tuam.
verses.eng: 50:16 Deliver me from blood, O God, thou God of my salvation: * and my tongue shall extol thy justice.

verses.lat: 50:17 Dómine, lábia mea apéries: * et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.
verses.eng: 50:17 O Lord, thou wilt open my lips: * and my mouth shall declare thy praise.

verses.lat: 50:18 Quóniam si voluísses sacrifícium, dedíssem útique: * holocáustis non delectáberis.
verses.eng: 50:18 For if thou hadst desired sacrifice, I would indeed have given it: * with burnt offerings thou wilt not be delighted.

verses.lat: 50:19 Sacrifícium Deo spíritus contribulátus: * cor contrítum, et humiliátum, Deus, non despícies.
verses.eng: 50:19 A sacrifice to God is an afflicted spirit: * a contrite and humbled heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.

verses.lat: 50:20 Benígne fac, Dómine, in bona voluntáte tua Sion: * ut ædificéntur muri Jerúsalem.
verses.eng: 50:20 Deal favourably, O Lord, in thy good will with Sion; * that the walls of Jerusalem may be built up.

verses.lat: 50:21 Tunc acceptábis sacrifícium justítiæ, oblatiónes, et holocáusta: * tunc impónent super altáre tuum vítulos.
verses.eng: 50:21 Then shalt thou accept the sacrifice of justice, oblations and whole burnt offerings: * then shall they lay calves upon thy altar.

matutinum.psalm10.antiphonLat: Acceptábis sacrifícium * justítiæ super altáre tuum, Dómine.
matutinum.psalm10.antiphonEng: Thou shalt accept the sacrifice * of justice, upon thy altar, O Lord.

vesperae.psalm1.label: Psalmus 127
vesperae.psalm1.antiphonEng: Blessed are all * they that fear the Lord.

verses.lat: 127:1 Beáti, omnes, qui timent Dóminum, * qui ámbulant in viis ejus.
verses.eng: 127:1 Blessed are all they that fear the Lord: * that walk in his ways.

verses.lat: 127:2 Labóres mánuum tuárum quia manducábis: * beátus es, et bene tibi erit.
verses.eng: 127:2 For thou shalt eat the labours of thy hands: * blessed art thou, and it shall be well with thee.

verses.lat: 127:3a Uxor tua sicut vitis abúndans, * in latéribus domus tuæ.
verses.eng: 127:3a Thy wife as a fruitful vine, * on the sides of thy house.

verses.lat: 127:3b Fílii tui sicut novéllæ olivárum, * in circúitu mensæ tuæ.
verses.eng: 127:3b Thy children as olive plants, * round about thy table.

verses.lat: 127:4 Ecce, sic benedicétur homo, * qui timet Dóminum.
verses.eng: 127:4 Behold, thus shall the man be blessed * that feareth the Lord.

verses.lat: 127:5 Benedícat tibi Dóminus ex Sion: * et vídeas bona Jerúsalem ómnibus diébus vitæ tuæ.
verses.eng: 127:5 May the Lord bless thee out of Sion: * and mayst thou see the good things of Jerusalem all the days of thy life.

verses.lat: 127:6 Et vídeas fílios filiórum tuórum, * pacem super Israël.
verses.eng: 127:6 And mayst thou see thy children’s children, * peace upon Israel.

vesperae.psalm2.label: Psalmus 128
vesperae.psalm2.antiphonEng: Let them all be confounded * who hate Sion.

verses.lat: 128:1 Sæpe expugnavérunt me a juventúte mea, * dicat nunc Israël.
verses.eng: 128:1 Often have they fought against me from my youth, * let Israel now say.

verses.lat: 128:2 Sæpe expugnavérunt me a juventúte mea: * étenim non potuérunt mihi.
verses.eng: 128:2 Often have they fought against me from my youth: * but they could not prevail over me.

verses.lat: 128:3 Supra dorsum meum fabricavérunt peccatóres: * prolongavérunt iniquitátem suam.
verses.eng: 128:3 The wicked have wrought upon my back: * they have lengthened their iniquity.

verses.lat: 128:4 Dóminus justus concídit cervíces peccatórum: * confundántur et convertántur retrórsum omnes, qui odérunt Sion.
verses.eng: 128:4 The Lord who is just will cut the necks of sinners: * let them all be confounded and turned back that hate Sion.

verses.lat: 128:6 Fiant sicut fænum tectórum: * quod priúsquam evellátur, exáruit:
verses.eng: 128:6 Let them be as grass upon the tops of houses: * which withereth before it be plucked up:

verses.lat: 128:7 De quo non implévit manum suam qui metit, * et sinum suum qui manípulos cólligit.
verses.eng: 128:7 Wherewith the mower filleth not his hand: * nor he that gathereth sheaves his bosom.

verses.lat: 128:8 Et non dixérunt qui præteríbant: Benedíctio Dómini super vos: * benedíximus vobis in nómine Dómini.
verses.eng: 128:8 And they that passed by have not said: The blessing of the Lord be upon you: * we have blessed you in the name of the Lord.

vesperae.psalm3.label: Psalmus 129
vesperae.psalm3.antiphonLat: De profúndis * clamávi ad te, Dómine.
vesperae.psalm3.antiphonEng: Out of the depths * I have cried to thee, O Lord.

verses.lat: 129:1 De profúndis clamávi ad te, Dómine: * Dómine, exáudi vocem meam:
verses.eng: 129:1 Out of the depths I have cried to thee, O Lord: * Lord, hear my voice.

verses.lat: 129:2 Fiant aures tuæ intendéntes, * in vocem deprecatiónis meæ.
verses.eng: 129:2 Let thy ears be attentive * to the voice of my supplication.

verses.lat: 129:3 Si iniquitátes observáveris, Dómine: * Dómine, quis sustinébit?
verses.eng: 129:3 If thou, O Lord, wilt mark iniquities: * Lord, who shall stand it.

verses.lat: 129:4 Quia apud te propitiátio est: * et propter legem tuam sustínui te, Dómine.
verses.eng: 129:4 For with thee there is merciful forgiveness: * and by reason of thy law, I have waited for thee, O Lord.

verses.lat: 129:5 Sustínuit ánima mea in verbo ejus: * sperávit ánima mea in Dómino.
verses.eng: 129:5 My soul hath relied on his word: * my soul hath hoped in the Lord.

verses.lat: 129:6 A custódia matutína usque ad noctem: * speret Israël in Dómino.
verses.eng: 129:6 From the morning watch even until night, * let Israel hope in the Lord.

verses.lat: 129:7 Quia apud Dóminum misericórdia: * et copiósa apud eum redémptio.
verses.eng: 129:7 Because with the Lord there is mercy: * and with him plentiful redemption.

verses.lat: 129:8 Et ipse rédimet Israël, * ex ómnibus iniquitátibus ejus.
verses.eng: 129:8 And he shall redeem Israel * from all his iniquities.

vesperae.psalm4.label: Psalmus 130
vesperae.psalm4.antiphonLat: Dómine, * non est exaltátum cor meum.
vesperae.psalm4.antiphonEng: O Lord * my heart is not exalted.

verses.lat: 130:1 Dómine, non est exaltátum cor meum: * neque eláti sunt óculi mei.
verses.eng: 130:1 O Lord, my heart is not exalted: * nor are my eyes lofty.

verses.lat: 130:1 Neque ambulávi in magnis: * neque in mirabílibus super me.
verses.eng: 130:1 Neither have I walked in great matters, * nor in wonderful things above me.

verses.lat: 130:2 Si non humíliter sentiébam: * sed exaltávi ánimam meam:
verses.eng: 130:2 If I was not humbly minded, * but exalted my soul:

verses.lat: 130:2 Sicut ablactátus est super matre sua, * ita retribútio in ánima mea.
verses.eng: 130:2 As a child that is weaned is towards his mother, * so reward in my soul.

verses.lat: 130:3 Speret Israël in Dómino, * ex hoc nunc et usque in sǽculum.
verses.eng: 130:3 Let Israel hope in the Lord, * from henceforth now and for ever.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Blessed are all * they that fear the Lord.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Let them all be confounded * who hate Sion.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.lat: De profúndis * clamávi ad te, Dómine.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Out of the depths * I have cried to thee, O Lord.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Dómine, * non est exaltátum cor meum.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.eng: O Lord * my heart is not exalted.

vesperae.psalm5.label: Psalmus 131
vesperae.psalm5.antiphonLat: Elégit Dóminus * Sion in habitatiónem sibi.
vesperae.psalm5.antiphonEng: The Lord hath chosen * Sion for his dwelling.

verses.lat: 131:1 Meménto, Dómine, David, * et omnis mansuetúdinis ejus:
verses.eng: 131:1 Lord, remember David, * and all his meekness.

verses.lat: 131:2 Sicut jurávit Dómino, * votum vovit Deo Jacob:
verses.eng: 131:2 How he swore to the Lord, * he vowed a vow to the God of Jacob:

verses.lat: 131:3 Si introíero in tabernáculum domus meæ, * si ascéndero in lectum strati mei:
verses.eng: 131:3 If I shall enter into the tabernacle of my house: * if I shall go up into the bed wherein I lie:

verses.lat: 131:4 Si dédero somnum óculis meis, * et pálpebris meis dormitatiónem:
verses.eng: 131:4 If I shall give sleep to my eyes, * or slumber to my eyelids,

verses.lat: 131:5 Et réquiem tempóribus meis: donec invéniam locum Dómino, * tabernáculum Deo Jacob.
verses.eng: 131:5 Or rest to my temples: until I find out a place for the Lord, * a tabernacle for the God of Jacob.

verses.lat: 131:6 Ecce, audívimus eam in Éphrata: * invénimus eam in campis silvæ.
verses.eng: 131:6 Behold we have heard of it in Ephrata: * we have found it in the fields of the wood.

verses.lat: 131:7 Introíbimus in tabernáculum ejus: * adorábimus in loco, ubi stetérunt pedes ejus.
verses.eng: 131:7 We will go into his tabernacle: * we will adore in the place where his feet stood.

verses.lat: 131:8 Surge, Dómine, in réquiem tuam, * tu et arca sanctificatiónis tuæ.
verses.eng: 131:8 Arise, O Lord, into thy resting place: * thou and the ark, which thou hast sanctified.

verses.lat: 131:9 Sacerdótes tui induántur justítiam: * et sancti tui exsúltent.
verses.eng: 131:9 Let thy priests be clothed with justice: * and let thy saints rejoice.

verses.lat: 131:10 Propter David, servum tuum, * non avértas fáciem Christi tui.
verses.eng: 131:10 For thy servant David’s sake, * turn not away the face of thy anointed.

verses.lat: 131:11 Jurávit Dóminus David veritátem, et non frustrábitur eam: * De fructu ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam.
verses.eng: 131:11 The Lord hath sworn truth to David, and he will not make it void: * of the fruit of thy womb I will set upon thy throne.

verses.lat: 131:12 Si custodíerint fílii tui testaméntum meum, * et testimónia mea hæc, quæ docébo eos:
verses.eng: 131:12 If thy children will keep my covenant, * and these my testimonies which I shall teach them:

verses.lat: 131:12 Et fílii eórum usque in sǽculum, * sedébunt super sedem tuam.
verses.eng: 131:12 Their children also for evermore * shall sit upon thy throne.

verses.lat: 131:13 Quóniam elégit Dóminus Sion: * elégit eam in habitatiónem sibi.
verses.eng: 131:13 For the Lord hath chosen Sion: * he hath chosen it for his dwelling.

verses.lat: 131:14 Hæc réquies mea in sǽculum sǽculi: * hic habitábo quóniam elégi eam.
verses.eng: 131:14 This is my rest for ever and ever: * here will I dwell, for I have chosen it.

verses.lat: 131:15 Víduam ejus benedícens benedícam: * páuperes ejus saturábo pánibus.
verses.eng: 131:15 Blessing I will bless her widow: * I will satisfy her poor with bread.

verses.lat: 131:16 Sacerdótes ejus índuam salutári: * et sancti ejus exsultatióne exsultábunt.
verses.eng: 131:16 I will clothe her priests with salvation: * and her saints shall rejoice with exceeding great joy.

verses.lat: 131:17 Illuc prodúcam cornu David, * parávi lucérnam Christo meo.
verses.eng: 131:17 There will I bring forth a horn to David: * I have prepared a lamp for my anointed.

verses.lat: 131:18 Inimícos ejus índuam confusióne: * super ipsum autem efflorébit sanctificátio mea.
verses.eng: 131:18 His enemies I will clothe with confusion: * but upon him shall my sanctification flourish.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Elégit Dóminus * Sion in habitatiónem sibi.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.eng: The Lord hath chosen * Sion for his dwelling.

ant_prima.label: Antíphona
ant_prima.lat: Misericórdia tua, * Dómine, ante óculos meos: et complácui in veritáte tua.
ant_prima.eng: For thy mercy, * O Lord, is before my eyes; and I am well pleased with thy truth.

verses.lat: 25:1 Júdica me, Dómine, quóniam ego in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum: * et in Dómino sperans non infirmábor.
verses.eng: 25:1 Judge me, O Lord, for I have walked in my innocence: * and I have put my trust in the Lord, and shall not be weakened.

verses.lat: 25:2 Proba me, Dómine, et tenta me: * ure renes meos et cor meum.
verses.eng: 25:2 Prove me, O Lord, and try me; * burn my reins and my heart.

verses.lat: 25:3 Quóniam misericórdia tua ante óculos meos est: * et complácui in veritáte tua.
verses.eng: 25:3 For thy mercy is before my eyes; * and I am well pleased with thy truth.

verses.lat: 25:4 Non sedi cum concílio vanitátis: * et cum iníqua geréntibus non introíbo.
verses.eng: 25:4 I have not sat with the council of vanity: * neither will I go in with the doers of unjust things.

verses.lat: 25:5 Odívi ecclésiam malignántium: * et cum ímpiis non sedébo.
verses.eng: 25:5 I have hated the assembly of the malignant; * and with the wicked I will not sit.

verses.lat: 25:6 Lavábo inter innocéntes manus meas: * et circúmdabo altáre tuum, Dómine:
verses.eng: 25:6 I will wash my hands among the innocent; * and will compass thy altar, O Lord:

verses.lat: 25:7 Ut áudiam vocem laudis, * et enárrem univérsa mirabília tua.
verses.eng: 25:7 That I may hear the voice of thy praise: * and tell of all thy wondrous works.

verses.lat: 25:8 Dómine, diléxi decórem domus tuæ, * et locum habitatiónis glóriæ tuæ.
verses.eng: 25:8 I have loved, O Lord, the beauty of thy house; * and the place where thy glory dwelleth.

verses.lat: 25:9 Ne perdas cum ímpiis, Deus, ánimam meam, * et cum viris sánguinum vitam meam:
verses.eng: 25:9 Take not away my soul, O God, with the wicked: * nor my life with bloody men:

verses.lat: 25:10 In quorum mánibus iniquitátes sunt: * déxtera eórum repléta est munéribus.
verses.eng: 25:10 In whose hands are iniquities: * their right hand is filled with gifts.

verses.lat: 25:11 Ego autem in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum: * rédime me, et miserére mei.
verses.eng: 25:11 But as for me, I have walked in my innocence: * redeem me, and have mercy on me.

verses.lat: 25:12 Pes meus stetit in dirécto: * in ecclésiis benedícam te, Dómine.
verses.eng: 25:12 My foot hath stood in the direct way: * in the churches I will bless thee, O Lord.

verses.lat: 51:3 Quid gloriáris in malítia, * qui potens es in iniquitáte?
verses.eng: 51:3 Why dost thou glory in malice, * thou that art mighty in iniquity?

verses.lat: 51:4 Tota die injustítiam cogitávit lingua tua: * sicut novácula acúta fecísti dolum.
verses.eng: 51:4 All the day long thy tongue hath devised injustice: * as a sharp razor, thou hast wrought deceit.

verses.lat: 51:5 Dilexísti malítiam super benignitátem: * iniquitátem magis quam loqui æquitátem.
verses.eng: 51:5 Thou hast loved malice more than goodness: * and iniquity rather than to speak righteousness.

verses.lat: 51:6 Dilexísti ómnia verba præcipitatiónis, * lingua dolósa.
verses.eng: 51:6 Thou hast loved all the words of ruin, * O deceitful tongue.

verses.lat: 51:7 Proptérea Deus déstruet te in finem, * evéllet te, et emigrábit te de tabernáculo tuo: et radícem tuam de terra vivéntium.
verses.eng: 51:7 Therefore will God destroy thee for ever: * he will pluck thee out, and remove thee from thy dwelling place: and thy root out of the land of the living.

verses.lat: 51:8 Vidébunt justi, et timébunt, et super eum ridébunt, et dicent: * Ecce homo, qui non pósuit Deum adjutórem suum:
verses.eng: 51:8 The just shall see and fear, and shall laugh at him, and say: * Behold the man that made not God his helper:

verses.lat: 51:9 Sed sperávit in multitúdine divitiárum suárum: * et præváluit in vanitáte sua.
verses.eng: 51:9 But trusted in the abundance of his riches: * and prevailed in his vanity.

verses.lat: 51:10 Ego autem, sicut olíva fructífera in domo Dei, * sperávi in misericórdia Dei in ætérnum: et in sǽculum sǽculi.
verses.eng: 51:10 But I, as a fruitful olive tree in the house of God, * have hoped in the mercy of God for ever, yea for ever and ever.

verses.lat: 51:11 Confitébor tibi in sǽculum, quia fecísti: * et exspectábo nomen tuum, quóniam bonum est in conspéctu sanctórum tuórum.
verses.eng: 51:11 I will praise thee for ever, because thou hast done it: * and I will wait on thy name, for it is good in the sight of thy saints.

verses.lat: 52:1 Dixit insípiens in corde suo: * Non est Deus.
verses.eng: 52:1 The fool said in his heart: * There is no God.

verses.lat: 52:2 Corrúpti sunt, et abominábiles facti sunt in iniquitátibus: * non est qui fáciat bonum.
verses.eng: 52:2 They are corrupted, and become abominable in iniquities: * there is none that doth good.

verses.lat: 52:3 Deus de cælo prospéxit super fílios hóminum: * ut vídeat si est intéllegens, aut requírens Deum.
verses.eng: 52:3 God looked down from heaven on the children of men: * to see if there were any that did understand, or did seek God.

verses.lat: 52:4 Omnes declinavérunt, simul inútiles facti sunt: * non est qui fáciat bonum, non est usque ad unum.
verses.eng: 52:4 All have gone aside, they are become unprofitable together, * there is none that doth good, no not one.

verses.lat: 52:5 Nonne scient omnes qui operántur iniquitátem, * qui dévorant plebem meam ut cibum panis?
verses.eng: 52:5 Shall not all the workers of iniquity know, * who eat up my people as they eat bread?

verses.lat: 52:6 Deum non invocavérunt: * illic trepidavérunt timóre, ubi non erat timor.
verses.eng: 52:6 They have not called upon God: * there have they trembled for fear, where there was no fear.

verses.lat: 52:6 Quóniam Deus dissipávit ossa eórum qui homínibus placent: * confúsi sunt, quóniam Deus sprevit eos.
verses.eng: 52:6 For God hath scattered the bones of them that please men: * they have been confounded, because God hath despised them.

verses.lat: 52:7 Quis dabit ex Sion salutáre Israël? * cum convérterit Deus captivitátem plebis suæ, exsultábit Jacob, et lætábitur Israël.
verses.eng: 52:7 Who will give out of Sion the salvation of Israel? * when God shall bring back the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad.

ant_tertia.label: Antíphona
ant_tertia.lat: Deus ádjuvat me: * et Dóminus suscéptor est ánimæ meæ.
ant_tertia.eng: For behold God is my helper: * and the Lord is the protector of my soul.

verses.lat: 53:3 Deus, in nómine tuo salvum me fac: * et in virtúte tua júdica me.
verses.eng: 53:3 Save me, O God, by thy name, * and judge me in thy strength.

verses.lat: 53:4 Deus, exáudi oratiónem meam: * áuribus pércipe verba oris mei.
verses.eng: 53:4 O God, hear my prayer: * give ear to the words of my mouth.

verses.lat: 53:5 Quóniam aliéni insurrexérunt advérsum me, et fortes quæsiérunt ánimam meam: * et non proposuérunt Deum ante conspéctum suum.
verses.eng: 53:5 For strangers have risen up against me; and the mighty have sought after my soul: * and they have not set God before their eyes.

verses.lat: 53:6 Ecce enim, Deus ádjuvat me: * et Dóminus suscéptor est ánimæ meæ.
verses.eng: 53:6 For behold God is my helper: * and the Lord is the protector of my soul.

verses.lat: 53:7 Avérte mala inimícis meis: * et in veritáte tua dispérde illos.
verses.eng: 53:7 Turn back the evils upon my enemies; * and cut them off in thy truth.

verses.lat: 53:8 Voluntárie sacrificábo tibi, * et confitébor nómini tuo, Dómine: quóniam bonum est:
verses.eng: 53:8 I will freely sacrifice to thee, * and will give praise, O God, to thy name: because it is good:

verses.lat: 53:9 Quóniam ex omni tribulatióne eripuísti me: * et super inimícos meos despéxit óculus meus.
verses.eng: 53:9 For thou hast delivered me out of all trouble: * and my eye hath looked down upon my enemies.

verses.lat: 54:2 Exáudi, Deus, oratiónem meam, et ne despéxeris deprecatiónem meam: * inténde mihi, et exáudi me.
verses.eng: 54:2 Hear, O God, my prayer, and despise not my supplication: * be attentive to me and hear me.

verses.lat: 54:3 Contristátus sum in exercitatióne mea: * et conturbátus sum a voce inimíci, et a tribulatióne peccatóris.
verses.eng: 54:3 I am grieved in my exercise; * and am troubled, at the voice of the enemy, and at the tribulation of the sinner.

verses.lat: 54:4 Quóniam declinavérunt in me iniquitátes: * et in ira molésti erant mihi.
verses.eng: 54:4 For they have cast iniquities upon me; * and in wrath they were troublesome to me.

verses.lat: 54:5 Cor meum conturbátum est in me: * et formído mortis cécidit super me.
verses.eng: 54:5 My heart is troubled within me: * and the fear of death is fallen upon me.

verses.lat: 54:6 Timor et tremor venérunt super me: * et contexérunt me ténebræ.
verses.eng: 54:6 Fear and trembling are come upon me: * and darkness hath covered me.

verses.lat: 54:7 Et dixi: Quis dabit mihi pennas sicut colúmbæ, * et volábo, et requiéscam?
verses.eng: 54:7 And I said: Who will give me wings like a dove, * and I will fly and be at rest?

verses.lat: 54:8 Ecce, elongávi fúgiens: * et mansi in solitúdine.
verses.eng: 54:8 Lo, I have gone far off flying away; * and I abode in the wilderness.

verses.lat: 54:9 Exspectábam eum, qui salvum me fecit * a pusillanimitáte spíritus et tempestáte.
verses.eng: 54:9 I waited for him that hath saved me * from pusillanimity of spirit, and a storm.

verses.lat: 54:10 Præcípita, Dómine, dívide linguas eórum: * quóniam vidi iniquitátem, et contradictiónem in civitáte.
verses.eng: 54:10 Cast down, O Lord, and divide their tongues; * for I have seen iniquity and contradiction in the city.

verses.lat: 54:11 Die ac nocte circúmdabit eam super muros ejus iníquitas: * et labor in médio ejus, et injustítia.
verses.eng: 54:11 Day and night shall iniquity surround it upon its walls: * and in the midst thereof are labour, and injustice.

verses.lat: 54:12 Et non defécit de platéis ejus * usúra, et dolus.
verses.eng: 54:12 And usury and deceit * have not departed from its streets.

verses.lat: 54:13 Quóniam si inimícus meus maledixísset mihi, * sustinuíssem útique.
verses.eng: 54:13 For if my enemy had reviled me, * I would verily have borne with it.

verses.lat: 54:13 Et si is, qui óderat me, super me magna locútus fuísset, * abscondíssem me fórsitan ab eo.
verses.eng: 54:13 And if he that hated me had spoken great things against me, * I would perhaps have hidden myself from him.

verses.lat: 54:14 Tu vero, homo unánimis: * dux meus, et notus meus:
verses.eng: 54:14 But thou a man of one mind, * my guide, and my familiar.

verses.lat: 54:15 Qui simul mecum dulces capiébas cibos: * in domo Dei ambulávimus cum consénsu.
verses.eng: 54:15 Who didst take sweetmeats together with me: * in the house of God we walked with consent.

verses.lat: 54:16 Véniat mors super illos: * et descéndant in inférnum vivéntes:
verses.eng: 54:16 Let death come upon them, * and let them go down alive into hell.

verses.lat: 54:16 Quóniam nequítiæ in habitáculis eórum: * in médio eórum.
verses.eng: 54:16 For there is wickedness in their dwellings: * in the midst of them.

verses.lat: 54:17 Ego autem ad Deum clamávi: * et Dóminus salvábit me.
verses.eng: 54:17 But I have cried to God: * and the Lord will save me.

verses.lat: 54:18 Véspere, et mane, et merídie narrábo et annuntiábo: * et exáudiet vocem meam.
verses.eng: 54:18 Evening and morning, and at noon I will speak and declare: * and he shall hear my voice.

verses.lat: 54:19 Rédimet in pace ánimam meam ab his, qui appropínquant mihi: * quóniam inter multos erant mecum.
verses.eng: 54:19 He shall redeem my soul in peace from them that draw near to me: * for among many they were with me.

verses.lat: 54:20 Exáudiet Deus, et humiliábit illos, * qui est ante sǽcula.
verses.eng: 54:20 God shall hear, * and the Eternal shall humble them.

verses.lat: 54:20 Non enim est illis commutátio, et non timuérunt Deum: * exténdit manum suam in retribuéndo.
verses.eng: 54:20 For there is no change with them, and they have not feared God: * he hath stretched forth his hand to repay.

verses.lat: 54:21 Contaminavérunt testaméntum ejus, divísi sunt ab ira vultus ejus: * et appropinquávit cor illíus.
verses.eng: 54:21 They have defiled his covenant, they are divided by the wrath of his countenance, * and his heart hath drawn near.

verses.lat: 54:22 Mollíti sunt sermónes ejus super óleum: * et ipsi sunt jácula.
verses.eng: 54:22 His words are smoother than oil, * and the same are darts.

verses.lat: 54:23 Jacta super Dóminum curam tuam, et ipse te enútriet: * non dabit in ætérnum fluctuatiónem justo.
verses.eng: 54:23 Cast thy care upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee: * he shall not suffer the just to waver for ever.

verses.lat: 54:24 Tu vero, Deus, dedúces eos, * in púteum intéritus.
verses.eng: 54:24 But thou, O God, shalt bring them down * into the pit of destruction.

verses.lat: 54:24 Viri sánguinum, et dolósi non dimidiábunt dies suos: * ego autem sperábo in te, Dómine.
verses.eng: 54:24 Bloody and deceitful men shall not live out half their days; * but I will trust in thee, O Lord.

ant_sexta.label: Antíphona
ant_sexta.lat: In Deo sperávi * non timébo quid fáciat mihi homo.
ant_sexta.eng: In God I have put my trust * I will not fear what flesh can do against me.

verses.lat: 55:2 Miserére mei, Deus, quóniam conculcávit me homo: * tota die impúgnans tribulávit me.
verses.eng: 55:2 Have mercy on me, O God, for man hath trodden me under foot; * all the day long he hath afflicted me fighting against me.

verses.lat: 55:3 Conculcavérunt me inimíci mei tota die: * quóniam multi bellántes advérsum me.
verses.eng: 55:3 My enemies have trodden on me all the day long; * for they are many that make war against me.

verses.lat: 55:4 Ab altitúdine diéi timébo: * ego vero in te sperábo.
verses.eng: 55:4 From the height of the day I shall fear: * but I will trust in thee.

verses.lat: 55:5 In Deo laudábo sermónes meos, in Deo sperávi: * non timébo quid fáciat mihi caro.
verses.eng: 55:5 In God I will praise my words, in God I have put my trust: * I will not fear what flesh can do against me.

verses.lat: 55:6 Tota die verba mea exsecrabántur: * advérsum me omnes cogitatiónes eórum in malum.
verses.eng: 55:6 All the day long they detested my words: * all their thoughts were against me unto evil.

verses.lat: 55:7 Inhabitábunt et abscóndent: * ipsi calcáneum meum observábunt.
verses.eng: 55:7 They will dwell and hide themselves: * they will watch my heel.

verses.lat: 55:8 Sicut sustinuérunt ánimam meam, pro níhilo salvos fácies illos: * in ira pópulos confrínges.
verses.eng: 55:8 As they have waited for my soul, for nothing shalt thou save them: * in thy anger thou shalt break the people in pieces.

verses.lat: 55:9 Deus, vitam meam annuntiávi tibi: * posuísti lácrimas meas in conspéctu tuo.
verses.eng: 55:9 O God, I have declared to thee my life: * thou hast set my tears in thy sight,

verses.lat: 55:9 Sicut et in promissióne tua: * tunc converténtur inimíci mei retrórsum:
verses.eng: 55:9 As also in thy promise. * Then shall my enemies be turned back.

verses.lat: 55:10 In quacúmque die invocávero te: * ecce, cognóvi, quóniam Deus meus es.
verses.eng: 55:10 In what day soever I shall call upon thee, * behold I know thou art my God.

verses.lat: 55:11 In Deo laudábo verbum, in Dómino laudábo sermónem: * in Deo sperávi, non timébo quid fáciat mihi homo.
verses.eng: 55:11 In God will I praise the word, in the Lord will I praise his speech. * In God have I hoped, I will not fear what man can do to me.

verses.lat: 55:12 In me sunt, Deus, vota tua, * quæ reddam, laudatiónes tibi.
verses.eng: 55:12 In me, O God, are vows to thee, * which I will pay, praises to thee:

verses.lat: 55:13 Quóniam eripuísti ánimam meam de morte, et pedes meos de lapsu: * ut pláceam coram Deo in lúmine vivéntium.
verses.eng: 55:13 Because thou hast delivered my soul from death, my feet from falling: * that I may please in the sight of God, in the light of the living.

verses.lat: 56:2 Miserére mei, Deus, miserére mei: * quóniam in te confídit ánima mea.
verses.eng: 56:2 Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me: * for my soul trusteth in thee.

verses.lat: 56:2 Et in umbra alárum tuárum sperábo, * donec tránseat iníquitas.
verses.eng: 56:2 And in the shadow of thy wings will I hope, * until iniquity pass away.

verses.lat: 56:3 Clamábo ad Deum altíssimum: * Deum qui benefécit mihi.
verses.eng: 56:3 I will cry to God the most High; * to God who hath done good to me.

verses.lat: 56:4 Misit de cælo, et liberávit me: * dedit in oppróbrium conculcántes me.
verses.eng: 56:4 He hath sent from heaven and delivered me: * he hath made them a reproach that trod upon me.

verses.lat: 56:4 Misit Deus misericórdiam suam, et veritátem suam, * et erípuit ánimam meam de médio catulórum leónum: dormívi conturbátus.
verses.eng: 56:4 God hath sent his mercy and his truth, * and he hath delivered my soul from the midst of the young lions. I slept troubled.

verses.lat: 56:5 Fílii hóminum dentes eórum arma et sagíttæ: * et lingua eórum gládius acútus.
verses.eng: 56:5 The sons of men, whose teeth are weapons and arrows, * and their tongue a sharp sword.

verses.lat: 56:6 Exaltáre super cælos, Deus, * et in omnem terram glória tua.
verses.eng: 56:6 Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens, * and thy glory above all the earth.

verses.lat: 56:7 Láqueum paravérunt pédibus meis: * et incurvavérunt ánimam meam.
verses.eng: 56:7 They prepared a snare for my feet; * and they bowed down my soul.

verses.lat: 56:7 Fodérunt ante fáciem meam fóveam: * et incidérunt in eam.
verses.eng: 56:7 They dug a pit before my face, * and they are fallen into it.

verses.lat: 56:8 Parátum cor meum, Deus, parátum cor meum: * cantábo, et psalmum dicam.
verses.eng: 56:8 My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready: * I will sing, and rehearse a psalm.

verses.lat: 56:9 Exsúrge, glória mea, exsúrge, psaltérium et cíthara: * exsúrgam dilúculo.
verses.eng: 56:9 Arise, O my glory, arise psaltery and harp: * I will arise early.

verses.lat: 56:10 Confitébor tibi in pópulis, Dómine: * et psalmum dicam tibi in géntibus:
verses.eng: 56:10 I will give praise to thee, O Lord, among the people: * I will sing a psalm to thee among the nations.

verses.lat: 56:11 Quóniam magnificáta est usque ad cælos misericórdia tua, * et usque ad nubes véritas tua.
verses.eng: 56:11 For thy mercy is magnified even to the heavens: * and thy truth unto the clouds.

verses.lat: 56:12 Exaltáre super cælos, Deus: * et super omnem terram glória tua.
verses.eng: 56:12 Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens: * and thy glory above all the earth.

verses.lat: 57:2 Si vere útique justítiam loquímini: * recta judicáte, fílii hóminum.
verses.eng: 57:2 If in very deed you speak justice: * judge right things, ye sons of men.

verses.lat: 57:3 Étenim in corde iniquitátes operámini: * in terra injustítias manus vestræ concínnant.
verses.eng: 57:3 For in your heart you work iniquity: * your hands forge injustice in the earth.

verses.lat: 57:4 Alienáti sunt peccatóres a vulva, erravérunt ab útero: * locúti sunt falsa.
verses.eng: 57:4 The wicked are alienated from the womb; they have gone astray from the womb: * they have spoken false things.

verses.lat: 57:5 Furor illis secúndum similitúdinem serpéntis: * sicut áspidis surdæ, et obturántis aures suas,
verses.eng: 57:5 Their madness is according to the likeness of a serpent: * like the deaf asp that stoppeth her ears:

verses.lat: 57:6 Quæ non exáudiet vocem incantántium: * et venéfici incantántis sapiénter.
verses.eng: 57:6 Which will not hear the voice of the charmers; * nor of the wizard that charmeth wisely.

verses.lat: 57:7 Deus cónteret dentes eórum in ore ipsórum: * molas leónum confrínget Dóminus.
verses.eng: 57:7 God shall break in pieces their teeth in their mouth: * the Lord shall break the grinders of the lions.

verses.lat: 57:8 Ad níhilum devénient tamquam aqua decúrrens: * inténdit arcum suum donec infirméntur.
verses.eng: 57:8 They shall come to nothing, like water running down; * he hath bent his bow till they be weakened.

verses.lat: 57:9 Sicut cera, quæ fluit, auferéntur: * supercécidit ignis, et non vidérunt solem.
verses.eng: 57:9 Like wax that melteth they shall be taken away: * fire hath fallen on them, and they shall not see the sun.

verses.lat: 57:10 Priúsquam intellégerent spinæ vestræ rhamnum: * sicut vivéntes, sic in ira absórbet eos.
verses.eng: 57:10 Before your thorns could know the brier; he swalloweth them up, * as alive, in his wrath.

verses.lat: 57:11 Lætábitur justus cum víderit vindíctam: * manus suas lavábit in sánguine peccatóris.
verses.eng: 57:11 The just shall rejoice when he shall see the revenge: * he shall wash his hands in the blood of the sinner.

verses.lat: 57:12 Et dicet homo: Si útique est fructus justo: * útique est Deus júdicans eos in terra.
verses.eng: 57:12 And man shall say: If indeed there be fruit to the just: * there is indeed a God that judgeth them on the earth.

ant_nona.label: Antíphona
ant_nona.lat: Deus meus * misericórdia tua prævéniet me.
ant_nona.eng: My God, * his mercy shall prevent me.

verses.lat: 58:2 Éripe me de inimícis meis, Deus meus: * et ab insurgéntibus in me líbera me.
verses.eng: 58:2 Deliver me from my enemies, O my God; * and defend me from them that rise up against me.

verses.lat: 58:3 Éripe me de operántibus iniquitátem: * et de viris sánguinum salva me.
verses.eng: 58:3 Deliver me from them that work iniquity, * and save me from bloody men.

verses.lat: 58:4 Quia ecce cepérunt ánimam meam: * irruérunt in me fortes.
verses.eng: 58:4 For behold they have caught my soul: * the mighty have rushed in upon me:

verses.lat: 58:5 Neque iníquitas mea, neque peccátum meum, Dómine: * sine iniquitáte cucúrri, et diréxi.
verses.eng: 58:5 Neither is it my iniquity, nor my sin, O Lord: * without iniquity have I run, and directed my steps.

verses.lat: 58:6 Exsúrge in occúrsum meum, et vide: * et tu, Dómine, Deus virtútum, Deus Israël,
verses.eng: 58:6 Rise up thou to meet me, and behold: * even thou, O Lord, the God of hosts, the God of Israel.

verses.lat: 58:6 Inténde ad visitándas omnes gentes: * non misereáris ómnibus, qui operántur iniquitátem.
verses.eng: 58:6 Attend to visit all the nations: * have no mercy on all them that work iniquity.

verses.lat: 58:7 Converténtur ad vésperam: et famem patiéntur ut canes, * et circuíbunt civitátem.
verses.eng: 58:7 They shall return at evening, and shall suffer hunger like dogs: * and shall go round about the city.

verses.lat: 58:8 Ecce, loquéntur in ore suo, et gládius in lábiis eórum: * quóniam quis audívit?
verses.eng: 58:8 Behold they shall speak with their mouth, and a sword is in their lips: * for who, say they, hath heard us?

verses.lat: 58:9 Et tu, Dómine, deridébis eos: * ad níhilum dedúces omnes gentes.
verses.eng: 58:9 But thou, O Lord, shalt laugh at them: * thou shalt bring all the nations to nothing.

verses.lat: 58:10 Fortitúdinem meam ad te custódiam, quia, Deus, suscéptor meus es: * Deus meus, misericórdia ejus prævéniet me.
verses.eng: 58:10 I will keep my strength to thee: for thou art my protector: * my God, his mercy shall prevent me.

verses.lat: 58:12 Deus osténdet mihi super inimícos meos, ne occídas eos: * nequándo obliviscántur pópuli mei.
verses.eng: 58:12 God shall let me see over my enemies: slay them not, * lest at any time my people forget.

verses.lat: 58:12 Dispérge illos in virtúte tua: * et depóne eos, protéctor meus, Dómine:
verses.eng: 58:12 And scatter them by thy power; * and bring them down, O Lord, my protector:

verses.lat: 58:13 Delíctum oris eórum, sermónem labiórum ipsórum: * et comprehendántur in supérbia sua.
verses.eng: 58:13 For the sin of their mouth, and the word of their lips: * and let them be taken in their pride.

verses.lat: 58:13 Et de exsecratióne et mendácio annuntiabúntur in consummatióne: * in ira consummatiónis, et non erunt.
verses.eng: 58:13 And for their cursing and lying they shall be talked of, when they are consumed: * when they are consumed by thy wrath, and they shall be no more.

verses.lat: 58:14 Et scient quia Deus dominábitur Jacob: * et fínium terræ.
verses.eng: 58:14 And they shall know that God will rule Jacob, * and all the ends of the earth.

verses.lat: 58:15 Converténtur ad vésperam: et famem patiéntur ut canes, * et circuíbunt civitátem.
verses.eng: 58:15 They shall return at evening and shall suffer hunger like dogs: * and shall go round about the city.

verses.lat: 58:16 Ipsi dispergéntur ad manducándum: * si vero non fúerint saturáti, et murmurábunt.
verses.eng: 58:16 They shall be scattered abroad to eat, * and shall murmur if they be not filled.

verses.lat: 58:17 Ego autem cantábo fortitúdinem tuam: * et exsultábo mane misericórdiam tuam.
verses.eng: 58:17 But I will sing thy strength: * and will extol thy mercy in the morning.

verses.lat: 58:17 Quia factus es suscéptor meus, * et refúgium meum, in die tribulatiónis meæ.
verses.eng: 58:17 For thou art become my support, * and my refuge, in the day of my trouble.

verses.lat: 58:18 Adjútor meus, tibi psallam, quia, Deus, suscéptor meus es: * Deus meus, misericórdia mea.
verses.eng: 58:18 Unto thee, O my helper, will I sing, for thou art God my defence: * my God my mercy.

verses.lat: 59:3 Deus, repulísti nos, et destruxísti nos: * irátus es, et misértus es nobis.
verses.eng: 59:3 God, thou hast cast us off, and hast destroyed us; * thou hast been angry, and hast had mercy on us.

verses.lat: 59:4 Commovísti terram, et conturbásti eam: * sana contritiónes ejus, quia commóta est.
verses.eng: 59:4 Thou hast moved the earth, and hast troubled it: * heal thou the breaches thereof, for it has been moved.

verses.lat: 59:5 Ostendísti pópulo tuo dura: * potásti nos vino compunctiónis.
verses.eng: 59:5 Thou hast shewn thy people hard things; * thou hast made us drink the wine of sorrow.

verses.lat: 59:6 Dedísti metuéntibus te significatiónem: * ut fúgiant a fácie arcus:
verses.eng: 59:6 Thou hast given a warning to them that fear thee: * that they may flee from before the bow:

verses.lat: 59:7 Ut liberéntur dilécti tui: * salvum fac déxtera tua, et exáudi me.
verses.eng: 59:7 That thy beloved may be delivered. * Save me with thy right hand, and hear me.

verses.lat: 59:8 Deus locútus est in sancto suo: * lætábor, et partíbor Síchimam: et convállem tabernaculórum metíbor.
verses.eng: 59:8 God hath spoken in his holy place: * I will rejoice, and I will divide Sichem; and will mete out the vale of tabernacles.

verses.lat: 59:9 Meus est Gálaad, et meus est Manásses: * et Éphraim fortitúdo cápitis mei.
verses.eng: 59:9 Galaad is mine, and Manasses is mine: * and Ephraim is the strength of my head.

verses.lat: 59:9 Juda rex meus: * Moab olla spei meæ.
verses.eng: 59:9 Juda is my king: * Moab is the pot of my hope.

verses.lat: 59:10 In Idumǽam exténdam calceaméntum meum: * mihi alienígenæ súbditi sunt.
verses.eng: 59:10 Into Edom will I stretch out my shoe: * to me the foreigners are made subject.

verses.lat: 59:11 Quis dedúcet me in civitátem munítam? * quis dedúcet me usque in Idumǽam?
verses.eng: 59:11 Who will bring me into the strong city? * who will lead me into Edom?

verses.lat: 59:12 Nonne tu, Deus, qui repulísti nos? * et non egrediéris, Deus, in virtútibus nostris?
verses.eng: 59:12 Wilt not thou, O God, who hast cast us off? * and wilt not thou, O God, go out with our armies?

verses.lat: 59:13 Da nobis auxílium de tribulatióne: * quia vana salus hóminis.
verses.eng: 59:13 Give us help from trouble: * for vain is the salvation of man.

verses.lat: 59:14 In Deo faciémus virtútem: * et ipse ad níhilum dedúcet tribulántes nos.
verses.eng: 59:14 Through God we shall do mightily: * and he shall bring to nothing them that afflict us.

completorium.antiphon.label: Antíphona
completorium.antiphon.lat: Immíttet Ángelus Dómini * in circúitu timéntium eum: et erípiet eos.
completorium.antiphon.eng: The angel of the Lord * shall encamp round about them that fear him: and shall deliver them.

verses.lat: 33:2 Benedícam Dóminum in omni témpore: * semper laus ejus in ore meo.
verses.eng: 33:2 I will bless the Lord at all times, * his praise shall be always in my mouth.

verses.lat: 33:3 In Dómino laudábitur ánima mea: * áudiant mansuéti, et læténtur.
verses.eng: 33:3 In the Lord shall my soul be praised: * let the meek hear and rejoice.

verses.lat: 33:4 Magnificáte Dóminum mecum: * et exaltémus nomen ejus in idípsum.
verses.eng: 33:4 O magnify the Lord with me; * and let us extol his name together.

verses.lat: 33:5 Exquisívi Dóminum, et exaudívit me: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus meis erípuit me.
verses.eng: 33:5 I sought the Lord, and he heard me; * and he delivered me from all my troubles.

verses.lat: 33:6 Accédite ad eum, et illuminámini: * et fácies vestræ non confundéntur.
verses.eng: 33:6 Come ye to him and be enlightened: * and your faces shall not be confounded.

verses.lat: 33:7 Iste pauper clamávit, et Dóminus exaudívit eum: * et de ómnibus tribulatiónibus ejus salvávit eum.
verses.eng: 33:7 This poor man cried, and the Lord heard him: * and saved him out of all his troubles.

verses.lat: 33:8 Immíttet Ángelus Dómini in circúitu timéntium eum: * et erípiet eos.
verses.eng: 33:8 The Angel of the Lord shall encamp round about them that fear him: * and shall deliver them.

verses.lat: 33:9 Gustáte, et vidéte quóniam suávis est Dóminus: * beátus vir, qui sperat in eo.
verses.eng: 33:9 O taste, and see that the Lord is sweet: * blessed is the man that hopeth in him.

verses.lat: 33:10 Timéte Dóminum, omnes sancti ejus: * quóniam non est inópia timéntibus eum.
verses.eng: 33:10 Fear the Lord, all ye his saints: * for there is no want to them that fear him.

verses.lat: 33:11 Dívites eguérunt et esuriérunt: * inquiréntes autem Dóminum non minuéntur omni bono.
verses.eng: 33:11 The rich have wanted, and have suffered hunger: * but they that seek the Lord shall not be deprived of any good.

verses.lat: 33:12 Veníte, fílii, audíte me: * timórem Dómini docébo vos.
verses.eng: 33:12 Come, children, hearken to me: * I will teach you the fear of the Lord.

verses.lat: 33:13 Quis est homo qui vult vitam: * díligit dies vidére bonos?
verses.eng: 33:13 Who is the man that desireth life: * who loveth to see good days?

verses.lat: 33:14 Próhibe linguam tuam a malo: * et lábia tua ne loquántur dolum.
verses.eng: 33:14 Keep thy tongue from evil, * and thy lips from speaking guile.

verses.lat: 33:15 Divérte a malo, et fac bonum: * inquíre pacem, et perséquere eam.
verses.eng: 33:15 Turn away from evil and do good: * seek after peace and pursue it.

verses.lat: 33:16 Óculi Dómini super justos: * et aures ejus in preces eórum.
verses.eng: 33:16 The eyes of the Lord are upon the just: * and his ears unto their prayers.

verses.lat: 33:17 Vultus autem Dómini super faciéntes mala: * ut perdat de terra memóriam eórum.
verses.eng: 33:17 But the countenance of the Lord is against them that do evil things: * to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth.

verses.lat: 33:18 Clamavérunt justi, et Dóminus exaudívit eos: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus eórum liberávit eos.
verses.eng: 33:18 The just cried, and the Lord heard them: * and delivered them out of all their troubles.

verses.lat: 33:19 Juxta est Dóminus iis, qui tribuláto sunt corde: * et húmiles spíritu salvábit.
verses.eng: 33:19 The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a contrite heart: * and he will save the humble of spirit.

verses.lat: 33:20 Multæ tribulatiónes justórum: * et de ómnibus his liberábit eos Dóminus.
verses.eng: 33:20 Many are the afflictions of the just; * but out of them all will the Lord deliver them.

verses.lat: 33:21 Custódit Dóminus ómnia ossa eórum: * unum ex his non conterétur.
verses.eng: 33:21 The Lord keepeth all their bones, * not one of them shall be broken.

verses.lat: 33:22 Mors peccatórum péssima: * et qui odérunt justum, delínquent.
verses.eng: 33:22 The death of the wicked is very evil: * and they that hate the just shall be guilty.

verses.lat: 33:23 Rédimet Dóminus ánimas servórum suórum: * et non delínquent omnes qui sperant in eo.
verses.eng: 33:23 The Lord will redeem the souls of his servants: * and none of them that trust in him shall offend.

verses.lat: 60:2 Exáudi, Deus, deprecatiónem meam: * inténde oratióni meæ.
verses.eng: 60:2 Hear, O God, my supplication: * be attentive to my prayer.

verses.lat: 60:3 A fínibus terræ ad te clamávi: * dum anxiarétur cor meum, in petra exaltásti me.
verses.eng: 60:3 To thee have I cried from the ends of the earth: * when my heart was in anguish, thou hast exalted me on a rock.

verses.lat: 60:4 Deduxísti me, quia factus es spes mea: * turris fortitúdinis a fácie inimíci.
verses.eng: 60:4 Thou hast conducted me; for thou hast been my hope: * a tower of strength against the face of the enemy.
