verses.lat: 60:5 Inhabitábo in tabernáculo tuo in sǽcula: * prótegar in velaménto alárum tuárum.
verses.eng: 60:5 In thy tabernacle I shall dwell for ever: * I shall be protected under the covert of thy wings.

verses.lat: 60:6 Quóniam tu, Deus meus, exaudísti oratiónem meam: * dedísti hereditátem timéntibus nomen tuum.
verses.eng: 60:6 For thou, my God, hast heard my prayer: * thou hast given an inheritance to them that fear thy name.

verses.lat: 60:7 Dies super dies regis adícies: * annos ejus usque in diem generatiónis et generatiónis.
verses.eng: 60:7 Thou wilt add days to the days of the king: * his years even to generation and generation.

verses.lat: 60:8 Pérmanet in ætérnum in conspéctu Dei: * misericórdiam et veritátem ejus quis requíret?
verses.eng: 60:8 He abideth for ever in the sight of God: * his mercy and truth who shall search?

verses.lat: 60:9 Sic psalmum dicam nómini tuo in sǽculum sǽculi: * ut reddam vota mea de die in diem.
verses.eng: 60:9 So will I sing a psalm to thy name for ever and ever: * that I may pay my vows from day to day.

tertia.capitulum.label: Capitulum
tertia.capitulum.lat: Sana me, Dómine, et sanábor: salvum me fac, et salvus ero: quóniam laus mea tu es.
tertia.capitulum.eng: Heal me, O Lord, and I shall be healed: save me, and I shall be saved, for Thou art my praise.

responsory_breve_tertia.label: Responsory
responsory_breve_tertia.lat:
℟.br. Sana ánimam meam, * quia peccávi tibi.
℣. Ego dixi: Dómine, miserére mei.
℟. Quia peccávi tibi.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Sana ánimam meam, * quia peccávi tibi.
responsory_breve_tertia.eng:
℟.br. Heal my soul, * for I have sinned against Thee.
℣. I said: O Lord, be Thou merciful to me.
℟. For I have sinned against Thee.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. Heal my soul, * for I have sinned against Thee.

capitulum_sexta.label: Capitulum
capitulum_sexta.lat: Némini quidquam debeátis, nisi ut ínvicem diligátis: qui enim díligit próximum, legem implévit.
capitulum_sexta.eng: Owe no man any thing, but to love one another. For he that loveth his neighbour, hath fulfilled the law.

responsory_breve_sexta.label: Responsory
responsory_breve_sexta.lat:
℟.br. Benedícam Dóminum * in omni témpore.
℣. Semper laus ejus in ore meo.
℟. In omni témpore.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Benedícam Dóminum * in omni témpore.
responsory_breve_sexta.eng:
℟.br. I will bless the Lord * at all times.
℣. His praise shall be always in my mouth.
℟. At all times.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. I will bless the Lord * at all times.

capitulum_nona.label: Capitulum
capitulum_nona.lat: In timóre incolátus vestri témpore conversámini: sciéntes quod non corruptibílibus auro vel argénto redémpti estis, sed pretióso sánguine quasi Agni immaculáti Christi.
capitulum_nona.eng: Converse in fear during the time of your sojourning here. Knowing that you were not redeemed with corruptible things as gold or silver, but with the precious blood of Christ.

responsory_breve_nona.label: Responsory
responsory_breve_nona.lat:
℟.br. Rédime me, Dómine, * et miserére mei.
℣. Pes enim meus stetit in via recta.
℟. Et miserére mei.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Rédime me, Dómine, * et miserére mei.
responsory_breve_nona.eng:
℟.br. Redeem me, O Lord, * and have mercy on me.
℣. For my feet stood in the right way.
℟. And have mercy on me.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. Redeem me, O Lord, * and have mercy on me.

laudes.psalm1.label: Psalmus 96
laudes.psalm1.antiphonEng: The Lord hath reigned * let the earth rejoice.

verses.lat: 96:1 Dóminus regnávit, exsúltet terra: * læténtur ínsulæ multæ.
verses.eng: 96:1 The Lord hath reigned, let the earth rejoice: * let many islands be glad.

verses.lat: 96:2 Nubes, et calígo in circúitu ejus: * justítia, et judícium corréctio sedis ejus.
verses.eng: 96:2 Clouds and darkness are round about him: * justice and judgment are the establishment of his throne.

verses.lat: 96:3 Ignis ante ipsum præcédet, * et inflammábit in circúitu inimícos ejus.
verses.eng: 96:3 A fire shall go before him, * and shall burn his enemies round about.

verses.lat: 96:4 Illuxérunt fúlgura ejus orbi terræ: * vidit, et commóta est terra.
verses.eng: 96:4 His lightnings have shone forth to the world: * the earth saw and trembled.

verses.lat: 96:5 Montes, sicut cera fluxérunt a fácie Dómini: * a fácie Dómini omnis terra.
verses.eng: 96:5 The mountains melted like wax, at the presence of the Lord: * at the presence of the Lord of all the earth.

verses.lat: 96:6 Annuntiavérunt cæli justítiam ejus: * et vidérunt omnes pópuli glóriam ejus.
verses.eng: 96:6 The heavens declared his justice: * and all people saw his glory.

verses.lat: 96:7 Confundántur omnes, qui adórant sculptília: * et qui gloriántur in simulácris suis.
verses.eng: 96:7 Let them be all confounded that adore graven things, * and that glory in their idols.

verses.lat: 96:7 Adoráte eum, omnes Ángeli ejus: * audívit, et lætáta est Sion.
verses.eng: 96:7 Adore him, all you his angels: * Sion heard, and was glad.

verses.lat: 96:8 Et exsultavérunt fíliæ Judæ, * propter judícia tua, Dómine:
verses.eng: 96:8 And the daughters of Juda rejoiced, * because of thy judgments, O Lord.

verses.lat: 96:9 Quóniam tu Dóminus Altíssimus super omnem terram: * nimis exaltátus es super omnes deos.
verses.eng: 96:9 For thou art the most high Lord over all the earth: * thou art exalted exceedingly above all gods.

verses.lat: 96:10 Qui dilígitis Dóminum, odíte malum: * custódit Dóminus ánimas sanctórum suórum, de manu peccatóris liberábit eos.
verses.eng: 96:10 You that love the Lord, hate evil: * the Lord preserveth the souls of his saints, he will deliver them out of the hand of the sinner.

verses.lat: 96:11 Lux orta est justo, * et rectis corde lætítia.
verses.eng: 96:11 Light is risen to the just, * and joy to the right of heart.

verses.lat: 96:12 Lætámini, justi, in Dómino: * et confitémini memóriæ sanctificatiónis ejus.
verses.eng: 96:12 Rejoice, ye just, in the Lord: * and give praise to the remembrance of his holiness.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: The Lord hath reigned * let the earth rejoice.

laudes.psalm2.label: Psalmus 64
laudes.psalm2.antiphonLat: Te decet hymnus, * Deus, in Sion.
laudes.psalm2.antiphonEng: A hymn, O God, * becometh thee in Sion.

verses.lat: 64:2 Te decet hymnus, Deus, in Sion: * et tibi reddétur votum in Jerúsalem.
verses.eng: 64:2 A hymn, O God, becometh thee in Sion: * and a vow shall be paid to thee in Jerusalem.

verses.lat: 64:3 Exáudi oratiónem meam: * ad te omnis caro véniet.
verses.eng: 64:3 O hear my prayer: * all flesh shall come to thee.

verses.lat: 64:4 Verba iniquórum prævaluérunt super nos: * et impietátibus nostris tu propitiáberis.
verses.eng: 64:4 The words of the wicked have prevailed over us: * and thou wilt pardon our transgressions.

verses.lat: 64:5 Beátus, quem elegísti, et assumpsísti: * inhabitábit in átriis tuis.
verses.eng: 64:5 Blessed is he whom thou hast chosen and taken to thee: * he shall dwell in thy courts.

verses.lat: 64:5 Replébimur in bonis domus tuæ: * sanctum est templum tuum, mirábile in æquitáte.
verses.eng: 64:5 We shall be filled with the good things of thy house; holy is thy temple, * wonderful in justice.

verses.lat: 64:6 Exáudi nos, Deus, salutáris noster, * spes ómnium fínium terræ, et in mari longe.
verses.eng: 64:6 Hear us, O God our saviour, * who art the hope of all the ends of the earth, and in the sea afar off.

verses.lat: 64:7 Prǽparans montes in virtúte tua, accínctus poténtia: * qui contúrbas profúndum maris sonum flúctuum ejus.
verses.eng: 64:7 Thou who preparest the mountains by thy strength, being girded with power: * who troublest the depth of the sea, the noise of its waves.

verses.lat: 64:8 Turbabúntur gentes, et timébunt qui hábitant términos a signis tuis: * éxitus matutíni, et véspere delectábis.
verses.eng: 64:8 The Gentiles shall be troubled, and they that dwell in the uttermost borders shall be afraid at thy signs: * thou shalt make the outgoings of the morning and of the evening to be joyful.

verses.lat: 64:10 Visitásti terram, et inebriásti eam: * multiplicásti locupletáre eam.
verses.eng: 64:10 Thou hast visited the earth, and hast plentifully watered it; * thou hast many ways enriched it.

verses.lat: 64:10 Flumen Dei replétum est aquis, parásti cibum illórum: * quóniam ita est præparátio ejus.
verses.eng: 64:10 The river of God is filled with water, thou hast prepared their food; * for so is its preparation.

verses.lat: 64:11 Rivos ejus inébria, multíplica genímina ejus: * in stillicídiis ejus lætábitur gérminans.
verses.eng: 64:11 Fill up plentifully the streams thereof, multiply its fruits; * it shall spring up and rejoice in its showers.

verses.lat: 64:12 Benedíces corónæ anni benignitátis tuæ: * et campi tui replebúntur ubertáte.
verses.eng: 64:12 Thou shalt bless the crown of the year of thy goodness: * and thy fields shall be filled with plenty.

verses.lat: 64:13 Pinguéscent speciósa desérti: * et exsultatióne colles accingéntur.
verses.eng: 64:13 The beautiful places of the wilderness shall grow fat: * and the hills shall be girded about with joy.

verses.lat: 64:14 Indúti sunt aríetes óvium, et valles abundábunt fruménto: * clamábunt, étenim hymnum dicent.
verses.eng: 64:14 The rams of the flock are clothed, and the vales shall abound with corn: * they shall shout, yea they shall sing a hymn.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Te decet hymnus, * Deus, in Sion.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: A hymn, O God, * becometh thee in Sion.

laudes.psalm3.label: Psalmus 100
laudes.psalm3.antiphonLat: Tibi, Dómine, psallam, * et intéllegam in via immaculáta.
laudes.psalm3.antiphonEng: I shall sing to thee, O Lord * and I shall understand with a perfect heart.

verses.lat: 100:1 Misericórdiam, et judícium * cantábo tibi, Dómine:
verses.eng: 100:1 Mercy and judgment * I will sing to thee, O Lord:

verses.lat: 100:2 Psallam, et intéllegam in via immaculáta, * quando vénies ad me.
verses.eng: 100:2 I will sing, and I will understand in the unspotted way, * when thou shalt come to me.

verses.lat: 100:2 Perambulábam in innocéntia cordis mei, * in médio domus meæ.
verses.eng: 100:2 I walked in the innocence of my heart, * in the midst of my house.

verses.lat: 100:3 Non proponébam ante óculos meos rem injústam: * faciéntes prævaricatiónes odívi.
verses.eng: 100:3 I did not set before my eyes any unjust thing: * I hated the workers of iniquities.

verses.lat: 100:4 Non adhǽsit mihi cor pravum: * declinántem a me malígnum non cognoscébam.
verses.eng: 100:4 The perverse heart did not cleave to me: * and the malignant, that turned aside from me, I would not know.

verses.lat: 100:5 Detrahéntem secréto próximo suo, * hunc persequébar.
verses.eng: 100:5 The man that in private detracted his neighbour, * him did I persecute.

verses.lat: 100:5 Supérbo óculo, et insatiábili corde, * cum hoc non edébam.
verses.eng: 100:5 With him that had a proud eye, and an unsatiable heart, * I would not eat.

verses.lat: 100:6 Óculi mei ad fidéles terræ ut sédeant mecum: * ámbulans in via immaculáta, hic mihi ministrábat.
verses.eng: 100:6 My eyes were upon the faithful of the earth, to sit with me: * the man that walked in the perfect way, he served me.

verses.lat: 100:7 Non habitábit in médio domus meæ qui facit supérbiam: * qui lóquitur iníqua, non diréxit in conspéctu oculórum meórum.
verses.eng: 100:7 He that worketh pride shall not dwell in the midst of my house: * he that speaketh unjust things did not prosper before my eyes.

verses.lat: 100:8 In matutíno interficiébam omnes peccatóres terræ: * ut dispérderem de civitáte Dómini omnes operántes iniquitátem.
verses.eng: 100:8 In the morning I put to death all the wicked of the land: * that I might cut off all the workers of iniquity from the city of the Lord.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Tibi, Dómine, psallam, * et intéllegam in via immaculáta.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: I shall sing to thee, O Lord * and I shall understand with a perfect heart.

laudes.canticle1.label: Canticum 213
laudes.canticle1.antiphonLat: Dómine, magnus es tu, * et præclárus in virtúte tua.
laudes.canticle1.antiphonEng: O Lord, great art thou * and glorious in thy power.

verses.lat: (Canticum Judith * Judith 16:15-22)
verses.eng: (Canticle of_Judith * Judith 16:15-22)

verses.lat: 16:15 Hymnum cantémus Dómino, * hymnum novum cantémus Deo nostro.
verses.eng: 16:15 Let us sing a hymn to the Lord, * let us sing a new hymn to our God.

verses.lat: 16:16 Adonái, Dómine, magnus es tu, et præclárus in virtúte tua, * et quem superáre nemo potest.
verses.eng: 16:16 O Adonai, Lord, great art thou, and glorious in thy power, * and no one can overcome thee.

verses.lat: 16:17 Tibi sérviat omnis creatúra tua: * quia dixísti, et facta sunt:
verses.eng: 16:17 Let all thy creatures serve thee: * because thou hast spoken, and they were made:

verses.lat: 16:18 Misísti spíritum tuum, et creáta sunt, * et non est qui resístat voci tuæ.
verses.eng: 16:18 Thou didst send forth thy spirit, and they were created, * and there is no one that can resist thy voice.

verses.lat: 16:19 Montes a fundaméntis movebúntur cum aquis: * petræ, sicut cera, liquéscent ante fáciem tuam.
verses.eng: 16:19 The mountains shall be moved from the foundations with the waters: * the rocks shall melt as wax before thy face.

verses.lat: 16:20 Qui autem timent te, * magni erunt apud te per ómnia.
verses.eng: 16:20 But they that fear thee, * shall be great with thee in all things.

verses.lat: 16:21 Væ genti insurgénti super genus meum: Dóminus enim omnípotens vindicábit in eis, * in die judícii visitábit illos.
verses.eng: 16:21 Woe be to the nation that riseth up against my people: for the Lord almighty will take revenge on them, * in the day of judgment he will visit them.

verses.lat: 16:22 Dabit enim ignem, et vermes in carnes eórum, * ut urántur, et séntiant usque in sempitérnum.
verses.eng: 16:22 For he will give fire, and worms into their flesh, * that they may burn, and may feel for ever.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Dómine, magnus es tu, * et præclárus in virtúte tua.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: O Lord, great art thou * and glorious in thy power.

laudes.psalm4.label: Psalmus 145
laudes.psalm4.antiphonLat: Laudábo Deum meum * in vita mea.
laudes.psalm4.antiphonEng: I shall praise the Lord * in my life.

verses.lat: 145:2a Lauda, ánima mea, Dóminum, † laudábo Dóminum in vita mea: * psallam Deo meo quámdiu fúero.
verses.eng: 145:2a Praise the Lord, O my soul, † in my life I will praise the Lord: * I will sing to my God as long as I shall be.

verses.lat: 145:2b Nolíte confídere in princípibus: * (3) in fíliis hóminum, in quibus non est salus.
verses.eng: 145:2b Put not your trust in princes: * (3) in the children of men, in whom there is no salvation.

verses.lat: 145:4 Exíbit spíritus ejus, et revertétur in terram suam: * in illa die períbunt omnes cogitatiónes eórum.
verses.eng: 145:4 His spirit shall go forth, and he shall return into his earth: * in that day all their thoughts shall perish.

verses.lat: 145:5 Beátus, cujus Deus Jacob adjútor ejus, † spes ejus in Dómino, Deo ipsíus: * (6) qui fecit cælum et terram, mare, et ómnia, quæ in eis sunt.
verses.eng: 145:5 Blessed is he who hath the God of Jacob for his helper, † whose hope is in the Lord his God: * (6) who made heaven and earth, the sea, and all things that are in them.

verses.lat: 145:7a Qui custódit veritátem in sǽculum, † facit judícium injúriam patiéntibus: * dat escam esuriéntibus.
verses.eng: 145:7a Who keepeth truth for ever: † who executeth judgment for them that suffer wrong: * who giveth food to the hungry.

verses.lat: 145:7b Dóminus solvit compedítos: * (8a) Dóminus illúminat cæcos.
verses.eng: 145:7b The Lord looseth them that are fettered: * (8a) the Lord enlighteneth the blind.

verses.lat: 145:8b Dóminus érigit elísos, * Dóminus díligit justos.
verses.eng: 145:8b The Lord lifteth up them that are cast down: * the Lord loveth the just.

verses.lat: 145:9 Dóminus custódit ádvenas, † pupíllum et víduam suscípiet: * et vias peccatórum dispérdet.
verses.eng: 145:9 The Lord keepeth the strangers, † he will support the fatherless and the widow: * and the ways of sinners he will destroy.

verses.lat: 145:10 Regnábit Dóminus in sǽcula, Deus tuus, Sion, * in generatiónem et generatiónem.
verses.eng: 145:10 The Lord shall reign for ever: thy God, O Sion, * unto generation and generation.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Laudábo Deum meum * in vita mea.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: I shall praise the Lord * in my life.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (2 Cor 1:3-4)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Benedíctus Deus, et Pater Dómini nostri Jesu Christi, Pater misericordiárum, et Deus totíus consolatiónis, qui consolátur nos in omni tribulatióne nostra.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort, who comforteth us in all our tribulation.

capitulum_laudes.label: Capitulum (Rom 13:12-13)
capitulum_laudes.lat: Nox præcéssit, dies autem appropinquávit. Abiciámus ergo ópera tenebrárum, et induámur arma lucis. Sicut in die honéste ambulémus.
capitulum_laudes.eng: The night is passed, and the day is at hand. Let us therefore cast off the works of darkness, and put on the armour of light. Let us walk honestly, as in the day.

versum_tertia.label: Versiculus
versum_tertia.lat: ℣. Adjútor meus, esto, ne derelínquas me.
versum_tertia.eng: ℣. Be Thou my helper, forsake me not.
versum_tertia.latR: ℟. Neque despícias me, Deus, salutáris meus.
versum_tertia.engR: ℟. Do not Thou despise me, O God my Saviour.

versum_sexta.label: Versiculus
versum_sexta.lat: ℣. Dóminus regit me, et nihil mihi déerit.
versum_sexta.eng: ℣. The Lord ruleth me: and I shall want nothing.
versum_sexta.latR: ℟. In loco páscuæ ibi me collocávit.
versum_sexta.engR: ℟. He hath set me in a place of pasture.

versum_nona.label: Versiculus
versum_nona.lat: ℣. Ab occúltis meis munda me, Dómine.
versum_nona.eng: ℣. From my secret ones cleanse me, O Lord.
versum_nona.latR: ℟. Et ab aliénis parce servo tuo.
versum_nona.engR: ℟. And from those of others spare Thy servant.

ant_1.label: Antíphona
ant_1.lat: Speciósus forma * præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis.
ant_1.eng: Thou art beautiful * above the sons of men: grace is poured abroad in thy lips.

ant_2.label: Antíphona
ant_2.lat: Magnus Dóminus * et laudábilis nimis in civitáte Dei nostri.
ant_2.eng: Great is the Lord * and exceedingly to be praised in the city of our God.

ant_3.label: Antíphona
ant_3.eng: The God of gods, * the Lord hath spoken.

nocturn_1_versum.label: Versicle after Nocturn I
nocturn_1_versum.eng: ℣. The Lord of armies is with us.
nocturn_1_versum.engR: ℟. The God of Jacob is our protector.

nocturn_2_versum.label: Versicle after Nocturn II
nocturn_2_versum.lat: ℣. Deus rédimet ánimam meam de manu ínferi.
nocturn_2_versum.eng: ℣. God will redeem my soul from the hand of hell.

nocturn_3_versum.label: Versicle after Nocturn III
nocturn_3_versum.lat: ℣. Audítui meo dabis gáudium et lætítiam.
nocturn_3_versum.eng: ℣. To my hearing thou shalt give joy and gladness.
nocturn_3_versum.engR: ℟. And the bones that have been humbled shall rejoice.

hymnus_laudes.label: Hymn
hymnus_laudes.title: Nox, et tenébræ, et núbila
hymnus_laudes.lat:
Nox, et tenébræ, et núbila,
Confúsa mundi et túrbida:
Lux intrat, albéscit polus:
Christus venit: discédite.

Calígo terræ scínditur
Percússa solis spículo,
Rebúsque jam color redit,
Vultu niténtis síderis.

Te, Christe, solum nóvimus:
Te mente pura et simplici,
Flendo et canéndo quǽsumus,
Inténde nostris sénsibus.

Sunt multa fucis íllita,
Quæ luce purgéntur tua:
Tu, vera lux cæléstium,
Vultu seréno illúmina.

Deo Patri sit glória,
Ejúsque soli Fílio,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
Nunc et per omne sǽculum.
Amen.
hymnus_laudes.eng:
Day is breaking, dawn is bright:
Hence, vain shadows of the night!
Mists that dim our mortal sight,
Christ is come! Depart!

Darkness routed lifts her wings
As the radiance upwards springs:
Through the world of wakened things
Life and colour dart.

Thee, O Christ, alone we know:
Singing even in our woe,
With pure hearts to thee we go:
On our senses shine!

In thy beams be purged away
All that leads our thoughts astray!
Through our spirits, King of day,
Pour thy light divine!

Unto God the Father, Son,
Holy Spirit, Three in One,
One in Three, be glory done,
Now and evermore.
Amen.

hymnus_vespera.label: Hymn
hymnus_vespera.title: Cæli Deus sanctíssime
hymnus_vespera.lat:
Cæli Deus sanctíssime,
Qui lúcidas mundi plagas
Candóre pingis ígneo,
Augens decóro lúmine:

Quarto die qui flámmeam
Dum solis accéndis rotam,
Lunæ minístras órdinem,
Vagósque cursus síderum:

Ut nóctibus, vel lúmini
Diremptiónis términum,
Primórdiis et ménsium
Signum dares notíssimum;

Expélle noctem córdium:
Abstérge sordes méntium:
Resólve culpæ vínculum:
Evérte moles críminum.

Præsta, Pater piíssime,
Patríque compar Únice,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito
Regnans per omne sǽculum.
Amen.
hymnus_vespera.eng:
O God, whose hand hath spread the sky,
And all its shining hosts on high,
And painting it with fiery light,
Made it so beauteous and so bright:

Thou, when the fourth day was begun,
Didst frame the circle of the sun,
And set the moon for ordered change,
And planets for their wider range:

To night and day, by certain line,
Their varying bounds thou didst assign;
And gav’st a signal, known and meet,
For months begun and months complete.

Enlighten thou the hearts of men:
Polluted souls make pure again:
Unloose the bands of guilt within:
Remove the burden of our sin.

Grant this, O Father, ever One
With Christ thy sole-begotten Son,
Whom, with the Spirit we adore,
One God, both now and evermore.
Amen.

ant_laudes.label: Antiphon ad Benedictus
ant_laudes.lat: De manu ómnium * qui odérunt nos, liberávit nos Dóminus.
ant_laudes.eng: From the hand of all * who hate us, the Lord has delivered us.

ant_vespera.label: Antiphon ad Magnificat
ant_vespera.lat: Respéxit Dóminus * humilitátem meam, et fecit in me magna, qui potens est.
ant_vespera.eng: The Lord has regarded * my lowliness, and he who is mighty has done great things through me.

versum_1.label: Versicle
versum_1.eng: We are filled in the morning with thy mercy.
versum_1.engR: And we have rejoiced, and are delighted.

matutinum.psalm2.label: Psalmus 77 (1-8)

verses.lat: 77:1 Atténdite, pópule meus, legem meam: * inclináte aurem vestram in verba oris mei.
verses.eng: 77:1 Attend, O my people, to my law: * incline your ears to the words of my mouth.

verses.lat: 77:2 Apériam in parábolis os meum: * loquar propositiónes ab inítio.
verses.eng: 77:2 I will open my mouth in parables: * I will utter propositions from the beginning.

verses.lat: 77:3 Quanta audívimus et cognóvimus ea: * et patres nostri narravérunt nobis.
verses.eng: 77:3 How great things have we heard and known, * and our fathers have told us.

verses.lat: 77:4 Non sunt occultáta a fíliis eórum: * in generatióne áltera.
verses.eng: 77:4 They have not been hidden from their children, * in another generation.

verses.lat: 77:4 Narrántes laudes Dómini, et virtútes ejus: * et mirabília ejus, quæ fecit.
verses.eng: 77:4 Declaring the praises of the Lord, and his powers, * and his wonders which he hath done.

verses.lat: 77:5 Et suscitávit testimónium in Jacob: * et legem pósuit in Israël.
verses.eng: 77:5 And he set up a testimony in Jacob: * and made a law in Israel.

verses.lat: 77:5 Quanta mandávit pátribus nostris nota fácere ea fíliis suis: * ut cognóscat generátio áltera.
verses.eng: 77:5 How great things he commanded our fathers, that they should make the same known to their children: * that another generation might know them.

verses.lat: 77:6 Fílii qui nascéntur, et exsúrgent, * et narrábunt fíliis suis.
verses.eng: 77:6 The children that should be born and should rise up, * and declare them to their children.

verses.lat: 77:7 Ut ponant in Deo spem suam, et non obliviscántur óperum Dei: * et mandáta ejus exquírant.
verses.eng: 77:7 That they may put their hope in God and may not forget the works of God: * and may seek his commandments.

verses.lat: 77:8 Ne fiant sicut patres eórum: * generátio prava et exásperans.
verses.eng: 77:8 That they may not become like their fathers, * a perverse and exasperating generation.

verses.lat: 77:8 Generátio, quæ non diréxit cor suum: * et non est créditus cum Deo spíritus ejus.
verses.eng: 77:8 A generation that set not their heart aright: * and whose spirit was not faithful to God.

matutinum.psalm2.antiphonLat: Suscitávit Dóminus * testimónium in Jacob: et legem pósuit in Israël.
matutinum.psalm2.antiphonEng: The Lord set up a testimony in Jacob: * and made a law in Israel.

matutinum.psalm3.label: Psalmus 77 (9-16)

verses.lat: 77:9 Fílii Ephrem intendéntes et mitténtes arcum: * convérsi sunt in die belli.
verses.eng: 77:9 The sons of Ephraim who bend and shoot with the bow: * they have turned back in the day of battle.

verses.lat: 77:10 Non custodiérunt testaméntum Dei: * et in lege ejus noluérunt ambuláre.
verses.eng: 77:10 They kept not the covenant of God: * and in his law they would not walk.

verses.lat: 77:11 Et oblíti sunt benefactórum ejus: * et mirabílium ejus quæ osténdit eis.
verses.eng: 77:11 And they forgot his benefits, * and his wonders that he had shewn them.

verses.lat: 77:12 Coram pátribus eórum fecit mirabília in terra Ægýpti: * in campo Táneos.
verses.eng: 77:12 Wonderful things did he do in the sight of their fathers, in the land of Egypt, * in the field of Tanis.

verses.lat: 77:13 Interrúpit mare, et perdúxit eos: * et státuit aquas quasi in utre.
verses.eng: 77:13 He divided the sea and brought them through: * and he made the waters to stand as in a vessel.

verses.lat: 77:14 Et dedúxit eos in nube diéi: * et tota nocte in illuminatióne ignis.
verses.eng: 77:14 And he conducted them with a cloud by day: * and all the night with a light of fire.

verses.lat: 77:15 Interrúpit petram in erémo: * et adaquávit eos velut in abýsso multa.
verses.eng: 77:15 He struck the rock in the wilderness: * and gave them to drink, as out of the great deep.

verses.lat: 77:16 Et edúxit aquam de petra: * et dedúxit tamquam flúmina aquas.
verses.eng: 77:16 He brought forth water out of the rock: * and made streams run down as rivers.

matutinum.psalm3.antiphonLat: Coram pátribus eórum * fecit Deus mirabília.
matutinum.psalm3.antiphonEng: The Lord did wonderful things * in the sight of their fathers.

matutinum.psalm4.label: Psalmus 77 (17-31)

verses.lat: 77:17 Et apposuérunt adhuc peccáre ei: * in iram excitavérunt Excélsum in inaquóso.
verses.eng: 77:17 And they added yet more sin against him: * they provoked the most High to wrath in the place without water.

verses.lat: 77:18 Et tentavérunt Deum in córdibus suis, * ut péterent escas animábus suis.
verses.eng: 77:18 And they tempted God in their hearts, * by asking meat for their desires.

verses.lat: 77:19 Et male locúti sunt de Deo: * dixérunt: Numquid póterit Deus paráre mensam in desérto?
verses.eng: 77:19 And they spoke ill of God: * they said: Can God furnish a table in the wilderness?

verses.lat: 77:20 Quóniam percússit petram, et fluxérunt aquæ: * et torréntes inundavérunt.
verses.eng: 77:20 Because he struck the rock, and the waters gushed out, * and the streams overflowed.

verses.lat: 77:20 Numquid et panem póterit dare, * aut paráre mensam pópulo suo?
verses.eng: 77:20 Can he also give bread, * or provide a table for his people?

verses.lat: 77:21 Ídeo audívit Dóminus, et dístulit: * et ignis accénsus est in Jacob, et ira ascéndit in Israël.
verses.eng: 77:21 Therefore the Lord heard, and was angry: * and a fire was kindled against Jacob, and wrath came up against Israel.

verses.lat: 77:22 Quia non credidérunt in Deo: * nec speravérunt in salutári ejus:
verses.eng: 77:22 Because they believed not in God: * and trusted not in his salvation.

verses.lat: 77:23 Et mandávit núbibus désuper: * et jánuas cæli apéruit.
verses.eng: 77:23 And he had commanded the clouds from above, * and had opened the doors of heaven.

verses.lat: 77:24 Et pluit illis manna ad manducándum: * et panem cæli dedit eis.
verses.eng: 77:24 And had rained down manna upon them to eat, * and had given them the bread of heaven.

verses.lat: 77:25 Panem Angelórum manducávit homo, * cibária misit eis in abundántia.
verses.eng: 77:25 Man ate the bread of angels: * he sent them provisions in abundance.

verses.lat: 77:26 Tránstulit Austrum de cælo: * et indúxit in virtúte sua Áfricum.
verses.eng: 77:26 He removed the south wind from heaven: * and by his power brought in the southwest wind.

verses.lat: 77:27 Et pluit super eos sicut púlverem carnes: * et sicut arénam maris volatília pennáta.
verses.eng: 77:27 And he rained upon them flesh as dust: * and feathered fowls like as the sand of the sea.

verses.lat: 77:28 Et cecidérunt in médio castrórum eórum: * circa tabernácula eórum.
verses.eng: 77:28 And they fell in the midst of their camp, * round about their pavilions.

verses.lat: 77:29 Et manducavérunt, et saturáti sunt nimis, et desidérium eórum áttulit eis: * non sunt fraudáti a desidério suo.
verses.eng: 77:29 So they did eat, and were filled exceedingly, and he gave them their desire: * they were not defrauded of that which they craved.

verses.lat: 77:30 Adhuc escæ eórum erant in ore ipsórum: * et ira Dei ascéndit super eos.
verses.eng: 77:30 As yet their meat was in their mouth: * and the wrath of God came upon them.

verses.lat: 77:31 Et occídit pingues eórum, * et eléctos Israël impedívit.
verses.eng: 77:31 And he slew the fat ones amongst them, * and brought down the chosen men of Israel.

matutinum.psalm4.antiphonLat: Jánuas cæli apéruit * Dóminus, et pluit illis manna ad manducándum.
matutinum.psalm4.antiphonEng: The Lord opened * the doors of heaven and had rained down manna upon them to eat.

matutinum.psalm5.label: Psalmus 77 (32-41)

verses.lat: 77:32 In ómnibus his peccavérunt adhuc: * et non credidérunt in mirabílibus ejus.
verses.eng: 77:32 In all these things they sinned still: * and they believed not for his wondrous works.

verses.lat: 77:33 Et defecérunt in vanitáte dies eórum: * et anni eórum cum festinatióne.
verses.eng: 77:33 And their days were consumed in vanity, * and their years in haste.

verses.lat: 77:34 Cum occíderet eos, quærébant eum: * et revertebántur, et dilúculo veniébant ad eum.
verses.eng: 77:34 When he slew them, then they sought him: * and they returned, and came to him early in the morning.

verses.lat: 77:35 Et rememoráti sunt quia Deus adjútor est eórum: * et Deus excélsus redémptor eórum est.
verses.eng: 77:35 And they remembered that God was their helper: * and the most high God their redeemer.

verses.lat: 77:36 Et dilexérunt eum in ore suo, * et lingua sua mentíti sunt ei.
verses.eng: 77:36 And they loved him with their mouth: * and with their tongue they lied unto him:

verses.lat: 77:37 Cor autem eórum non erat rectum cum eo: * nec fidéles hábiti sunt in testaménto ejus.
verses.eng: 77:37 But their heart was not right with him: * nor were they counted faithful in his covenant.

verses.lat: 77:38 Ipse autem est miséricors, et propítius fiet peccátis eórum: * et non dispérdet eos.
verses.eng: 77:38 But he is merciful, and will forgive their sins: * and will not destroy them.

verses.lat: 77:38 Et abundávit ut avérteret iram suam: * et non accéndit omnem iram suam:
verses.eng: 77:38 And many a time did he turn away his anger: * and did not kindle all his wrath.

verses.lat: 77:39 Et recordátus est quia caro sunt: * spíritus vadens et non rédiens.
verses.eng: 77:39 And he remembered that they are flesh: * a wind that goeth and returneth not.

verses.lat: 77:40 Quóties exacerbavérunt eum in desérto, * in iram concitavérunt eum in inaquóso?
verses.eng: 77:40 How often did they provoke him in the desert: * and move him to wrath in the place without water?

verses.lat: 77:41 Et convérsi sunt, et tentavérunt Deum: * et Sanctum Israël exacerbavérunt.
verses.eng: 77:41 And they turned back and tempted God: * and grieved the holy one of Israel.

matutinum.psalm5.antiphonLat: Deus adjútor * est eórum: et Excélsus redémptor eórum est.
matutinum.psalm5.antiphonEng: God is their helper, * and the most high God their redeemer.

matutinum.psalm6.label: Psalmus 77 (42-58)

verses.lat: 77:42 Non sunt recordáti manus ejus, * die qua redémit eos de manu tribulántis.
verses.eng: 77:42 They remembered not his hand, * in the day that he redeemed them from the hand of him that afflicted them:

verses.lat: 77:43 Sicut pósuit in Ægýpto signa sua, * et prodígia sua in campo Táneos.
verses.eng: 77:43 How he wrought his signs in Egypt, * and his wonders in the field of Tanis.

verses.lat: 77:44 Et convértit in sánguinem flúmina eórum: * et imbres eórum, ne bíberent.
verses.eng: 77:44 And he turned their rivers into blood, * and their showers that they might not drink.

verses.lat: 77:45 Misit in eos cœnomyíam, et comédit eos: * et ranam, et dispérdidit eos.
verses.eng: 77:45 He sent amongst them diverse sorts of flies, which devoured them: * and frogs which destroyed them.

verses.lat: 77:46 Et dedit ærúgini fructus eórum: * et labóres eórum locústæ.
verses.eng: 77:46 And he gave up their fruits to the blast, * and their labours to the locust.

verses.lat: 77:47 Et occídit in grándine víneas eórum: * et moros eórum in pruína.
verses.eng: 77:47 And he destroyed their vineyards with hail, * and their mulberry trees with hoarfrost.

verses.lat: 77:48 Et trádidit grándini juménta eórum: * et possessiónem eórum igni.
verses.eng: 77:48 And he gave up their cattle to the hail, * and their stock to the fire.

verses.lat: 77:49 Misit in eos iram indignatiónis suæ: * indignatiónem, et iram, et tribulatiónem: immissiónes per ángelos malos.
verses.eng: 77:49 And he sent upon them the wrath of his indignation: * indignation and wrath and trouble, which he sent by evil angels.

verses.lat: 77:50 Viam fecit sémitæ iræ suæ, non pepércit a morte animábus eórum: * et juménta eórum in morte conclúsit.
verses.eng: 77:50 He made a way for a path to his anger: * he spared not their souls from death, and their cattle he shut up in death.

verses.lat: 77:51 Et percússit omne primogénitum in terra Ægýpti: * primítias omnis labóris eórum in tabernáculis Cham.
verses.eng: 77:51 And he killed all the firstborn in the land of Egypt: * the firstfruits of all their labour in the tabernacles of Cham.

verses.lat: 77:52 Et ábstulit sicut oves pópulum suum: * et perdúxit eos tamquam gregem in desérto.
verses.eng: 77:52 And he took away his own people as sheep: * and guided them in the wilderness like a flock.

verses.lat: 77:53 Et dedúxit eos in spe, et non timuérunt: * et inimícos eórum opéruit mare.
verses.eng: 77:53 And he brought them out in hope, and they feared not: * and the sea overwhelmed their enemies.

verses.lat: 77:54 Et indúxit eos in montem sanctificatiónis suæ: * montem, quem acquisívit déxtera ejus.
verses.eng: 77:54 And he brought them into the mountain of his sanctuary: * the mountain which his right hand had purchased.

verses.lat: 77:54 Et ejécit a fácie eórum gentes: * et sorte divísit eis terram in funículo distributiónis.
verses.eng: 77:54 And he cast out the Gentiles before them: * and by lot divided to them their land by a line of distribution.

verses.lat: 77:55 Et habitáre fecit in tabernáculis eórum: * tribus Israël.
verses.eng: 77:55 And he made the tribes of Israel * to dwell in their tabernacles.

verses.lat: 77:56 Et tentavérunt, et exacerbavérunt Deum excélsum: * et testimónia ejus non custodiérunt.
verses.eng: 77:56 Yet they tempted, and provoked the most high God: * and they kept not his testimonies.

verses.lat: 77:57 Et avertérunt se, et non servavérunt pactum: * quemádmodum patres eórum convérsi sunt in arcum pravum.
verses.eng: 77:57 And they turned away, and kept not the covenant: * even like their fathers they were turned aside as a crooked bow.

verses.lat: 77:58 In iram concitavérunt eum in cóllibus suis: * et in sculptílibus suis ad æmulatiónem eum provocavérunt.
verses.eng: 77:58 They provoked him to anger on their hills: * and moved him to jealousy with their graven things.

matutinum.psalm6.antiphonLat: Redémit eos * Dóminus de manu tribulántis.
matutinum.psalm6.antiphonEng: The Lord redeemed them * from the hand of him that afflicted them.

matutinum.psalm7.label: Psalmus 77 (59-72)

verses.lat: 77:59 Audívit Deus, et sprevit: * et ad níhilum redégit valde Israël.
verses.eng: 77:59 God heard, and despised them, * and he reduced Israel exceedingly as it were to nothing.

verses.lat: 77:60 Et répulit tabernáculum Silo: * tabernáculum suum, ubi habitávit in homínibus.
verses.eng: 77:60 And he put away the tabernacle of Silo, * his tabernacle where he dwelt among men.

verses.lat: 77:61 Et trádidit in captivitátem virtútem eórum: * et pulchritúdinem eórum in manus inimíci.
verses.eng: 77:61 And he delivered their strength into captivity: * and their beauty into the hands of the enemy.

verses.lat: 77:62 Et conclúsit in gládio pópulum suum: * et hereditátem suam sprevit.
verses.eng: 77:62 And he shut up his people under the sword: * and he despised his inheritance.

verses.lat: 77:63 Júvenes eórum comédit ignis: * et vírgines eórum non sunt lamentátæ.
verses.eng: 77:63 Fire consumed their young men: * and their maidens were not lamented.

verses.lat: 77:64 Sacerdótes eórum in gládio cecidérunt: * et víduæ eórum non plorabántur.
verses.eng: 77:64 Their priests fell by the sword: * and their widows did not mourn.

verses.lat: 77:65 Et excitátus est tamquam dórmiens Dóminus: * tamquam potens crapulátus a vino.
verses.eng: 77:65 And the Lord was awaked as one out of sleep, * and like a mighty man that hath been surfeited with wine.

verses.lat: 77:66 Et percússit inimícos suos in posterióra: * oppróbrium sempitérnum dedit illis.
verses.eng: 77:66 And he smote his enemies on the hinder parts: * he put them to an everlasting reproach.

verses.lat: 77:67 Et répulit tabernáculum Joseph: * et tribum Éphraim non elégit.
verses.eng: 77:67 And he rejected the tabernacle of Joseph: * and chose not the tribe of Ephraim:

verses.lat: 77:68 Sed elégit tribum Juda, * montem Sion quem diléxit.
verses.eng: 77:68 But he chose the tribe of Juda, * mount Sion which he loved.

verses.lat: 77:69 Et ædificávit sicut unicórnium sanctifícium suum in terra, * quam fundávit in sǽcula.
verses.eng: 77:69 And he built his sanctuary as of unicorns, in the land * which he founded for ever.

verses.lat: 77:70 Et elégit David, servum suum, et sústulit eum de grégibus óvium: * de post fœtántes accépit eum,
verses.eng: 77:70 And he chose his servant David, and took him from the flocks of sheep: * he brought him from following the ewes great with young,

verses.lat: 77:71 Páscere Jacob, servum suum, * et Israël, hereditátem suam:
verses.eng: 77:71 To feed Jacob his servant, * and Israel his inheritance.

verses.lat: 77:72 Et pavit eos in innocéntia cordis sui: * et in intelléctibus mánuum suárum dedúxit eos.
verses.eng: 77:72 And he fed them in the innocence of his heart: * and conducted them by the skilfulness of his hands.

matutinum.psalm7.antiphonLat: Ædificávit * Deus sanctifícium suum in terra.
matutinum.psalm7.antiphonEng: God built * his sanctuary in the earth.

matutinum.psalm8.label: Psalmus 78

verses.lat: 78:1 Deus, venérunt gentes in hereditátem tuam, polluérunt templum sanctum tuum: * posuérunt Jerúsalem in pomórum custódiam.
verses.eng: 78:1 O God, the heathens are come into thy inheritance, they have defiled thy holy temple: * they have made Jerusalem as a place to keep fruit.

verses.lat: 78:2 Posuérunt morticína servórum tuórum, escas volatílibus cæli: * carnes sanctórum tuórum béstiis terræ.
verses.eng: 78:2 They have given the dead bodies of thy servants to be meat for the fowls of the air: * the flesh of thy saints for the beasts of the earth.

verses.lat: 78:3 Effudérunt sánguinem eórum tamquam aquam in circúitu Jerúsalem: * et non erat qui sepelíret.
verses.eng: 78:3 They have poured out their blood as water, round about Jerusalem, * and there was none to bury them.

verses.lat: 78:4 Facti sumus oppróbrium vicínis nostris: * subsannátio et illúsio his, qui in circúitu nostro sunt.
verses.eng: 78:4 We are become a reproach to our neighbours: * a scorn and derision to them that are round about us.

verses.lat: 78:5 Úsquequo, Dómine, irascéris in finem: * accendétur velut ignis zelus tuus?
verses.eng: 78:5 How long, O Lord, wilt thou be angry for ever: * shall thy zeal be kindled like a fire?

verses.lat: 78:6 Effúnde iram tuam in gentes, quæ te non novérunt: * et in regna quæ nomen tuum non invocavérunt:
verses.eng: 78:6 Pour out thy wrath upon the nations that have not known thee: * and upon the kingdoms that have not called upon thy name.

verses.lat: 78:7 Quia comedérunt Jacob: * et locum ejus desolavérunt.
verses.eng: 78:7 Because they have devoured Jacob; * and have laid waste his place.

verses.lat: 78:8 Ne memíneris iniquitátum nostrárum antiquárum, cito antícipent nos misericórdiæ tuæ: * quia páuperes facti sumus nimis.
verses.eng: 78:8 Remember not our former iniquities: let thy mercies speedily prevent us, * for we are become exceeding poor.

verses.lat: 78:9 Ádjuva nos, Deus, salutáris noster: et propter glóriam nóminis tui, Dómine, líbera nos: * et propítius esto peccátis nostris, propter nomen tuum:
verses.eng: 78:9 Help us, O God, our saviour: and for the glory of thy name, O Lord, deliver us: * and forgive us our sins for thy name’s sake:

verses.lat: 78:10 Ne forte dicant in géntibus: Ubi est Deus eórum? * et innotéscat in natiónibus coram óculis nostris.
verses.eng: 78:10 Lest they should say among the Gentiles: Where is their God? * And let him be made known among the nations before our eyes,

verses.lat: 78:10 Últio sánguinis servórum tuórum, qui effúsus est: * intróeat in conspéctu tuo gémitus compeditórum.
verses.eng: 78:10 By the revenging the blood of thy servants, which hath been shed: * let the sighing of the prisoners come in before thee.

verses.lat: 78:11 Secúndum magnitúdinem brácchii tui, * pósside fílios mortificatórum.
verses.eng: 78:11 According to the greatness of thy arm, * take possession of the children of them that have been put to death.

verses.lat: 78:12 Et redde vicínis nostris séptuplum in sinu eórum: * impropérium ipsórum, quod exprobravérunt tibi, Dómine.
verses.eng: 78:12 And render to our neighbours sevenfold in their bosom: * the reproach wherewith they have reproached thee, O Lord.

verses.lat: 78:13 Nos autem pópulus tuus, et oves páscuæ tuæ, * confitébimur tibi in sǽculum.
verses.eng: 78:13 But we thy people, and the sheep of thy pasture, * will give thanks to thee for ever.

verses.lat: 78:13 In generatiónem et generatiónem * annuntiábimus laudem tuam.
verses.eng: 78:13 We will shew forth thy praise, * unto generation and generation.

matutinum.psalm8.antiphonLat: Ádjuva nos, * Deus, salutáris noster: et propítius esto peccátis nostris.
matutinum.psalm8.antiphonEng: Help us, O God, our Saviour, * deliver us: and forgive us our sins.

matutinum.psalm9.label: Psalmus 80

verses.lat: 80:2 Exsultáte Deo, adjutóri nostro: * jubiláte Deo Jacob.
verses.eng: 80:2 Rejoice to God, our helper: * sing aloud to the God of Jacob.

verses.lat: 80:3 Súmite psalmum, et date týmpanum: * psaltérium jucúndum cum cíthara.
verses.eng: 80:3 Take a psalm, and bring hither the timbrel: * the pleasant psaltery with the harp.

verses.lat: 80:4 Buccináte in Neoménia tuba, * in insígni die solemnitátis vestræ.
verses.eng: 80:4 Blow up the trumpet on the new moon, * on the noted day of your solemnity.

verses.lat: 80:5 Quia præcéptum in Israël est: * et judícium Deo Jacob.
verses.eng: 80:5 For it is a commandment in Israel, * and a judgment to the God of Jacob.

verses.lat: 80:6 Testimónium in Joseph pósuit illud, cum exíret de terra Ægýpti: * linguam, quam non nóverat, audívit.
verses.eng: 80:6 He ordained it for a testimony in Joseph, when he came out of the land of Egypt: * he heard a tongue which he knew not.

verses.lat: 80:7 Divértit ab onéribus dorsum ejus: * manus ejus in cóphino serviérunt.
verses.eng: 80:7 He removed his back from the burdens: * his hands had served in baskets.

verses.lat: 80:8 In tribulatióne invocásti me, et liberávi te: * exaudívi te in abscóndito tempestátis: probávi te apud aquam contradictiónis.
verses.eng: 80:8 Thou calledst upon me in affliction, and I delivered thee: * I heard thee in the secret place of tempest: I proved thee at the waters of contradiction.

verses.lat: 80:9 Audi, pópulus meus, et contestábor te: * Israël, si audíeris me, non erit in te deus recens, neque adorábis deum aliénum.
verses.eng: 80:9 Hear, O my people, and I will testify to thee: * O Israel, if thou wilt hearken to me; there shall be no new god in thee: neither shalt thou adore a strange god.

verses.lat: 80:11 Ego enim sum Dóminus Deus tuus, qui edúxi te de terra Ægýpti: * diláta os tuum, et implébo illud.
verses.eng: 80:11 For I am the Lord thy God, who brought thee out of the land of Egypt: * open thy mouth wide, and I will fill it.

verses.lat: 80:12 Et non audívit pópulus meus vocem meam: * et Israël non inténdit mihi.
verses.eng: 80:12 But my people heard not my voice: * and Israel hearkened not to me.

verses.lat: 80:13 Et dimísi eos secúndum desidéria cordis eórum: * ibunt in adinventiónibus suis.
verses.eng: 80:13 So I let them go according to the desires of their heart: * they shall walk in their own inventions.

verses.lat: 80:14 Si pópulus meus audísset me: * Israël si in viis meis ambulásset:
verses.eng: 80:14 If my people had heard me: * if Israel had walked in my ways:

verses.lat: 80:15 Pro níhilo fórsitan inimícos eórum humiliássem: * et super tribulántes eos misíssem manum meam.
verses.eng: 80:15 I should soon have humbled their enemies, * and laid my hand on them that troubled them.

verses.lat: 80:16 Inimíci Dómini mentíti sunt ei: * et erit tempus eórum in sǽcula.
verses.eng: 80:16 The enemies of the Lord have lied to him: * and their time shall be for ever.

verses.lat: 80:17 Et cibávit eos ex ádipe fruménti: * et de petra, melle saturávit eos.
verses.eng: 80:17 And he fed them with the fat of wheat, * and filled them with honey out of the rock.

matutinum.psalm9.antiphonLat: Ego sum Dóminus * Deus tuus Israël, qui edúxi te de terra Ægýpti.
matutinum.psalm9.antiphonEng: I am the Lord * God of Israel, who brought you out from the land of Egypt.

matutinum.psalm10.label: Psalmus 82

verses.lat: 82:2 Deus, quis símilis erit tibi? * Ne táceas, neque compescáris, Deus.
verses.eng: 82:2 O God, who shall be like to thee? * Hold not thy peace, neither be O God, thou still,

verses.lat: 82:3 Quóniam ecce inimíci tui sonuérunt: * et qui odérunt te extulérunt caput.
verses.eng: 82:3 For lo, thy enemies have made a noise: * and they that hate thee have lifted up the head.

verses.lat: 82:4 Super pópulum tuum malignavérunt consílium: * et cogitavérunt advérsus sanctos tuos.
verses.eng: 82:4 They have taken a malicious counsel against thy people, * and have consulted against thy saints.

verses.lat: 82:5 Dixérunt: Veníte, et disperdámus eos de gente: * et non memorétur nomen Israël ultra.
verses.eng: 82:5 They have said: Come and let us destroy them, * so that they be not a nation: and let the name of Israel be remembered no more.

verses.lat: 82:6 Quóniam cogitavérunt unanímiter: * simul advérsum te testaméntum disposuérunt, tabernácula Idumæórum et Ismahelítæ:
verses.eng: 82:6 For they have contrived with one consent: * they have made a covenant together against thee; the tabernacles of the Edomites, and the Ismahelites:

verses.lat: 82:8 Moab, et Agaréni, Gebal, et Ammon, et Ámalec: * alienígenæ cum habitántibus Tyrum.
verses.eng: 82:8 Moab, and the Agarens, Gebal, and Ammon and Amalec: * the Philistines, with the inhabitants of Tyre.

verses.lat: 82:9 Étenim Assur venit cum illis: * facti sunt in adjutórium fíliis Lot.
verses.eng: 82:9 Yea, and the Assyrian also is joined with them: * they are come to the aid of the sons of Lot.

verses.lat: 82:10 Fac illis sicut Mádian, et Sísaræ: * sicut Jabin in torrénte Cisson.
verses.eng: 82:10 Do to them as thou didst to Madian and to Sisara: * as to Jabin at the brook of Cisson.

verses.lat: 82:11 Disperiérunt in Endor: * facti sunt ut stercus terræ.
verses.eng: 82:11 Who perished at Endor: * and became as dung for the earth.

verses.lat: 82:12 Pone príncipes eórum sicut Oreb, et Zeb, * et Zébee, et Sálmana:
verses.eng: 82:12 Make their princes like Oreb, and Zeb, * and Zebee, and Salmana.

verses.lat: 82:13 Omnes príncipes eórum: * qui dixérunt: Hereditáte possideámus Sanctuárium Dei.
verses.eng: 82:13 All their princes, * who have said: Let us possess the sanctuary of God for an inheritance.

verses.lat: 82:14 Deus meus, pone illos ut rotam: * et sicut stípulam ante fáciem venti.
verses.eng: 82:14 O my God, make them like a wheel; * and as stubble before the wind.

verses.lat: 82:15 Sicut ignis, qui combúrit silvam: * et sicut flamma combúrens montes:
verses.eng: 82:15 As fire which burneth the wood: * and as a flame burning mountains:

verses.lat: 82:16 Ita persequéris illos in tempestáte tua: * et in ira tua turbábis eos.
verses.eng: 82:16 So shalt thou pursue them with thy tempest: * and shalt trouble them in thy wrath.

verses.lat: 82:17 Imple fácies eórum ignomínia: * et quærent nomen tuum, Dómine.
verses.eng: 82:17 Fill their faces with shame; * and they shall seek thy name, O Lord.

verses.lat: 82:18 Erubéscant, et conturbéntur in sǽculum sǽculi: * et confundántur, et péreant.
verses.eng: 82:18 Let them be ashamed and troubled for ever and ever: * and let them be confounded and perish.

verses.lat: 82:19 Et cognóscant quia nomen tibi Dóminus: * tu solus Altíssimus in omni terra.
verses.eng: 82:19 And let them know that the Lord is thy name: * thou alone art the most High over all the earth.

matutinum.psalm10.antiphonLat: Ne táceas Deus * quóniam inimíci tui extulérunt caput.
matutinum.psalm10.antiphonEng: Be not thou silent, O Lord, * for Thy enemies lifted up their head.

vesperae.psalm1.label: Psalmus 138(1-13)
vesperae.psalm1.antiphonLat: Dómine, * probásti me et cognovísti me.
vesperae.psalm1.antiphonEng: Lord, * thou hast proved me, and known me.

verses.lat: 138:1 Dómine, probásti me, et cognovísti me: * (2) tu cognovísti sessiónem meam, et resurrectiónem meam.
verses.eng: 138:1 Lord, thou hast proved me, and known me: * (2) thou hast known my sitting down, and my rising up.

verses.lat: 138:3 Intellexísti cogitatiónes meas de longe: * sémitam meam, et funículum meum investigásti.
verses.eng: 138:3 Thou hast understood my thoughts afar off: * my path and my life thou hast searched out.

verses.lat: 138:4 Et omnes vias meas prævidísti: * quia non est sermo in lingua mea.
verses.eng: 138:4 And thou hast foreseen all my ways: * for there is no speech on my tongue.

verses.lat: 138:5 Ecce, Dómine, tu cognovísti ómnia novíssima, et antíqua: * tu formásti me, et posuísti super me manum tuam.
verses.eng: 138:5 Behold, O Lord, thou hast known all things, the last and those of old: * thou hast formed me, and hast laid thy hand upon me.

verses.lat: 138:6 Mirábilis facta est sciéntia tua ex me: * confortáta est, et non pótero ad eam.
verses.eng: 138:6 Thy knowledge is become wonderful to me: * it is high, and I cannot reach to it.

verses.lat: 138:7 Quo ibo a spíritu tuo? * et quo a fácie tua fúgiam?
verses.eng: 138:7 Whither shall I go from thy spirit? * or whither shall I flee from thy face?

verses.lat: 138:8 Si ascéndero in cælum, tu illic es: * si descéndero in inférnum, ades.
verses.eng: 138:8 If I ascend into heaven, thou art there: * if I descend into hell, thou art present.

verses.lat: 138:9 Si súmpsero pennas meas dilúculo, * et habitávero in extrémis maris:
verses.eng: 138:9 If I take my wings early in the morning, * and dwell in the uttermost parts of the sea:

verses.lat: 138:10 Étenim illuc manus tua dedúcet me: * et tenébit me déxtera tua.
verses.eng: 138:10 Even there also shall thy hand lead me: * and thy right hand shall hold me.

verses.lat: 138:11 Et dixi: Fórsitan ténebræ conculcábunt me: * et nox illuminátio mea in delíciis meis.
verses.eng: 138:11 And I said: Perhaps darkness shall cover me: * and night shall be my light in my pleasures.

verses.lat: 138:12 Quia ténebræ non obscurabúntur a te, † et nox sicut dies illuminábitur: * sicut ténebræ ejus, ita et lumen ejus.
verses.eng: 138:12 But darkness shall not be dark to thee, † and night shall be light as the day: * the darkness thereof, and the light thereof are alike to thee.

verses.lat: 138:13 Quia tu possedísti renes meos: * suscepísti me de útero matris meæ.
verses.eng: 138:13 For thou hast possessed my reins: * thou hast protected me from my mother’s womb.

vesperae.psalm2.label: Psalmus 138(14-24)
vesperae.psalm2.antiphonLat: Mirabília ópera tua, * Dómine, et ánima mea cognóscit nimis.
vesperae.psalm2.antiphonEng: Wonderful are thy works * and my soul knoweth right well.

verses.lat: 138:14 Confitébor tibi quia terribíliter magnificátus es: ‡ mirabília ópera tua, * et ánima mea cognóscit nimis.
verses.eng: 138:14 I will praise thee, for thou art fearfully magnified: ‡ wonderful are thy works, * and my soul knoweth right well.

verses.lat: 138:15 Non est occultátum os meum a te, quod fecísti in occúlto: * et substántia mea in inferióribus terræ.
verses.eng: 138:15 My bone is not hidden from thee, which thou hast made in secret: * and my substance in the lower parts of the earth.

verses.lat: 138:16 Imperféctum meum vidérunt óculi tui, † et in libro tuo omnes scribéntur: * dies formabúntur, et nemo in eis.
verses.eng: 138:16 Thy eyes did see my imperfect being, † and in thy book all shall be written: * days shall be formed, and no one in them.

verses.lat: 138:17 Mihi autem nimis honorificáti sunt amíci tui, Deus: * nimis confortátus est principátus eórum.
verses.eng: 138:17 But to me thy friends, O God, are made exceedingly honourable: * their principality is exceedingly strengthened.

verses.lat: 138:18 Dinumerábo eos, et super arénam multiplicabúntur: * exsurréxi, et adhuc sum tecum.
verses.eng: 138:18 I will number them, and they shall be multiplied above the sand: * I rose up and am still with thee.

verses.lat: 138:19 Si occíderis, Deus, peccatóres: * viri sánguinum, declináte a me:
verses.eng: 138:19 If thou wilt kill the wicked, O God: * ye men of blood, depart from me:

verses.lat: 138:20 Quia dícitis in cogitatióne: * Accípient in vanitáte civitátes tuas.
verses.eng: 138:20 Because you say in thought: * They shall receive thy cities in vain.

verses.lat: 138:21 Nonne qui odérunt te, Dómine, óderam? * et super inimícos tuos tabescébam?
verses.eng: 138:21 Have I not hated them, O Lord, that hated thee: * and pined away because of thy enemies?

verses.lat: 138:22 Perfécto ódio óderam illos: * et inimíci facti sunt mihi.
verses.eng: 138:22 I have hated them with a perfect hatred: * and they are become enemies to me.

verses.lat: 138:23 Proba me, Deus, et scito cor meum: * intérroga me, et cognósce sémitas meas.
verses.eng: 138:23 Prove me, O God, and know my heart: * examine me, and know my paths.

verses.lat: 138:24 Et vide, si via iniquitátis in me est: * et deduc me in via ætérna.
verses.eng: 138:24 And see if there be in me the way of iniquity: * and lead me in the eternal way.

vesperae.psalm3.label: Psalmus 139
vesperae.psalm3.antiphonLat: Ne derelínquas me, * Dómine, virtus salútis meæ.
vesperae.psalm3.antiphonEng: Do not thou forsake me, * O Lord, the strength of my salvation.

verses.lat: 139:2 Éripe me, Dómine, ab hómine malo: * a viro iníquo éripe me.
verses.eng: 139:2 Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man: * rescue me from the unjust man.

verses.lat: 139:3 Qui cogitavérunt iniquitátes in corde: * tota die constituébant prǽlia.
verses.eng: 139:3 Who have devised iniquities in their hearts: * all the day long they designed battles.

verses.lat: 139:4 Acuérunt linguas suas sicut serpéntis: * venénum áspidum sub lábiis eórum.
verses.eng: 139:4 They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent: * the venom of asps is under their lips.

verses.lat: 139:5 Custódi me, Dómine, de manu peccatóris: * et ab homínibus iníquis éripe me.
verses.eng: 139:5 Keep me, O Lord, from the hand of the wicked: * and from unjust men deliver me.

verses.lat: 139:5 Qui cogitavérunt supplantáre gressus meos: * abscondérunt supérbi láqueum mihi:
verses.eng: 139:5 Who have proposed to supplant my steps: * the proud have hidden a net for me.

verses.lat: 139:6 Et funes extendérunt in láqueum: * juxta iter scándalum posuérunt mihi.
verses.eng: 139:6 And they have stretched out cords for a snare: * they have laid for me a stumbling block by the wayside.

verses.lat: 139:7 Dixi Dómino: Deus meus es tu: * exáudi, Dómine, vocem deprecatiónis meæ.
verses.eng: 139:7 I said to the Lord: Thou art my God: * hear, O Lord, the voice of my supplication.

verses.lat: 139:8 Dómine, Dómine, virtus salútis meæ: * obumbrásti super caput meum in die belli.
verses.eng: 139:8 O Lord, Lord, the strength of my salvation: * thou hast overshadowed my head in the day of battle.

verses.lat: 139:9 Ne tradas me, Dómine, a desidério meo peccatóri: * cogitavérunt contra me, ne derelínquas me, ne forte exalténtur.
verses.eng: 139:9 Give me not up, O Lord, from my desire to the wicked: * they have plotted against me; do not thou forsake me, lest they should triumph.

verses.lat: 139:10 Caput circúitus eórum: * labor labiórum ipsórum opériet eos.
verses.eng: 139:10 The head of them compassing me about: * the labour of their lips shall overwhelm them.

verses.lat: 139:11 Cadent super eos carbónes, in ignem deícies eos: * in misériis non subsístent.
verses.eng: 139:11 Burning coals shall fall upon them; thou wilt cast them down into the fire: * in miseries they shall not be able to stand.

verses.lat: 139:12 Vir linguósus non dirigétur in terra: * virum injústum mala cápient in intéritu.
verses.eng: 139:12 A man full of tongue shall not be established in the earth: * evil shall catch the unjust man unto destruction.

verses.lat: 139:13 Cognóvi quia fáciet Dóminus judícium ínopis: * et vindíctam páuperum.
verses.eng: 139:13 I know that the Lord will do justice to the needy, * and will revenge the poor.

verses.lat: 139:14 Verúmtamen justi confitebúntur nómini tuo: * et habitábunt recti cum vultu tuo.
verses.eng: 139:14 But as for the just, they shall give glory to thy name: * and the upright shall dwell with thy countenance.

vesperae.psalm4.label: Psalmus 140
vesperae.psalm4.antiphonLat: Dómine, * clamávi ad te, exáudi me.
vesperae.psalm4.antiphonEng: I have cried to thee, * O Lord, hear me.

verses.lat: 140:1 Dómine, clamávi ad te, exáudi me: * inténde voci meæ, cum clamávero ad te.
verses.eng: 140:1 I have cried to thee, O Lord, hear me: * hearken to my voice, when I cry to thee.

verses.lat: 140:2 Dirigátur orátio mea sicut incénsum in conspéctu tuo: * elevátio mánuum meárum sacrifícium vespertínum.
verses.eng: 140:2 Let my prayer be directed as incense in thy sight; * the lifting up of my hands, as evening sacrifice.

verses.lat: 140:3 Pone, Dómine, custódiam ori meo: * et óstium circumstántiæ lábiis meis.
verses.eng: 140:3 Set a watch, O Lord, before my mouth: * and a door round about my lips.

verses.lat: 140:4 Non declínes cor meum in verba malítiæ, * ad excusándas excusatiónes in peccátis.
verses.eng: 140:4 Incline not my heart to evil words; * to make excuses in sins.

verses.lat: 140:4 Cum homínibus operántibus iniquitátem: * et non communicábo cum eléctis eórum.
verses.eng: 140:4 With men that work iniquity: * and I will not communicate with the choicest of them.

verses.lat: 140:5 Corrípiet me justus in misericórdia, et increpábit me: * óleum autem peccatóris non impínguet caput meum.
verses.eng: 140:5 The just man shall correct me in mercy, and shall reprove me: * but let not the oil of the sinner fatten my head.

verses.lat: 140:6 Quóniam adhuc et orátio mea in beneplácitis eórum: * absórpti sunt juncti petræ júdices eórum.
verses.eng: 140:6 For my prayer also shall still be against the things with which they are well pleased: * their judges falling upon the rock have been swallowed up.

verses.lat: 140:7 Áudient verba mea quóniam potuérunt: * sicut crassitúdo terræ erúpta est super terram.
verses.eng: 140:7 They shall hear my words, for they have prevailed: * as when the thickness of the earth is broken up upon the ground.

verses.lat: 140:8 Dissipáta sunt ossa nostra secus inférnum: * quia ad te, Dómine, Dómine, óculi mei: in te sperávi, non áuferas ánimam meam.
verses.eng: 140:8 Our bones are scattered by the side of hell. * But to thee, O Lord, Lord, are my eyes: in thee have I put my trust, take not away my soul.

verses.lat: 140:9 Custódi me a láqueo, quem statuérunt mihi: * et a scándalis operántium iniquitátem.
verses.eng: 140:9 Keep me from the snare, which they have laid for me, * and from the stumbling blocks of them that work iniquity.

verses.lat: 140:10 Cadent in retiáculo ejus peccatóres: * singuláriter sum ego donec tránseam.
verses.eng: 140:10 The wicked shall fall in his net: * I am alone until I pass.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Dómine, * probásti me et cognovísti me.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Lord, * thou hast proved me, and known me.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Mirabília ópera tua, * Dómine, et ánima mea cognóscit nimis.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Wonderful are thy works * and my soul knoweth right well.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Ne derelínquas me, * Dómine, virtus salútis meæ.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Do not thou forsake me, * O Lord, the strength of my salvation.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Dómine, * clamávi ad te, exáudi me.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.eng: I have cried to thee, * O Lord, hear me.

vesperae.psalm5.label: Psalmus 141
vesperae.psalm5.antiphonLat: Educ de custódia * ánimam meam, Dómine, ad confiténdum nómini tuo.
vesperae.psalm5.antiphonEng: Bring my soul * out of prison, O Lord, that I may praise thy name.

verses.lat: 141:2 Voce mea ad Dóminum clamávi: * voce mea ad Dóminum deprecátus sum:
verses.eng: 141:2 I cried to the Lord with my voice: * with my voice I made supplication to the Lord.

verses.lat: 141:3 Effúndo in conspéctu ejus oratiónem meam, * et tribulatiónem meam ante ipsum pronúntio.
verses.eng: 141:3 In his sight I pour out my prayer, * and before him I declare my trouble:

verses.lat: 141:4 In deficiéndo ex me spíritum meum, * et tu cognovísti sémitas meas.
verses.eng: 141:4 When my spirit failed me, * then thou knewest my paths.

verses.lat: 141:4 In via hac, qua ambulábam, * abscondérunt láqueum mihi.
verses.eng: 141:4 In this way wherein I walked, * they have hidden a snare for me.

verses.lat: 141:5 Considerábam ad déxteram, et vidébam: * et non erat qui cognósceret me.
verses.eng: 141:5 I looked on my right hand, and beheld, * and there was no one that would know me.

verses.lat: 141:5 Périit fuga a me, * et non est qui requírat ánimam meam.
verses.eng: 141:5 Flight hath failed me: * and there is no one that hath regard to my soul.

verses.lat: 141:6 Clamávi ad te, Dómine, * dixi: Tu es spes mea, pórtio mea in terra vivéntium.
verses.eng: 141:6 I cried to thee, O Lord: * I said: Thou art my hope, my portion in the land of the living.

verses.lat: 141:7 Inténde ad deprecatiónem meam: * quia humiliátus sum nimis.
verses.eng: 141:7 Attend to my supplication: * for I am brought very low.

verses.lat: 141:7 Líbera me a persequéntibus me: * quia confortáti sunt super me.
verses.eng: 141:7 Deliver me from my persecutors; * for they are stronger than I.

verses.lat: 141:8 Educ de custódia ánimam meam ad confiténdum nómini tuo: * me exspéctant justi, donec retríbuas mihi.
verses.eng: 141:8 Bring my soul out of prison, that I may praise thy name: * the just wait for me, until thou reward me.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Educ de custódia * ánimam meam, Dómine, ad confiténdum nómini tuo.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Bring my soul * out of prison, O Lord, that I may praise thy name.

ant_prima.label: Antíphona
ant_prima.lat: Ne discédas a me, * Dómine: quóniam tribulátio próxima est: quóniam non est qui ádjuvet.
ant_prima.eng: Depart not from me, * O Lord, for tribulation is very near; for there is none to help me.

verses.lat: 21:2 Deus, Deus meus, réspice in me: quare me dereliquísti? * longe a salúte mea verba delictórum meórum.
verses.eng: 21:2 O God my God, look upon me: why hast thou forsaken me? * Far from my salvation are the words of my sins.

verses.lat: 21:3 Deus meus, clamábo per diem, et non exáudies: * et nocte, et non ad insipiéntiam mihi.
verses.eng: 21:3 O my God, I shall cry by day, and thou wilt not hear: * and by night, and it shall not be reputed as folly in me.

verses.lat: 21:4 Tu autem in sancto hábitas, * laus Israël.
verses.eng: 21:4 But thou dwellest in the holy place, * the praise of Israel.

verses.lat: 21:5 In te speravérunt patres nostri: * speravérunt, et liberásti eos.
verses.eng: 21:5 In thee have our fathers hoped: * they have hoped, and thou hast delivered them.

verses.lat: 21:6 Ad te clamavérunt, et salvi facti sunt: * in te speravérunt, et non sunt confúsi.
verses.eng: 21:6 They cried to thee, and they were saved: * they trusted in thee, and were not confounded.

verses.lat: 21:7 Ego autem sum vermis, et non homo: * oppróbrium hóminum, et abjéctio plebis.
verses.eng: 21:7 But I am a worm, and no man: * the reproach of men, and the outcast of the people.

verses.lat: 21:8 Omnes vidéntes me, derisérunt me: * locúti sunt lábiis, et movérunt caput.
verses.eng: 21:8 All they that saw me have laughed me to scorn: * they have spoken with the lips, and wagged the head.

verses.lat: 21:9 Sperávit in Dómino, erípiat eum: * salvum fáciat eum, quóniam vult eum.
verses.eng: 21:9 He hoped in the Lord, let him deliver him: * let him save him, seeing he delighteth in him.

verses.lat: 21:10 Quóniam tu es, qui extraxísti me de ventre: * spes mea ab ubéribus matris meæ. In te projéctus sum ex útero:
verses.eng: 21:10 For thou art he that hast drawn me out of the womb: * my hope from the breasts of my mother. I was cast upon thee from the womb.

verses.lat: 21:11 De ventre matris meæ Deus meus es tu, * ne discésseris a me:
verses.eng: 21:11 From my mother’s womb thou art my God, * depart not from me.

verses.lat: 21:12 Quóniam tribulátio próxima est: * quóniam non est qui ádjuvet.
verses.eng: 21:12 For tribulation is very near: * for there is none to help me.

verses.lat: 21:13 Circumdedérunt me vítuli multi: * tauri pingues obsedérunt me.
verses.eng: 21:13 Many calves have surrounded me: * fat bulls have besieged me.

verses.lat: 21:14 Aperuérunt super me os suum, * sicut leo rápiens et rúgiens.
verses.eng: 21:14 They have opened their mouths against me, * as a lion ravening and roaring.

verses.lat: 21:15 Sicut aqua effúsus sum: * et dispérsa sunt ómnia ossa mea.
verses.eng: 21:15 I am poured out like water; * and all my bones are scattered.

verses.lat: 21:15 Factum est cor meum tamquam cera liquéscens * in médio ventris mei.
verses.eng: 21:15 My heart is become like wax melting * in the midst of my bowels.

verses.lat: 21:16 Áruit tamquam testa virtus mea, et lingua mea adhǽsit fáucibus meis: * et in púlverem mortis deduxísti me.
verses.eng: 21:16 My strength is dried up like a potsherd, and my tongue hath cleaved to my jaws: * and thou hast brought me down into the dust of death.

verses.lat: 21:17 Quóniam circumdedérunt me canes multi: * concílium malignántium obsédit me.
verses.eng: 21:17 For many dogs have encompassed me: * the council of the malignant hath besieged me.

verses.lat: 21:17 Fodérunt manus meas et pedes meos: * dinumeravérunt ómnia ossa mea.
verses.eng: 21:17 They have dug my hands and feet. * They have numbered all my bones.

verses.lat: 21:18 Ipsi vero consideravérunt et inspexérunt me: * divisérunt sibi vestiménta mea, et super vestem meam misérunt sortem.
verses.eng: 21:18 And they have looked and stared upon me. * They parted my garments amongst them; and upon my vesture they cast lots.

verses.lat: 21:20 Tu autem, Dómine, ne elongáveris auxílium tuum a me: * ad defensiónem meam cónspice.
verses.eng: 21:20 But thou, O Lord, remove not thy help to a distance from me; * look towards my defence.

verses.lat: 21:21 Érue a frámea, Deus, ánimam meam: * et de manu canis únicam meam:
verses.eng: 21:21 Deliver, O God, my soul from the sword: * my only one from the hand of the dog.

verses.lat: 21:22 Salva me ex ore leónis: * et a córnibus unicórnium humilitátem meam.
verses.eng: 21:22 Save me from the lion’s mouth; * and my lowness from the horns of the unicorns.

verses.lat: 21:23 Narrábo nomen tuum frátribus meis: * in médio ecclésiæ laudábo te.
verses.eng: 21:23 I will declare thy name to my brethren: * in the midst of the church will I praise thee.

verses.lat: 21:24 Qui timétis Dóminum, laudáte eum: * univérsum semen Jacob, glorificáte eum.
verses.eng: 21:24 Ye that fear the Lord, praise him: * all ye the seed of Jacob, glorify him.

verses.lat: 21:25 Tímeat eum omne semen Israël: * quóniam non sprevit, neque despéxit deprecatiónem páuperis:
verses.eng: 21:25 Let all the seed of Israel fear him: * because he hath not slighted nor despised the supplication of the poor man.

verses.lat: 21:25 Nec avértit fáciem suam a me: * et cum clamárem ad eum, exaudívit me.
verses.eng: 21:25 Neither hath he turned away his face from me: * and when I cried to him he heard me.

verses.lat: 21:26 Apud te laus mea in ecclésia magna: * vota mea reddam in conspéctu timéntium eum.
verses.eng: 21:26 With thee is my praise in a great church: * I will pay my vows in the sight of them that fear him.

verses.lat: 21:27 Edent páuperes, et saturabúntur: et laudábunt Dóminum qui requírunt eum: * vivent corda eórum in sǽculum sǽculi.
verses.eng: 21:27 The poor shall eat and shall be filled: and they shall praise the Lord that seek him: * their hearts shall live for ever and ever.

verses.lat: 21:28 Reminiscéntur et converténtur ad Dóminum * univérsi fines terræ:
verses.eng: 21:28 All the ends of the earth * shall remember, and shall be converted to the Lord:

verses.lat: 21:28 Et adorábunt in conspéctu ejus * univérsæ famíliæ géntium.
verses.eng: 21:28 And all the kindreds of the Gentiles * shall adore in his sight.

verses.lat: 21:29 Quóniam Dómini est regnum: * et ipse dominábitur géntium.
verses.eng: 21:29 For the kingdom is the Lord’s; * and he shall have dominion over the nations.

verses.lat: 21:30 Manducavérunt et adoravérunt omnes pingues terræ: * in conspéctu ejus cadent omnes qui descéndunt in terram.
verses.eng: 21:30 All the fat ones of the earth have eaten and have adored: * all they that go down to the earth shall fall before him.

verses.lat: 21:31 Et ánima mea illi vivet: * et semen meum sérviet ipsi.
verses.eng: 21:31 And to him my soul shall live: * and my seed shall serve him.

verses.lat: 21:32 Annuntiábitur Dómino generátio ventúra: * et annuntiábunt cæli justítiam ejus pópulo qui nascétur, quem fecit Dóminus.
verses.eng: 21:32 There shall be declared to the Lord a generation to come: * and the heavens shall shew forth his justice to a people that shall be born, which the Lord hath made.

ant_tertia.label: Antíphona
ant_tertia.lat: Éxcita, Dómine, * poténtiam tuam, ut salvos fácias nos.
ant_tertia.eng: Stir up thy might, O Lord, * and come to save us.

verses.lat: 79:2 Qui regis Israël, inténde: * qui dedúcis velut ovem Joseph.
verses.eng: 79:2 Give ear, O thou that rulest Israel: * thou that leadest Joseph like a sheep.

verses.lat: 79:2 Qui sedes super Chérubim, * manifestáre coram Éphraim, Bénjamin, et Manásse.
verses.eng: 79:2 Thou that sittest upon the cherubims, * shine forth before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasses.

verses.lat: 79:3 Éxcita poténtiam tuam, et veni, * ut salvos fácias nos.
verses.eng: 79:3 Stir up thy might, and come * to save us.

verses.lat: 79:4 Deus, convérte nos: * et osténde fáciem tuam, et salvi érimus.
verses.eng: 79:4 Convert us, O God: * and shew us thy face, and we shall be saved.

verses.lat: 79:5 Dómine, Deus virtútum, * quoúsque irascéris super oratiónem servi tui?
verses.eng: 79:5 O Lord God of hosts, * how long wilt thou be angry against the prayer of thy servant?

verses.lat: 79:6 Cibábis nos pane lacrimárum: * et potum dabis nobis in lácrimis in mensúra?
verses.eng: 79:6 How long wilt thou feed us with the bread of tears: * and give us for our drink tears in measure?

verses.lat: 79:7 Posuísti nos in contradictiónem vicínis nostris: * et inimíci nostri subsannavérunt nos.
verses.eng: 79:7 Thou hast made us to be a contradiction to our neighbours: * and our enemies have scoffed at us.

verses.lat: 79:8 Deus virtútum, convérte nos: * et osténde fáciem tuam, et salvi érimus.
verses.eng: 79:8 O God of hosts, convert us: * and shew thy face, and we shall be saved.

verses.lat: 79:9 Víneam de Ægýpto transtulísti: * ejecísti gentes, et plantásti eam.
verses.eng: 79:9 Thou hast brought a vineyard out of Egypt: * thou hast cast out the Gentiles and planted it.

verses.lat: 79:10 Dux itíneris fuísti in conspéctu ejus: * plantásti radíces ejus, et implévit terram.
verses.eng: 79:10 Thou wast the guide of its journey in its sight: * thou plantedst the roots thereof, and it filled the land.

verses.lat: 79:11 Opéruit montes umbra ejus: * et arbústa ejus cedros Dei.
verses.eng: 79:11 The shadow of it covered the hills: * and the branches thereof the cedars of God.

verses.lat: 79:12 Exténdit pálmites suos usque ad mare: * et usque ad flumen propágines ejus.
verses.eng: 79:12 It stretched forth its branches unto the sea, * and its boughs unto the river.

verses.lat: 79:13 Ut quid destruxísti macériam ejus: * et vindémiant eam omnes, qui prætergrediúntur viam?
verses.eng: 79:13 Why hast thou broken down the hedge thereof, * so that all they who pass by the way do pluck it?

verses.lat: 79:14 Exterminávit eam aper de silva: * et singuláris ferus depástus est eam.
verses.eng: 79:14 The boar out of the wood hath laid it waste: * and a singular wild beast hath devoured it.

verses.lat: 79:15 Deus virtútum, convértere: * réspice de cælo, et vide, et vísita víneam istam.
verses.eng: 79:15 Turn again, O God of hosts, * look down from heaven, and see, and visit this vineyard:

verses.lat: 79:16 Et pérfice eam, quam plantávit déxtera tua: * et super fílium hóminis, quem confirmásti tibi.
verses.eng: 79:16 And perfect the same which thy right hand hath planted: * and upon the son of man whom thou hast confirmed for thyself.

verses.lat: 79:17 Incénsa igni, et suffóssa * ab increpatióne vultus tui períbunt.
verses.eng: 79:17 Things set on fire and dug down * shall perish at the rebuke of thy countenance.

verses.lat: 79:18 Fiat manus tua super virum déxteræ tuæ: * et super fílium hóminis, quem confirmásti tibi.
verses.eng: 79:18 Let thy hand be upon the man of thy right hand: * and upon the son of man whom thou hast confirmed for thyself.

verses.lat: 79:19 Et non discédimus a te, vivificábis nos: * et nomen tuum invocábimus.
verses.eng: 79:19 And we depart not from thee, thou shalt quicken us: * and we will call upon thy name.

verses.lat: 79:20 Dómine, Deus virtútum, convérte nos: * et osténde fáciem tuam, et salvi érimus.
verses.eng: 79:20 O Lord God of hosts, convert us: * and shew thy face, and we shall be saved.

verses.lat: 81:1 Deus stetit in synagóga deórum: * in médio autem deos dijúdicat.
verses.eng: 81:1 God hath stood in the congregation of gods: * and being in the midst of them he judgeth gods.

verses.lat: 81:2 Úsquequo judicátis iniquitátem: * et fácies peccatórum súmitis?
verses.eng: 81:2 How long will you judge unjustly: * and accept the persons of the wicked?

verses.lat: 81:3 Judicáte egéno, et pupíllo: * húmilem, et páuperem justificáte.
verses.eng: 81:3 Judge for the needy and fatherless: * do justice to the humble and the poor.

verses.lat: 81:4 Erípite páuperem: * et egénum de manu peccatóris liberáte.
verses.eng: 81:4 Rescue the poor; * and deliver the needy out of the hand of the sinner.

verses.lat: 81:5 Nesciérunt, neque intellexérunt, in ténebris ámbulant: * movebúntur ómnia fundaménta terræ.
verses.eng: 81:5 They have not known nor understood: they walk on in darkness: * all the foundations of the earth shall be moved.

verses.lat: 81:6 Ego dixi: Dii estis, * et fílii Excélsi omnes.
verses.eng: 81:6 I have said: You are gods * and all of you the sons of the most High.

verses.lat: 81:7 Vos autem sicut hómines moriémini: * et sicut unus de princípibus cadétis.
verses.eng: 81:7 But you like men shall die: * and shall fall like one of the princes.

verses.lat: 81:8 Surge, Deus, júdica terram: * quóniam tu hereditábis in ómnibus géntibus.
verses.eng: 81:8 Arise, O God, judge thou the earth: * for thou shalt inherit among all the nations.

ant_sexta.label: Antíphona
ant_sexta.lat: Beáti, qui hábitant * in domo tua, Dómine.
ant_sexta.eng: Blessed are they * that dwell in thy house, O Lord.

verses.lat: 83:2 Quam dilécta tabernácula tua, Dómine virtútum: * concupíscit, et déficit ánima mea in átria Dómini.
verses.eng: 83:2 How lovely are thy tabernacles, O Lord of hosts! * my soul longeth and fainteth for the courts of the Lord.

verses.lat: 83:3 Cor meum, et caro mea * exsultavérunt in Deum vivum.
verses.eng: 83:3 My heart and my flesh * have rejoiced in the living God.

verses.lat: 83:4 Étenim passer invénit sibi domum: * et turtur nidum sibi, ubi ponat pullos suos.
verses.eng: 83:4 For the sparrow hath found herself a house, * and the turtledove a nest for herself where she may lay her young ones:

verses.lat: 83:4 Altária tua, Dómine virtútum: * Rex meus, et Deus meus.
verses.eng: 83:4 Thy altars, O Lord of hosts, * my king and my God.

verses.lat: 83:5 Beáti, qui hábitant in domo tua, Dómine: * in sǽcula sæculórum laudábunt te.
verses.eng: 83:5 Blessed are they that dwell in thy house, O Lord: * they shall praise thee for ever and ever.

verses.lat: 83:6 Beátus vir, cujus est auxílium abs te: * ascensiónes in corde suo dispósuit, in valle lacrimárum in loco, quem pósuit.
verses.eng: 83:6 Blessed is the man whose help is from thee: * in his heart he hath disposed to ascend by steps, in the vale of tears, in the place which he hath set.

verses.lat: 83:8 Étenim benedictiónem dabit legislátor, ibunt de virtúte in virtútem: * vidébitur Deus deórum in Sion.
verses.eng: 83:8 For the lawgiver shall give a blessing, they shall go from virtue to virtue: * the God of gods shall be seen in Sion.

verses.lat: 83:9 Dómine, Deus virtútum, exáudi oratiónem meam: * áuribus pércipe, Deus Jacob.
verses.eng: 83:9 O Lord God of hosts, hear my prayer: * give ear, O God of Jacob.

verses.lat: 83:10 Protéctor noster, áspice, Deus: * et réspice in fáciem Christi tui:
verses.eng: 83:10 Behold, O God our protector: * and look on the face of thy Christ.

verses.lat: 83:11 Quia mélior est dies una in átriis tuis, * super míllia.
verses.eng: 83:11 For better is one day in thy courts * above thousands.

verses.lat: 83:11 Elégi abjéctus esse in domo Dei mei: * magis quam habitáre in tabernáculis peccatórum.
verses.eng: 83:11 I have chosen to be an abject in the house of my God, * rather than to dwell in the tabernacles of sinners.
