verses.lat: 68:12 Et pósui vestiméntum meum cilícium: * et factus sum illis in parábolam.
verses.eng: 68:12 And I made haircloth my garment: * and I became a byword to them.

verses.lat: 68:13 Advérsum me loquebántur, qui sedébant in porta: * et in me psallébant qui bibébant vinum.
verses.eng: 68:13 They that sat in the gate spoke against me: * and they that drank wine made me their song.

verses.lat: 68:13 Ego vero oratiónem meam ad te, Dómine: * tempus benepláciti, Deus.
verses.eng: 68:13 But as for me, my prayer is to thee, O Lord; * for the time of thy good pleasure, O God.

matutinum.psalm8.antiphonLat: Salvum me fac, * Deus, quóniam intravérunt aquæ usque ad ánimam meam.
matutinum.psalm8.antiphonEng: Save me, O God * for the waters are come in even unto my soul.

matutinum.psalm9.label: Psalmus 68 (14-29)

verses.lat: 68:14 In multitúdine misericórdiæ tuæ exáudi me, * in veritáte salútis tuæ:
verses.eng: 68:14 In the multitude of thy mercy hear me, * in the truth of thy salvation.

verses.lat: 68:15 Éripe me de luto, ut non infígar: * líbera me ab iis, qui odérunt me, et de profúndis aquárum.
verses.eng: 68:15 Draw me out of the mire, that I may not stick fast: * deliver me from them that hate me, and out of the deep waters.

verses.lat: 68:16 Non me demérgat tempéstas aquæ, neque absórbeat me profúndum: * neque úrgeat super me púteus os suum.
verses.eng: 68:16 Let not the tempest of water drown me, nor the deep swallow me up: * and let not the pit shut her mouth upon me.

verses.lat: 68:17 Exáudi me, Dómine, quóniam benígna est misericórdia tua: * secúndum multitúdinem miseratiónum tuárum réspice in me.
verses.eng: 68:17 Hear me, O Lord, for thy mercy is kind; * look upon me according to the multitude of thy tender mercies.

verses.lat: 68:18 Et ne avértas fáciem tuam a púero tuo: * quóniam tríbulor, velóciter exáudi me.
verses.eng: 68:18 And turn not away thy face from thy servant: * for I am in trouble, hear me speedily.

verses.lat: 68:19 Inténde ánimæ meæ, et líbera eam: * propter inimícos meos éripe me.
verses.eng: 68:19 Attend to my soul, and deliver it: * save me because of my enemies.

verses.lat: 68:20 Tu scis impropérium meum, et confusiónem meam, * et reveréntiam meam.
verses.eng: 68:20 Thou knowest my reproach, and my confusion, * and my shame.

verses.lat: 68:21 In conspéctu tuo sunt omnes qui tríbulant me: * impropérium exspectávit cor meum, et misériam.
verses.eng: 68:21 In thy sight are all they that afflict me; * my heart hath expected reproach and misery.

verses.lat: 68:21 Et sustínui qui simul contristarétur, et non fuit: * et qui consolarétur, et non invéni.
verses.eng: 68:21 And I looked for one that would grieve together with me, * but there was none: and for one that would comfort me, and I found none.

verses.lat: 68:22 Et dedérunt in escam meam fel: * et in siti mea potavérunt me acéto.
verses.eng: 68:22 And they gave me gall for my food, * and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.

verses.lat: 68:23 Fiat mensa eórum coram ipsis in láqueum, * et in retributiónes, et in scándalum.
verses.eng: 68:23 Let their table become as a snare before them, * and a recompense, and a stumblingblock.

verses.lat: 68:24 Obscuréntur óculi eórum ne vídeant: * et dorsum eórum semper incúrva.
verses.eng: 68:24 Let their eyes be darkened that they see not; * and their back bend thou down always.

verses.lat: 68:25 Effúnde super eos iram tuam: * et furor iræ tuæ comprehéndat eos.
verses.eng: 68:25 Pour out thy indignation upon them: * and let thy wrathful anger take hold of them.

verses.lat: 68:26 Fiat habitátio eórum desérta: * et in tabernáculis eórum non sit qui inhábitet.
verses.eng: 68:26 Let their habitation be made desolate: * and let there be none to dwell in their tabernacles.

verses.lat: 68:27 Quóniam quem tu percussísti, persecúti sunt: * et super dolórem vúlnerum meórum addidérunt.
verses.eng: 68:27 Because they have persecuted him whom thou hast smitten; * and they have added to the grief of my wounds.

verses.lat: 68:28 Appóne iniquitátem super iniquitátem eórum: * et non intrent in justítiam tuam.
verses.eng: 68:28 Add thou iniquity upon their iniquity: * and let them not come into thy justice.

verses.lat: 68:29 Deleántur de libro vivéntium: * et cum justis non scribántur.
verses.eng: 68:29 Let them be blotted out of the book of the living; * and with the just let them not be written.

matutinum.psalm9.antiphonLat: Propter inimícos meos * éripe me, Dómine.
matutinum.psalm9.antiphonEng: O Lord, save me * from my enemies.

matutinum.psalm10.label: Psalmus 68 (30-37)

verses.lat: 68:30 Ego sum pauper et dolens: * salus tua, Deus, suscépit me.
verses.eng: 68:30 I am poor and sorrowful: * thy salvation, O God, hath set me up.

verses.lat: 68:31 Laudábo nomen Dei cum cántico: * et magnificábo eum in laude:
verses.eng: 68:31 I will praise the name of God with a canticle: * and I will magnify him with praise.

verses.lat: 68:32 Et placébit Deo super vítulum novéllum: * córnua producéntem et úngulas.
verses.eng: 68:32 And it shall please God better than a young calf, * that bringeth forth horns and hoofs.

verses.lat: 68:33 Vídeant páuperes et læténtur: * quǽrite Deum, et vivet ánima vestra.
verses.eng: 68:33 Let the poor see and rejoice: * seek ye God, and your soul shall live.

verses.lat: 68:34 Quóniam exaudívit páuperes Dóminus: * et vinctos suos non despéxit.
verses.eng: 68:34 For the Lord hath heard the poor: * and hath not despised his prisoners.

verses.lat: 68:35 Laudent illum cæli et terra, * mare et ómnia reptília in eis.
verses.eng: 68:35 Let the heavens and the earth praise him; * the sea, and every thing that creepeth therein.

verses.lat: 68:36 Quóniam Deus salvam fáciet Sion: * et ædificabúntur civitátes Juda.
verses.eng: 68:36 For God will save Sion, * and the cities of Juda shall be built up.

verses.lat: 68:36 Et inhabitábunt ibi, * et hereditáte acquírent eam.
verses.eng: 68:36 And they shall dwell there, * and acquire it by inheritance.

verses.lat: 68:37 Et semen servórum ejus possidébit eam: * et qui díligunt nomen ejus, habitábunt in ea.
verses.eng: 68:37 And the seed of his servants shall possess it; * and they that love his name shall dwell therein.

matutinum.psalm10.antiphonLat: Quǽrite Dóminum, * et vivet ánima vestra.
matutinum.psalm10.antiphonEng: Look for the Lord * and your soul shall live.

vesperae.psalm1.label: Psalmus 132
vesperae.psalm1.antiphonLat: Ecce quam bonum * et quam jucúndum habitáre fratres in unum.
vesperae.psalm1.antiphonEng: Behold how good * and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity.

verses.lat: 132:1 Ecce quam bonum et quam jucúndum, * habitáre fratres in unum:
verses.eng: 132:1 Behold how good and how pleasant it is * for brethren to dwell together in unity:

verses.lat: 132:2 Sicut unguéntum in cápite, * quod descéndit in barbam, barbam Aaron,
verses.eng: 132:2 Like the precious ointment on the head, * that ran down upon the beard, the beard of Aaron,

verses.lat: 132:2 Quod descéndit in oram vestiménti ejus: * sicut ros Hermon, qui descéndit in montem Sion.
verses.eng: 132:2 Which ran down to the skirt of his garment: * as the dew of Hermon, which descendeth upon mount Sion.

verses.lat: 132:3 Quóniam illic mandávit Dóminus benedictiónem, * et vitam usque in sǽculum.
verses.eng: 132:3 For there the Lord hath commanded blessing, * and life for evermore.

vesperae.psalm2.label: Psalmus 135(1-9)
vesperae.psalm2.antiphonLat: Confitémini Dómino * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia ejus.
vesperae.psalm2.antiphonEng: Give ye glory to the Lord * for his mercy endureth for ever.

verses.lat: 135:1 Confitémini Dómino quóniam bonus: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia ejus.
verses.eng: 135:1 Praise the Lord, for he is good: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

verses.lat: 135:2 Confitémini Deo deórum: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia ejus.
verses.eng: 135:2 Praise ye the God of gods: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

verses.lat: 135:3 Confitémini Dómino dominórum: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia ejus.
verses.eng: 135:3 Praise ye the Lord of lords: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

verses.lat: 135:4 Qui facit mirabília magna solus: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia ejus.
verses.eng: 135:4 Who alone doth great wonders: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

verses.lat: 135:5 Qui fecit cælos in intelléctu: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia ejus.
verses.eng: 135:5 Who made the heavens in understanding: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

verses.lat: 135:6 Qui firmávit terram super aquas: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia ejus.
verses.eng: 135:6 Who established the earth above the waters: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

verses.lat: 135:7 Qui fecit luminária magna: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia ejus.
verses.eng: 135:7 Who made the great lights: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

verses.lat: 135:8 Solem in potestátem diéi: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia ejus.
verses.eng: 135:8 The sun to rule the day: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

verses.lat: 135:9 Lunam, et stellas in potestátem noctis: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia ejus.
verses.eng: 135:9 The moon and the stars to rule the night: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

vesperae.psalm3.label: Psalmus 135(10-26)
vesperae.psalm3.antiphonLat: Confitémini Dómino * quia in humilitáte nostra memor fuit nostri.
vesperae.psalm3.antiphonEng: Give ye glory to the Lord * for he was mindful of us in our affliction.

verses.lat: 135:10 Qui percússit Ægýptum cum primogénitis eórum: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia ejus.
verses.eng: 135:10 Who smote Egypt with their firstborn: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

verses.lat: 135:11 Qui edúxit Israël de médio eórum: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia ejus.
verses.eng: 135:11 Who brought out Israel from among them: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

verses.lat: 135:12 In manu poténti, et brácchio excélso: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia ejus.
verses.eng: 135:12 With a mighty hand and with a stretched out arm: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

verses.lat: 135:13 Qui divísit Mare Rubrum in divisiónes: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia ejus.
verses.eng: 135:13 Who divided the Red sea into parts: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

verses.lat: 135:14 Et edúxit Israël per médium ejus: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia ejus.
verses.eng: 135:14 And brought out Israel through the midst thereof: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

verses.lat: 135:15 Et excússit Pharaónem, et virtútem ejus in Mari Rubro: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia ejus.
verses.eng: 135:15 And overthrew Pharao and his host in the Red sea: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

verses.lat: 135:16 Qui tradúxit pópulum suum per desértum: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia ejus.
verses.eng: 135:16 Who led his people through the desert: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

verses.lat: 135:17 Qui percússit reges magnos: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia ejus.
verses.eng: 135:17 Who smote great kings: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

verses.lat: 135:18 Et occídit reges fortes: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia ejus.
verses.eng: 135:18 And slew strong kings: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

verses.lat: 135:19 Sehon, regem Amorrhæórum: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia ejus.
verses.eng: 135:19 Sehon king of the Amorrhites: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

verses.lat: 135:20 Et Og, regem Basan: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia ejus.
verses.eng: 135:20 And Og king of Basan: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

verses.lat: 135:21 Et dedit terram eórum hereditátem: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia ejus.
verses.eng: 135:21 And he gave their land for an inheritance: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

verses.lat: 135:22 Hereditátem Israël, servo suo: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia ejus.
verses.eng: 135:22 For an inheritance to his servant Israel: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

verses.lat: 135:23 Quia in humilitáte nostra memor fuit nostri: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia ejus.
verses.eng: 135:23 For he was mindful of us in our affliction: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

verses.lat: 135:24 Et redémit nos ab inimícis nostris: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia ejus.
verses.eng: 135:24 And he redeemed us from our enemies: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

verses.lat: 135:25 Qui dat escam omni carni: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia ejus.
verses.eng: 135:25 Who giveth food to all flesh: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

verses.lat: 135:26 Confitémini Deo cæli: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia ejus.
verses.eng: 135:26 Give glory to the God of heaven: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

verses.lat: 135:26 Confitémini Dómino dominórum: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia ejus.
verses.eng: 135:26 Give glory to the Lord of lords: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

vesperae.psalm4.label: Psalmus 136
vesperae.psalm4.antiphonLat: Adhǽreat lingua mea * fáucibus meis, si non memínero tui Jerúsalem.
vesperae.psalm4.antiphonEng: Let my tongue cleave to my jaws * if I do not remember thee, Jerusalem.

verses.lat: 136:1 Super flúmina Babylónis, illic sédimus et flévimus: * cum recordarémur Sion:
verses.eng: 136:1 Upon the rivers of Babylon, there we sat and wept: * when we remembered Sion:

verses.lat: 136:2 In salícibus in médio ejus, * suspéndimus órgana nostra.
verses.eng: 136:2 On the willows in the midst thereof * we hung up our instruments.

verses.lat: 136:3 Quia illic interrogavérunt nos, qui captívos duxérunt nos, * verba cantiónum:
verses.eng: 136:3 For there they that led us into captivity required of us * the words of songs.

verses.lat: 136:3 Et qui abduxérunt nos: * Hymnum cantáte nobis de cánticis Sion.
verses.eng: 136:3 And they that carried us away, said: * Sing ye to us a hymn of the songs of Sion.

verses.lat: 136:4 Quómodo cantábimus cánticum Dómini * in terra aliéna?
verses.eng: 136:4 How shall we sing the song of the Lord * in a strange land?

verses.lat: 136:5 Si oblítus fúero tui, Jerúsalem, * oblivióni detur déxtera mea.
verses.eng: 136:5 If I forget thee, O Jerusalem, * let my right hand be forgotten.

verses.lat: 136:6 Adhǽreat lingua mea fáucibus meis, * si non memínero tui:
verses.eng: 136:6 Let my tongue cleave to my jaws, * if I do not remember thee:

verses.lat: 136:6 Si non proposúero Jerúsalem, * in princípio lætítiæ meæ.
verses.eng: 136:6 If I make not Jerusalem * the beginning of my joy.

verses.lat: 136:7 Memor esto, Dómine, filiórum Edom, * in die Jerúsalem:
verses.eng: 136:7 Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom, * in the day of Jerusalem:

verses.lat: 136:7 Qui dicunt: Exinaníte, exinaníte * usque ad fundaméntum in ea.
verses.eng: 136:7 Who say: Rase it, rase it, * even to the foundation thereof.

verses.lat: 136:8 Fília Babylónis mísera: * beátus, qui retríbuet tibi retributiónem tuam, quam retribuísti nobis.
verses.eng: 136:8 O daughter of Babylon, miserable: * blessed shall he be who shall repay thee thy payment which thou hast paid us.

verses.lat: 136:9 Beátus, qui tenébit, * et allídet párvulos tuos ad petram.
verses.eng: 136:9 Blessed be he that shall take * and dash thy little ones against the rock.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Ecce quam bonum * et quam jucúndum habitáre fratres in unum.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Behold how good * and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Confitémini Dómino * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia ejus.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Give ye glory to the Lord * for his mercy endureth for ever.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Confitémini Dómino * quia in humilitáte nostra memor fuit nostri.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Give ye glory to the Lord * for he was mindful of us in our affliction.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Adhǽreat lingua mea * fáucibus meis, si non memínero tui Jerúsalem.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.eng: Let my tongue cleave to my jaws * if I do not remember thee, Jerusalem.

vesperae.psalm5.label: Psalmus 137
vesperae.psalm5.antiphonLat: Confitébor * nómini tuo, Dómine, super misericórdia et veritáte tua.
vesperae.psalm5.antiphonEng: I will give glory * to thy name, for thy mercy, and for thy truth.

verses.lat: 137:1 Confitébor tibi, Dómine, in toto corde meo: * quóniam audísti verba oris mei.
verses.eng: 137:1 I will praise thee, O Lord, with my whole heart: * for thou hast heard the words of my mouth.

verses.lat: 137:2 In conspéctu Angelórum psallam tibi: * adorábo ad templum sanctum tuum, et confitébor nómini tuo.
verses.eng: 137:2 I will sing praise to thee in the sight of the Angels: * I will worship towards thy holy temple, and I will give glory to thy name.

verses.lat: 137:3 Super misericórdia tua, et veritáte tua: * quóniam magnificásti super omne, nomen sanctum tuum.
verses.eng: 137:3 For thy mercy, and for thy truth: * for thou hast magnified thy holy name

verses.lat: 137:4 In quacúmque die invocávero te, exáudi me: * multiplicábis in ánima mea virtútem.
verses.eng: 137:4 In what day soever I shall call upon thee, hear me: * thou shalt multiply strength in my soul.

verses.lat: 137:5 Confiteántur tibi, Dómine, omnes reges terræ: * quia audiérunt ómnia verba oris tui:
verses.eng: 137:5 May all the kings of the earth give glory to thee: * for they have heard all the words of thy mouth.

verses.lat: 137:6 Et cantent in viis Dómini: * quóniam magna est glória Dómini.
verses.eng: 137:6 And let them sing in the ways of the Lord: * for great is the glory of the Lord.

verses.lat: 137:7 Quóniam excélsus Dóminus, et humília réspicit: * et alta a longe cognóscit.
verses.eng: 137:7 For the Lord is high, and looketh on the low: * and the high he knoweth afar off.

verses.lat: 137:8 Si ambulávero in médio tribulatiónis, vivificábis me: * et super iram inimicórum meórum extendísti manum tuam, et salvum me fecit déxtera tua.
verses.eng: 137:8 If I shall walk in the midst of tribulation, thou wilt quicken me: * and thou hast stretched forth thy hand against the wrath of my enemies: and thy right hand hath saved me.

verses.lat: 137:9 Dóminus retríbuet pro me: * Dómine, misericórdia tua in sǽculum: ópera mánuum tuárum ne despícias.
verses.eng: 137:9 The Lord will repay for me: * thy mercy, O Lord, endureth for ever: O despise not the works of thy hands.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Confitébor * nómini tuo, Dómine, super misericórdia et veritáte tua.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.eng: I will give glory * to thy name, for thy mercy, and for thy truth.

ant_prima.label: Antíphona
ant_prima.lat: In loco páscuæ * ibi Dóminus me collocávit.
ant_prima.eng: The Lord hath set me * in a place of pasture.

verses.lat: 22:1 Dóminus regit me, et nihil mihi déerit: * in loco páscuæ ibi me collocávit.
verses.eng: 22:1 The Lord ruleth me: and I shall want nothing. * He hath set me in a place of pasture.

verses.lat: 22:2 Super aquam refectiónis educávit me: * ánimam meam convértit.
verses.eng: 22:2 He hath brought me up, on the water of refreshment: * he hath converted my soul.

verses.lat: 22:3 Dedúxit me super sémitas justítiæ, * propter nomen suum.
verses.eng: 22:3 He hath led me on the paths of justice, * for his own name’s sake.

verses.lat: 22:4 Nam, et si ambulávero in médio umbræ mortis, non timébo mala: * quóniam tu mecum es.
verses.eng: 22:4 For though I should walk in the midst of the shadow of death, I will fear no evils, * for thou art with me.

verses.lat: 22:4 Virga tua, et báculus tuus: * ipsa me consoláta sunt.
verses.eng: 22:4 Thy rod and thy staff, * they have comforted me.

verses.lat: 22:5 Parásti in conspéctu meo mensam, * advérsus eos, qui tríbulant me.
verses.eng: 22:5 Thou hast prepared a table before me * against them that afflict me.

verses.lat: 22:5 Impinguásti in óleo caput meum: * et calix meus inébrians quam præclárus est!
verses.eng: 22:5 Thou hast anointed my head with oil; * and my chalice which inebriateth me, how goodly is it!

verses.lat: 22:6 Et misericórdia tua subsequétur me * ómnibus diébus vitæ meæ:
verses.eng: 22:6 And thy mercy will follow me * all the days of my life.

verses.lat: 22:6 Et ut inhábitem in domo Dómini, * in longitúdinem diérum.
verses.eng: 22:6 And that I may dwell in the house of the Lord * unto length of days.

verses.lat: 71:2 Deus, judícium tuum regi da: * et justítiam tuam fílio regis:
verses.eng: 71:2 Give to the king thy judgment, O God: * and to the king’s son thy justice:

verses.lat: 71:2 Judicáre pópulum tuum in justítia, * et páuperes tuos in judício.
verses.eng: 71:2 To judge thy people with justice, * and thy poor with judgment.

verses.lat: 71:3 Suscípiant montes pacem pópulo: * et colles justítiam.
verses.eng: 71:3 Let the mountains receive peace for the people: * and the hills justice.

verses.lat: 71:4 Judicábit páuperes pópuli, et salvos fáciet fílios páuperum: * et humiliábit calumniatórem.
verses.eng: 71:4 He shall judge the poor of the people, and he shall save the children of the poor: * and he shall humble the oppressor.

verses.lat: 71:5 Et permanébit cum sole, et ante lunam, * in generatióne et generatiónem.
verses.eng: 71:5 And he shall continue with the sun, and before the moon, * throughout all generations.

verses.lat: 71:6 Descéndet sicut plúvia in vellus: * et sicut stillicídia stillántia super terram.
verses.eng: 71:6 He shall come down like rain upon the fleece; * and as showers falling gently upon the earth.

verses.lat: 71:7 Oriétur in diébus ejus justítia, et abundántia pacis: * donec auferátur luna.
verses.eng: 71:7 In his days shall justice spring up, and abundance of peace, * till the moon be taken away.

verses.lat: 71:8 Et dominábitur a mari usque ad mare: * et a flúmine usque ad términos orbis terrárum.
verses.eng: 71:8 And he shall rule from sea to sea, * and from the river unto the ends of the earth.

verses.lat: 71:9 Coram illo prócident Æthíopes: * et inimíci ejus terram lingent.
verses.eng: 71:9 Before him the Ethiopians shall fall down: * and his enemies shall lick the ground.

verses.lat: 71:10 Reges Tharsis, et ínsulæ múnera ófferent: * reges Árabum et Saba dona addúcent.
verses.eng: 71:10 The kings of Tharsis and the islands shall offer presents: * the kings of the Arabians and of Saba shall bring gifts:

verses.lat: 71:11 Et adorábunt eum omnes reges terræ: * omnes gentes sérvient ei:
verses.eng: 71:11 And all kings of the earth shall adore him: * all nations shall serve him.

verses.lat: 71:12 Quia liberábit páuperem a poténte: * et páuperem, cui non erat adjútor.
verses.eng: 71:12 For he shall deliver the poor from the mighty: * and the needy that had no helper.

verses.lat: 71:13 Parcet páuperi et ínopi: * et ánimas páuperum salvas fáciet.
verses.eng: 71:13 He shall spare the poor and needy: * and he shall save the souls of the poor.

verses.lat: 71:14 Ex usúris et iniquitáte rédimet ánimas eórum: * et honorábile nomen eórum coram illo.
verses.eng: 71:14 He shall redeem their souls from usuries and iniquity: * and their names shall be honourable in his sight.

verses.lat: 71:15 Et vivet, et dábitur ei de auro Arábiæ, et adorábunt de ipso semper: * tota die benedícent ei.
verses.eng: 71:15 And he shall live, and to him shall be given of the gold of Arabia, for him they shall always adore: * they shall bless him all the day.

verses.lat: 71:16 Et erit firmaméntum in terra in summis móntium, superextollétur super Líbanum fructus ejus: * et florébunt de civitáte sicut fænum terræ.
verses.eng: 71:16 And there shall be a firmament on the earth on the tops of mountains, above Libanus shall the fruit thereof be exalted: * and they of the city shall flourish like the grass of the earth.

verses.lat: 71:17 Sit nomen ejus benedíctum in sǽcula: * ante solem pérmanet nomen ejus.
verses.eng: 71:17 Let his name be blessed for evermore: * his name continueth before the sun.

verses.lat: 71:17 Et benedicéntur in ipso omnes tribus terræ: * omnes gentes magnificábunt eum.
verses.eng: 71:17 And in him shall all the tribes of the earth be blessed: * all nations shall magnify him.

verses.lat: 71:18 Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël, * qui facit mirabília solus:
verses.eng: 71:18 Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, * who alone doth wonderful things.

verses.lat: 71:19 Et benedíctum nomen majestátis ejus in ætérnum: * et replébitur majestáte ejus omnis terra: fiat, fiat.
verses.eng: 71:19 And blessed be the name of his majesty for ever: * and the whole earth shall be filled with his majesty. So be it. So be it.

ant_tertia.label: Antíphona
ant_tertia.lat: Quam bonus * Israël Deus, his, qui recto sunt corde.
ant_tertia.eng: How good is God * to Israel, to them that are of a right heart!

verses.lat: 72:1 Quam bonus Israël Deus, * his, qui recto sunt corde!
verses.eng: 72:1 How good is God to Israel, * to them that are of a right heart!

verses.lat: 72:2 Mei autem pæne moti sunt pedes: * pæne effúsi sunt gressus mei.
verses.eng: 72:2 But my feet were almost moved; * my steps had wellnigh slipped.

verses.lat: 72:3 Quia zelávi super iníquos, * pacem peccatórum videns.
verses.eng: 72:3 Because I had a zeal on occasion of the wicked, * seeing the prosperity of sinners.

verses.lat: 72:4 Quia non est respéctus morti eórum: * et firmaméntum in plaga eórum.
verses.eng: 72:4 For there is no regard to their death, * nor is there strength in their stripes.

verses.lat: 72:5 In labóre hóminum non sunt, * et cum homínibus non flagellabúntur:
verses.eng: 72:5 They are not in the labour of men: * neither shall they be scourged like other men.

verses.lat: 72:6 Ídeo ténuit eos supérbia, * opérti sunt iniquitáte et impietáte sua.
verses.eng: 72:6 Therefore pride hath held them fast: * they are covered with their iniquity and their wickedness.

verses.lat: 72:7 Pródiit quasi ex ádipe iníquitas eórum: * transiérunt in afféctum cordis.
verses.eng: 72:7 Their iniquity hath come forth, as it were from fatness: * they have passed into the affection of the heart.

verses.lat: 72:8 Cogitavérunt, et locúti sunt nequítiam: * iniquitátem in excélso locúti sunt.
verses.eng: 72:8 They have thought and spoken wickedness: * they have spoken iniquity on high.

verses.lat: 72:9 Posuérunt in cælum os suum: * et lingua eórum transívit in terra.
verses.eng: 72:9 They have set their mouth against heaven: * and their tongue hath passed through the earth.

verses.lat: 72:10 Ídeo convertétur pópulus meus hic: * et dies pleni inveniéntur in eis.
verses.eng: 72:10 Therefore will my people return here * and full days shall be found in them.

verses.lat: 72:11 Et dixérunt: Quómodo scit Deus, * et si est sciéntia in excélso?
verses.eng: 72:11 And they said: How doth God know? * and is there knowledge in the most High?

verses.lat: 72:12 Ecce, ipsi peccatóres, et abundántes in sǽculo, * obtinuérunt divítias.
verses.eng: 72:12 Behold these are sinners; and yet abounding in the world * they have obtained riches.

verses.lat: 72:13 Et dixi: Ergo sine causa justificávi cor meum, * et lavi inter innocéntes manus meas:
verses.eng: 72:13 And I said: Then have I in vain justified my heart, * and washed my hands among the innocent.

verses.lat: 72:14 Et fui flagellátus tota die, * et castigátio mea in matutínis.
verses.eng: 72:14 And I have been scourged all the day; * and my chastisement hath been in the mornings.

verses.lat: 72:15 Si dicébam: Narrábo sic: * ecce, natiónem filiórum tuórum reprobávi.
verses.eng: 72:15 If I said: I will speak thus; * behold I should condemn the generation of thy children.

verses.lat: 72:16 Existimábam ut cognóscerem hoc, * labor est ante me:
verses.eng: 72:16 I studied that I might know this thing, * it is a labour in my sight:

verses.lat: 72:17 Donec intrem in Sanctuárium Dei: * et intéllegam in novíssimis eórum.
verses.eng: 72:17 Until I go into the sanctuary of God, * and understand concerning their last ends.

verses.lat: 72:18 Verúmtamen propter dolos posuísti eis: * dejecísti eos dum allevaréntur.
verses.eng: 72:18 But indeed for deceits thou hast put it to them: * when they were lifted up, thou hast cast them down.

verses.lat: 72:19 Quómodo facti sunt in desolatiónem, súbito defecérunt: * periérunt propter iniquitátem suam.
verses.eng: 72:19 How are they brought to desolation? they have suddenly ceased to be: * they have perished by reason of their iniquity.

verses.lat: 72:20 Velut sómnium surgéntium, Dómine, * in civitáte tua imáginem ipsórum ad níhilum rédiges.
verses.eng: 72:20 As the dream of them that awake, O Lord; * so in thy city thou shalt bring their image to nothing.

verses.lat: 72:21 Quia inflammátum est cor meum, et renes mei commutáti sunt: * et ego ad níhilum redáctus sum, et nescívi.
verses.eng: 72:21 For my heart hath been inflamed, and my reins have been changed: * and I am brought to nothing, and I knew not.

verses.lat: 72:23 Ut juméntum factus sum apud te: * et ego semper tecum.
verses.eng: 72:23 I am become as a beast before thee: * and I am always with thee.

verses.lat: 72:24 Tenuísti manum déxteram meam: et in voluntáte tua deduxísti me, * et cum glória suscepísti me.
verses.eng: 72:24 Thou hast held me by my right hand; and by thy will thou hast conducted me, * and with thy glory thou hast received me.

verses.lat: 72:25 Quid enim mihi est in cælo? * et a te quid vólui super terram?
verses.eng: 72:25 For what have I in heaven? * and besides thee what do I desire upon earth?

verses.lat: 72:26 Defécit caro mea, et cor meum: * Deus cordis mei, et pars mea Deus in ætérnum.
verses.eng: 72:26 For thee my flesh and my heart hath fainted away: * thou art the God of my heart, and the God that is my portion for ever.

verses.lat: 72:27 Quia ecce, qui elóngant se a te, períbunt: * perdidísti omnes, qui fornicántur abs te.
verses.eng: 72:27 For behold they that go far from thee shall perish: * thou hast destroyed all them that are disloyal to thee.

verses.lat: 72:28 Mihi autem adhærére Deo bonum est: * pónere in Dómino Deo spem meam:
verses.eng: 72:28 But it is good for me to adhere to my God, * to put my hope in the Lord God:

verses.lat: 72:28 Ut annúntiem omnes prædicatiónes tuas, * in portis fíliæ Sion.
verses.eng: 72:28 That I may declare all thy praises, * in the gates of the daughter of Sion.

ant_sexta.label: Antíphona
ant_sexta.lat: Memor esto * congregatiónis tuæ, Dómine, quam possedísti ab inítio.
ant_sexta.eng: Remember * thy congregation, which thou hast possessed from the beginning.

verses.lat: 73:1 Ut quid, Deus, repulísti in finem: * irátus est furor tuus super oves páscuæ tuæ?
verses.eng: 73:1 O God, why hast thou cast us off unto the end: * why is thy wrath enkindled against the sheep of thy pasture?

verses.lat: 73:2 Memor esto congregatiónis tuæ, * quam possedísti ab inítio.
verses.eng: 73:2 Remember thy congregation, * which thou hast possessed from the beginning.

verses.lat: 73:2 Redemísti virgam hereditátis tuæ: * mons Sion, in quo habitásti in eo.
verses.eng: 73:2 The sceptre of thy inheritance which thou hast redeemed: * mount Sion in which thou hast dwelt.

verses.lat: 73:3 Leva manus tuas in supérbias eórum in finem: * quanta malignátus est inimícus in sancto!
verses.eng: 73:3 Lift up thy hands against their pride unto the end; * see what things the enemy hath done wickedly in the sanctuary.

verses.lat: 73:4 Et gloriáti sunt qui odérunt te: * in médio solemnitátis tuæ.
verses.eng: 73:4 And they that hate thee have made their boasts, * in the midst of thy solemnity.

verses.lat: 73:5 Posuérunt signa sua, signa: * et non cognovérunt sicut in éxitu super summum.
verses.eng: 73:5 They have set up their ensigns for signs, * and they knew not both in the going out and on the highest top.

verses.lat: 73:6 Quasi in silva lignórum secúribus excidérunt jánuas ejus in idípsum: * in secúri et áscia dejecérunt eam.
verses.eng: 73:6 As with axes in a wood of trees, they have cut down at once the gates thereof, * with axe and hatchet they have brought it down.

verses.lat: 73:7 Incendérunt igni Sanctuárium tuum: * in terra polluérunt tabernáculum nóminis tui.
verses.eng: 73:7 They have set fire to thy sanctuary: * they have defiled the dwelling place of thy name on the earth.

verses.lat: 73:8 Dixérunt in corde suo cognátio eórum simul: * Quiéscere faciámus omnes dies festos Dei a terra.
verses.eng: 73:8 They said in their heart, the whole kindred of them together: * Let us abolish all the festival days of God from the land.

verses.lat: 73:9 Signa nostra non vídimus, jam non est prophéta: * et nos non cognóscet ámplius.
verses.eng: 73:9 Our signs we have not seen, there is now no prophet: * and he will know us no more.

verses.lat: 73:10 Úsquequo, Deus, improperábit inimícus: * irrítat adversárius nomen tuum in finem?
verses.eng: 73:10 How long, O God, shall the enemy reproach: * is the adversary to provoke thy name for ever?

verses.lat: 73:11 Ut quid avértis manum tuam, et déxteram tuam, * de médio sinu tuo in finem?
verses.eng: 73:11 Why dost thou turn away thy hand: and thy right hand * out of the midst of thy bosom for ever?

verses.lat: 73:12 Deus autem Rex noster ante sǽcula: * operátus est salútem in médio terræ.
verses.eng: 73:12 But God is our king before ages: * he hath wrought salvation in the midst of the earth.

verses.lat: 73:13 Tu confirmásti in virtúte tua mare: * contribulásti cápita dracónum in aquis.
verses.eng: 73:13 Thou by thy strength didst make the sea firm: * thou didst crush the heads of the dragons in the waters.

verses.lat: 73:14 Tu confregísti cápita dracónis: * dedísti eum escam pópulis Æthíopum.
verses.eng: 73:14 Thou hast broken the heads of the dragon: * thou hast given him to be meat for the people of the Ethiopians.

verses.lat: 73:15 Tu dirupísti fontes, et torréntes: * tu siccásti flúvios Ethan.
verses.eng: 73:15 Thou hast broken up the fountains and the torrents: * thou hast dried up the Ethan rivers.

verses.lat: 73:16 Tuus est dies, et tua est nox: * tu fabricátus es auróram et solem.
verses.eng: 73:16 Thine is the day, and thine is the night: * thou hast made the morning light and the sun.

verses.lat: 73:17 Tu fecísti omnes términos terræ: * æstátem et ver tu plasmásti ea.
verses.eng: 73:17 Thou hast made all the borders of the earth: * the summer and the spring were formed by thee.

verses.lat: 73:18 Memor esto hujus, inimícus improperávit Dómino: * et pópulus insípiens incitávit nomen tuum.
verses.eng: 73:18 Remember this, the enemy hath reproached the Lord: * and a foolish people hath provoked thy name.

verses.lat: 73:19 Ne tradas béstiis ánimas confiténtes tibi, * et ánimas páuperum tuórum ne obliviscáris in finem.
verses.eng: 73:19 Deliver not up to beasts the souls that confess to thee: * and forget not to the end the souls of thy poor.

verses.lat: 73:20 Réspice in testaméntum tuum: * quia repléti sunt, qui obscuráti sunt terræ dómibus iniquitátum.
verses.eng: 73:20 Have regard to thy covenant: * for they that are the obscure of the earth have been filled with dwellings of iniquity.

verses.lat: 73:21 Ne avertátur húmilis factus confúsus: * pauper et inops laudábunt nomen tuum.
verses.eng: 73:21 Let not the humble be turned away with confusion: * the poor and needy shall praise thy name.

verses.lat: 73:22 Exsúrge, Deus, júdica causam tuam: * memor esto improperiórum tuórum, eórum quæ ab insipiénte sunt tota die.
verses.eng: 73:22 Arise, O God, judge thy own cause: * remember thy reproaches with which the foolish man hath reproached thee all the day.

verses.lat: 73:23 Ne obliviscáris voces inimicórum tuórum: * supérbia eórum, qui te odérunt, ascéndit semper.
verses.eng: 73:23 Forget not the voices of thy enemies: * the pride of them that hate thee ascendeth continually.

ant_nona.label: Antíphona
ant_nona.lat: Invocábimus * nomen tuum, Dómine: narrábimus mirabília tua.
ant_nona.eng: We will call * upon thy name O Lord. We will relate thy wondrous works.

verses.lat: 74:2 Confitébimur tibi, Deus: * confitébimur, et invocábimus nomen tuum.
verses.eng: 74:2 We will praise thee, O God: * we will praise, and we will call upon thy name.

verses.lat: 74:3 Narrábimus mirabília tua: * cum accépero tempus, ego justítias judicábo.
verses.eng: 74:3 We will relate thy wondrous works: * when I shall take a time, I will judge justices.

verses.lat: 74:4 Liquefácta est terra, et omnes qui hábitant in ea: * ego confirmávi colúmnas ejus.
verses.eng: 74:4 The earth is melted, and all that dwell therein: * I have established the pillars thereof.

verses.lat: 74:5 Dixi iníquis: Nolíte iníque ágere: * et delinquéntibus: Nolíte exaltáre cornu:
verses.eng: 74:5 I said to the wicked: Do not act wickedly: * and to the sinners: Lift not up the horn.

verses.lat: 74:6 Nolíte extóllere in altum cornu vestrum: * nolíte loqui advérsus Deum iniquitátem.
verses.eng: 74:6 Lift not up your horn on high: * speak not iniquity against God.

verses.lat: 74:7 Quia neque ab Oriénte, neque ab Occidénte, neque a desértis móntibus: * quóniam Deus judex est.
verses.eng: 74:7 For neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the desert hills: * for God is the judge.

verses.lat: 74:8 Hunc humíliat, et hunc exáltat: * quia calix in manu Dómini vini meri plenus misto.
verses.eng: 74:8 One he putteth down, and another he lifteth up: * for in the hand of the Lord there is a cup of strong wine full of mixture.

verses.lat: 74:9 Et inclinávit ex hoc in hoc: verúmtamen fæx ejus non est exinaníta: * bibent omnes peccatóres terræ.
verses.eng: 74:9 And he hath poured it out from this to that: but the dregs thereof are not emptied: * all the sinners of the earth shall drink.

verses.lat: 74:10 Ego autem annuntiábo in sǽculum: * cantábo Deo Jacob.
verses.eng: 74:10 But I will declare for ever: * I will sing to the God of Jacob.

verses.lat: 74:11 Et ómnia córnua peccatórum confríngam: * et exaltabúntur córnua justi.
verses.eng: 74:11 And I will break all the horns of sinners: * but the horns of the just shall be exalted.

verses.lat: 75:2 Notus in Judǽa Deus: * in Israël magnum nomen ejus.
verses.eng: 75:2 In Judea God is known: * his name is great in Israel.

verses.lat: 75:3 Et factus est in pace locus ejus: * et habitátio ejus in Sion.
verses.eng: 75:3 And his place is in peace: * and his abode in Sion:

verses.lat: 75:4 Ibi confrégit poténtias árcuum, * scutum, gládium, et bellum.
verses.eng: 75:4 There hath he broken the powers of bows, * the shield, the sword, and the battle.

verses.lat: 75:5 Illúminans tu mirabíliter a móntibus ætérnis: * turbáti sunt omnes insipiéntes corde.
verses.eng: 75:5 Thou enlightenest wonderfully from the everlasting hills. * All the foolish of heart were troubled.

verses.lat: 75:6 Dormiérunt somnum suum: * et nihil invenérunt omnes viri divitiárum in mánibus suis.
verses.eng: 75:6 They have slept their sleep; * and all the men of riches have found nothing in their hands.

verses.lat: 75:7 Ab increpatióne tua, Deus Jacob, * dormitavérunt qui ascendérunt equos.
verses.eng: 75:7 At thy rebuke, O God of Jacob, * they have all slumbered that mounted on horseback.

verses.lat: 75:8 Tu terríbilis es, et quis resístet tibi? * ex tunc ira tua.
verses.eng: 75:8 Thou art terrible, and who shall resist thee? * from that time thy wrath.

verses.lat: 75:9 De cælo audítum fecísti judícium: * terra trémuit et quiévit,
verses.eng: 75:9 Thou hast caused judgment to be heard from heaven: * the earth trembled and was still,

verses.lat: 75:10 Cum exsúrgeret in judícium Deus, * ut salvos fáceret omnes mansuétos terræ.
verses.eng: 75:10 When God arose in judgment, * to save all the meek of the earth.

verses.lat: 75:11 Quóniam cogitátio hóminis confitébitur tibi: * et relíquiæ cogitatiónis diem festum agent tibi.
verses.eng: 75:11 For the thought of man shall give praise to thee: * and the remainders of the thought shall keep holiday to thee.

verses.lat: 75:12 Vovéte, et réddite Dómino, Deo vestro: * omnes, qui in circúitu ejus affértis múnera.
verses.eng: 75:12 Vow ye, and pay to the Lord your God: * all you that are round about him bring presents.

verses.lat: 75:13 Terríbili et ei qui aufert spíritum príncipum, * terríbili apud reges terræ.
verses.eng: 75:13 To him that is terrible, even to him who taketh away the spirit of princes: * to the terrible with the kings of the earth.

completorium.antiphon.label: Antíphona
completorium.antiphon.lat: Adjútor meus * et liberátor meus esto, Dómine.
completorium.antiphon.eng: Thou art my helper * and my deliverer, O Lord.

verses.lat: 69:2 Deus, in adjutórium meum inténde: * Dómine, ad adjuvándum me festína.
verses.eng: 69:2 O God, come to my assistance; * O Lord, make haste to help me.

verses.lat: 69:3 Confundántur et revereántur, * qui quærunt ánimam meam.
verses.eng: 69:3 Let them be confounded and ashamed * that seek my soul:

verses.lat: 69:4 Avertántur retrórsum, et erubéscant, * qui volunt mihi mala.
verses.eng: 69:4 Let them be turned backward, and blush for shame * that desire evils to me:

verses.lat: 69:4 Avertántur statim erubescéntes, * qui dicunt mihi: Euge, euge.
verses.eng: 69:4 Let them be presently turned away blushing for shame * that say to me: ’T is well, ’t is well.

verses.lat: 69:5 Exsúltent et læténtur in te omnes qui quærunt te, * et dicant semper: Magnificétur Dóminus: qui díligunt salutáre tuum.
verses.eng: 69:5 Let all that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee; * and let such as love thy salvation say always: The Lord be magnified.

verses.lat: 69:6 Ego vero egénus, et pauper sum: * Deus, ádjuva me.
verses.eng: 69:6 But I am needy and poor; * O God, help me.

verses.lat: 69:6 Adjútor meus, et liberátor meus es tu: * Dómine, ne moréris.
verses.eng: 69:6 Thou art my helper and my deliverer: * O Lord, make no delay.

verses.lat: 70:1 In te, Dómine, sperávi, non confúndar in ætérnum: * in justítia tua líbera me, et éripe me.
verses.eng: 70:1 In thee, O Lord, I have hoped, let me never be put to confusion: * deliver me in thy justice, and rescue me.

verses.lat: 70:2 Inclína ad me aurem tuam, * et salva me.
verses.eng: 70:2 Incline thy ear unto me, * and save me.

verses.lat: 70:3 Esto mihi in Deum protectórem, et in locum munítum: * ut salvum me fácias,
verses.eng: 70:3 Be thou unto me a God, a protector, and a place of strength: * that thou mayst make me safe.

verses.lat: 70:3 Quóniam firmaméntum meum, * et refúgium meum es tu.
verses.eng: 70:3 For thou art my firmament * and my refuge.

verses.lat: 70:4 Deus meus, éripe me de manu peccatóris, * et de manu contra legem agéntis et iníqui:
verses.eng: 70:4 Deliver me, O my God, out of the hand of the sinner, * and out of the hand of the transgressor of the law and of the unjust.

verses.lat: 70:5 Quóniam tu es patiéntia mea, Dómine: * Dómine, spes mea a juventúte mea.
verses.eng: 70:5 For thou art my patience, O Lord: * my hope, O Lord, from my youth.

verses.lat: 70:6 In te confirmátus sum ex útero: * de ventre matris meæ tu es protéctor meus.
verses.eng: 70:6 By thee have I been confirmed from the womb: * from my mother’s womb thou art my protector.

verses.lat: 70:7 In te cantátio mea semper: * tamquam prodígium factus sum multis: et tu adjútor fortis.
verses.eng: 70:7 Of thee shall I continually sing: * I am become unto many as a wonder, but thou art a strong helper.

verses.lat: 70:8 Repleátur os meum laude, ut cantem glóriam tuam: * tota die magnitúdinem tuam.
verses.eng: 70:8 Let my mouth be filled with praise, that I may sing thy glory; * thy greatness all the day long.

verses.lat: 70:9 Ne proícias me in témpore senectútis: * cum defécerit virtus mea, ne derelínquas me.
verses.eng: 70:9 Cast me not off in the time of old age: * when my strength shall fail, do not thou forsake me.

verses.lat: 70:10 Quia dixérunt inimíci mei mihi: * et qui custodiébant ánimam meam, consílium fecérunt in unum.
verses.eng: 70:10 For my enemies have spoken against me; * and they that watched my soul have consulted together,

verses.lat: 70:11 Dicéntes: Deus derelíquit eum, persequímini, † et comprehéndite eum: * quia non est qui erípiat.
verses.eng: 70:11 Saying: God hath forsaken him: pursue and take him, * for there is none to deliver him.

verses.lat: 70:12 Deus, ne elongéris a me: * Deus meus, in auxílium meum réspice.
verses.eng: 70:12 O God, be not thou far from me: * O my God, make haste to my help.

verses.lat: 70:13 Confundántur, et defíciant detrahéntes ánimæ meæ: * operiántur confusióne, et pudóre qui quærunt mala mihi.
verses.eng: 70:13 Let them be confounded and come to nothing that detract my soul; * let them be covered with confusion and shame that seek my hurt.

verses.lat: 70:14 Ego autem semper sperábo: * et adíciam super omnem laudem tuam.
verses.eng: 70:14 But I will always hope; * and will add to all thy praise.

verses.lat: 70:15 Os meum annuntiábit justítiam tuam: * tota die salutáre tuum.
verses.eng: 70:15 My mouth shall shew forth thy justice; * thy salvation all the day long.

verses.lat: 70:16 Quóniam non cognóvi litteratúram, † introíbo in poténtias Dómini: * Dómine, memorábor justítiæ tuæ solíus.
verses.eng: 70:16 Because I have not known learning, I will enter into the powers of the Lord: * O Lord, I will be mindful of thy justice alone.

verses.lat: 70:17 Deus, docuísti me a juventúte mea: * et usque nunc pronuntiábo mirabília tua.
verses.eng: 70:17 Thou hast taught me, O God, from my youth: * and till now I will declare thy wonderful works.

verses.lat: 70:18 Et usque in senéctam et sénium: * Deus, ne derelínquas me,
verses.eng: 70:18 And unto old age and grey hairs: * O God, forsake me not,

verses.lat: 70:18 Donec annúntiem brácchium tuum * generatióni omni, quæ ventúra est:
verses.eng: 70:18 Until I shew forth thy arm * to all the generation that is to come:

verses.lat: 70:19 Poténtiam tuam, et justítiam tuam, Deus, † usque in altíssima, quæ fecísti magnália: * Deus, quis símilis tibi?
verses.eng: 70:19 Thy power, and thy justice, O God, even to the highest great things thou hast done: * O God, who is like to thee?

verses.lat: 70:20 Quantas ostendísti mihi tribulatiónes multas et malas: et convérsus vivificásti me: * et de abýssis terræ íterum reduxísti me:
verses.eng: 70:20 How great troubles hast thou shewn me, many and grievous: and turning thou hast brought me to life, * and hast brought me back again from the depths of the earth:

verses.lat: 70:21 Multiplicásti magnificéntiam tuam: * et convérsus consolátus es me.
verses.eng: 70:21 Thou hast multiplied thy magnificence; * and turning to me thou hast comforted me.

verses.lat: 70:22 Nam et ego confitébor tibi in vasis psalmi veritátem tuam: * Deus, psallam tibi in cíthara, Sanctus Israël.
verses.eng: 70:22 For I will also confess to thee thy truth with the instruments of psaltery: * O God, I will sing to thee with the harp,

verses.lat: 70:23 Exsultábunt lábia mea cum cantávero tibi: * et ánima mea, quam redemísti.
verses.eng: 70:23 My lips shall greatly rejoice, when I shall sing to thee; * and my soul which thou hast redeemed.

verses.lat: 70:24 Sed et lingua mea tota die meditábitur justítiam tuam: * cum confúsi et revériti fúerint, qui quærunt mala mihi.
verses.eng: 70:24 Yea and my tongue shall meditate on thy justice all the day; * when they shall be confounded and put to shame that seek evils to me.

tertia.capitulum.label: Capitulum
tertia.capitulum.lat: Sana me, Dómine, et sanábor: salvum me fac, et salvus ero: quóniam laus mea tu es.
tertia.capitulum.eng: Heal me, O Lord, and I shall be healed: save me, and I shall be saved, for Thou art my praise.

responsory_breve_tertia.label: Responsory
responsory_breve_tertia.lat:
℟.br. Sana ánimam meam, * quia peccávi tibi.
℣. Ego dixi: Dómine, miserére mei.
℟. Quia peccávi tibi.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Sana ánimam meam, * quia peccávi tibi.
responsory_breve_tertia.eng:
℟.br. Heal my soul, * for I have sinned against Thee.
℣. I said: O Lord, be Thou merciful to me.
℟. For I have sinned against Thee.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. Heal my soul, * for I have sinned against Thee.

capitulum_sexta.label: Capitulum
capitulum_sexta.lat: Némini quidquam debeátis, nisi ut ínvicem diligátis: qui enim díligit próximum, legem implévit.
capitulum_sexta.eng: Owe no man any thing, but to love one another. For he that loveth his neighbour, hath fulfilled the law.

responsory_breve_sexta.label: Responsory
responsory_breve_sexta.lat:
℟.br. Benedícam Dóminum * in omni témpore.
℣. Semper laus ejus in ore meo.
℟. In omni témpore.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Benedícam Dóminum * in omni témpore.
responsory_breve_sexta.eng:
℟.br. I will bless the Lord * at all times.
℣. His praise shall be always in my mouth.
℟. At all times.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. I will bless the Lord * at all times.

capitulum_nona.label: Capitulum
capitulum_nona.lat: In timóre incolátus vestri témpore conversámini: sciéntes quod non corruptibílibus auro vel argénto redémpti estis, sed pretióso sánguine quasi Agni immaculáti Christi.
capitulum_nona.eng: Converse in fear during the time of your sojourning here. Knowing that you were not redeemed with corruptible things as gold or silver, but with the precious blood of Christ.

responsory_breve_nona.label: Responsory
responsory_breve_nona.lat:
℟.br. Rédime me, Dómine, * et miserére mei.
℣. Pes enim meus stetit in via recta.
℟. Et miserére mei.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Rédime me, Dómine, * et miserére mei.
responsory_breve_nona.eng:
℟.br. Redeem me, O Lord, * and have mercy on me.
℣. For my feet stood in the right way.
℟. And have mercy on me.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. Redeem me, O Lord, * and have mercy on me.

laudes.psalm1.label: Psalmus 97
laudes.psalm1.antiphonEng: Make a joyful noise * before the Lord our King.

verses.lat: 97:1 Cantáte Dómino cánticum novum: * quia mirabília fecit.
verses.eng: 97:1 Sing ye to the Lord a new canticle: * because he hath done wonderful things.

verses.lat: 97:1 Salvávit sibi déxtera ejus: * et brácchium sanctum ejus.
verses.eng: 97:1 His right hand hath wrought for him salvation, * and his arm is holy.

verses.lat: 97:2 Notum fecit Dóminus salutáre suum: * in conspéctu géntium revelávit justítiam suam.
verses.eng: 97:2 The Lord hath made known his salvation: * he hath revealed his justice in the sight of the Gentiles.

verses.lat: 97:3 Recordátus est misericórdiæ suæ, * et veritátis suæ dómui Israël.
verses.eng: 97:3 He hath remembered his mercy * and his truth toward the house of Israel.

verses.lat: 97:3 Vidérunt omnes términi terræ * salutáre Dei nostri.
verses.eng: 97:3 All the ends of the earth have seen * the salvation of our God.

verses.lat: 97:4 Jubiláte Deo, omnis terra: * cantáte, et exsultáte, et psállite.
verses.eng: 97:4 Sing joyfully to God, all the earth; * make melody, rejoice and sing.

verses.lat: 97:5 Psállite Dómino in cíthara, in cíthara et voce psalmi: * in tubis ductílibus, et voce tubæ córneæ.
verses.eng: 97:5 Sing praise to the Lord on the harp, on the harp, and with the voice of a psalm: * with long trumpets, and sound of cornet.

verses.lat: 97:6 Jubiláte in conspéctu regis Dómini: * moveátur mare, et plenitúdo ejus: orbis terrárum, et qui hábitant in eo.
verses.eng: 97:6 Make a joyful noise before the Lord our king: * let the sea be moved and the fulness thereof: the world and they that dwell therein.

verses.lat: 97:8 Flúmina plaudent manu, simul montes exsultábunt a conspéctu Dómini: * quóniam venit judicáre terram.
verses.eng: 97:8 The rivers shall clap their hands, the mountains shall rejoice together at the presence of the Lord: * because he cometh to judge the earth.

verses.lat: 97:9 Judicábit orbem terrárum in justítia, * et pópulos in æquitáte.
verses.eng: 97:9 He shall judge the world with justice, * and the people with equity.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Make a joyful noise * before the Lord our King.

laudes.psalm2.label: Psalmus 89
laudes.psalm2.antiphonEng: Lord, * thou hast been our refuge.

verses.lat: 89:1 Dómine, refúgium factus es nobis: * a generatióne in generatiónem.
verses.eng: 89:1 Lord, thou hast been our refuge * from generation to generation.

verses.lat: 89:2 Priúsquam montes fíerent, aut formarétur terra et orbis: * a sǽculo et usque in sǽculum tu es, Deus.
verses.eng: 89:2 Before the mountains were made, or the earth and the world was formed; * from eternity and to eternity thou art God.

verses.lat: 89:3 Ne avértas hóminem in humilitátem: * et dixísti: Convertímini, fílii hóminum.
verses.eng: 89:3 Turn not man away to be brought low: * and thou hast said: Be converted, O ye sons of men.

verses.lat: 89:4 Quóniam mille anni ante óculos tuos, * tamquam dies hestérna, quæ prætériit,
verses.eng: 89:4 For a thousand years in thy sight * are as yesterday, which is past.

verses.lat: 89:5 Et custódia in nocte, * quæ pro níhilo habéntur, eórum anni erunt.
verses.eng: 89:5 And as a watch in the night, * things that are counted nothing, shall their years be.

verses.lat: 89:6 Mane sicut herba tránseat, mane flóreat, et tránseat: * véspere décidat, indúret et aréscat.
verses.eng: 89:6 In the morning man shall grow up like grass; in the morning he shall flourish and pass away: * in the evening he shall fall, grow dry, and wither.

verses.lat: 89:7 Quia defécimus in ira tua, * et in furóre tuo turbáti sumus.
verses.eng: 89:7 For in thy wrath we have fainted away: * and are troubled in thy indignation.

verses.lat: 89:8 Posuísti iniquitátes nostras in conspéctu tuo: * sǽculum nostrum in illuminatióne vultus tui.
verses.eng: 89:8 Thou hast set our iniquities before thy eyes: * our life in the light of thy countenance.

verses.lat: 89:9 Quóniam omnes dies nostri defecérunt: * et in ira tua defécimus.
verses.eng: 89:9 For all our days are spent; * and in thy wrath we have fainted away.

verses.lat: 89:9 Anni nostri sicut aránea meditabúntur: * dies annórum nostrórum in ipsis, septuagínta anni.
verses.eng: 89:9 Our years shall be considered as a spider: * the days of our years in them are threescore and ten years.

verses.lat: 89:10 Si autem in potentátibus, octogínta anni: * et ámplius eórum, labor et dolor.
verses.eng: 89:10 But if in the strong they be fourscore years: * and what is more of them is labour and sorrow.

verses.lat: 89:10 Quóniam supervénit mansuetúdo: * et corripiémur.
verses.eng: 89:10 For mildness is come upon us: * and we shall be corrected.

verses.lat: 89:11 Quis novit potestátem iræ tuæ: * et præ timóre tuo iram tuam dinumeráre?
verses.eng: 89:11 Who knoweth the power of thy anger, * and for thy fear can number thy wrath?

verses.lat: 89:12 Déxteram tuam sic notam fac: * et erudítos corde in sapiéntia.
verses.eng: 89:12 So make thy right hand known: * and men learned in heart, in wisdom.

verses.lat: 89:13 Convértere, Dómine, úsquequo? * et deprecábilis esto super servos tuos.
verses.eng: 89:13 Return, O Lord, how long? * and be entreated in favour of thy servants.

verses.lat: 89:14 Repléti sumus mane misericórdia tua: * et exsultávimus, et delectáti sumus ómnibus diébus nostris.
verses.eng: 89:14 We are filled in the morning with thy mercy: * and we have rejoiced, and are delighted all our days.

verses.lat: 89:15 Lætáti sumus pro diébus, quibus nos humiliásti: * annis, quibus vídimus mala.
verses.eng: 89:15 We have rejoiced for the days in which thou hast humbled us: * for the years in which we have seen evils.

verses.lat: 89:16 Réspice in servos tuos, et in ópera tua: * et dírige fílios eórum.
verses.eng: 89:16 Look upon thy servants and upon their works: * and direct their children.

verses.lat: 89:17 Et sit splendor Dómini, Dei nostri, super nos, et ópera mánuum nostrárum dírige super nos: * et opus mánuum nostrárum dírige.
verses.eng: 89:17 And let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us: and direct thou the works of our hands over us; * yea, the work of our hands do thou direct.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Lord, * thou hast been our refuge.

laudes.psalm3.label: Psalmus 35
laudes.psalm3.antiphonEng: O Lord, * thy mercy is in heaven.

verses.lat: 35:2 Dixit injústus ut delínquat in semetípso: * non est timor Dei ante óculos ejus.
verses.eng: 35:2 The unjust hath said within himself, that he would sin: * there is no fear of God before his eyes.

verses.lat: 35:3 Quóniam dolóse egit in conspéctu ejus: * ut inveniátur iníquitas ejus ad ódium.
verses.eng: 35:3 For in his sight he hath done deceitfully, * that his iniquity may be found unto hatred.

verses.lat: 35:4 Verba oris ejus iníquitas, et dolus: * nóluit intellégere ut bene ágeret.
verses.eng: 35:4 The words of his mouth are iniquity and guile: * he would not understand that he might do well.

verses.lat: 35:5 Iniquitátem meditátus est in cubíli suo: * ástitit omni viæ non bonæ, malítiam autem non odívit.
verses.eng: 35:5 He hath devised iniquity on his bed, * he hath set himself on every way that is not good: but evil he hath not hated.

verses.lat: 35:6 Dómine, in cælo misericórdia tua: * et véritas tua usque ad nubes.
verses.eng: 35:6 O Lord, thy mercy is in heaven, * and thy truth reacheth even to the clouds.

verses.lat: 35:7 Justítia tua sicut montes Dei: * judícia tua abýssus multa.
verses.eng: 35:7 Thy justice is as the mountains of God, * thy judgments are a great deep.

verses.lat: 35:7 Hómines, et juménta salvábis, Dómine: * quemádmodum multiplicásti misericórdiam tuam, Deus.
verses.eng: 35:7 Men and beasts thou wilt preserve, O Lord: * O how hast thou multiplied thy mercy, O God!

verses.lat: 35:8 Fílii autem hóminum, * in tégmine alárum tuárum sperábunt.
verses.eng: 35:8 But the children of men * shall put their trust under the covert of thy wings.

verses.lat: 35:9 Inebriabúntur ab ubertáte domus tuæ: * et torrénte voluptátis tuæ potábis eos.
verses.eng: 35:9 They shall be inebriated with the plenty of thy house; * and thou shalt make them drink of the torrent of thy pleasure.

verses.lat: 35:10 Quóniam apud te est fons vitæ: * et in lúmine tuo vidébimus lumen.
verses.eng: 35:10 For with thee is the fountain of life; * and in thy light we shall see light.

verses.lat: 35:11 Præténde misericórdiam tuam sciéntibus te, * et justítiam tuam his, qui recto sunt corde.
verses.eng: 35:11 Extend thy mercy to them that know thee, * and thy justice to them that are right in heart.

verses.lat: 35:12 Non véniat mihi pes supérbiæ: * et manus peccatóris non móveat me.
verses.eng: 35:12 Let not the foot of pride come to me, * and let not the hand of the sinner move me.

verses.lat: 35:13 Ibi cecidérunt qui operántur iniquitátem: * expúlsi sunt, nec potuérunt stare.
verses.eng: 35:13 There the workers of iniquity are fallen, * they are cast out, and could not stand.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: O Lord, * thy mercy is in heaven.

laudes.canticle1.label: Canticum 214
laudes.canticle1.antiphonLat: Pópulus meus, * ait Dóminus, bonis meis adimplébitur.
laudes.canticle1.antiphonEng: My people, * said the Lord, shall be filled with good things.

verses.lat: (Canticum Jeremiæ * Jer 31:10-18)
verses.eng: (Canticle of_Jeremias * Jer 31:10-18)

verses.lat: 31:10 Audíte verbum Dómini, gentes, * et annuntiáte in ínsulis, quæ procul sunt,
verses.eng: 31:10 Hear the word of the Lord, O ye nations, * and declare it in the islands that are afar off,

verses.lat: 31:11 Et dícite: Qui dispérsit Israël, congregábit eum: * et custódiet eum sicut pastor gregem suum.
verses.eng: 31:11 And say: He that scattered Israel will gather him: * and he will keep him as the shepherd doth his flock.

verses.lat: 31:12 Redémit enim Dóminus Jacob, * et liberávit eum de manu potentióris.
verses.eng: 31:12 For the Lord hath redeemed Jacob, * and delivered him out of the hand of one that was mightier than he.

verses.lat: 31:13 Et vénient, et laudábunt in monte Sion: * et cónfluent ad bona Dómini,
verses.eng: 31:13 And they shall come, and shall give praise in mount Sion: * and they shall flow together to the good things of the Lord,

verses.lat: 31:14 Super fruménto, et vino, et óleo, * et fœtu pécorum et armentórum:
verses.eng: 31:14 For the corn, and wine, and oil, * and the increase of cattle and herds,

verses.lat: 31:15 Erítque ánima eórum quasi hortus irríguus, * et ultra non esúrient.
verses.eng: 31:15 And their soul shall be as a watered garden, * and they shall be hungry no more.

verses.lat: 31:16 Tunc lætábitur virgo in choro, * júvenes et senes simul:
verses.eng: 31:16 Then shall the virgin rejoice in the dance, * the young men and old men together:

verses.lat: 31:17 Et convértam luctum eórum in gáudium, * et consolábor eos, et lætificábo a dolóre suo.
verses.eng: 31:17 And I will turn their mourning into joy, * and will comfort them, and make them joyful after their sorrow.

verses.lat: 31:18 Et inebriábo ánimam sacerdótum pinguédine: * et pópulus meus bonis meis adimplébitur.
verses.eng: 31:18 And I will fill the soul of the priests with fatness: * and my people shall be filled with my good things.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Pópulus meus, * ait Dóminus, bonis meis adimplébitur.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: My people, * said the Lord, shall be filled with good things.

laudes.psalm4.label: Psalmus 146
laudes.psalm4.antiphonEng: To our God * be joyful and fitting praise.

verses.lat: 146:1 Laudáte Dóminum quóniam bonus est psalmus: * Deo nostro sit jucúnda, decóraque laudátio.
verses.eng: 146:1 Praise ye the Lord, because psalm is good: * to our God be joyful and comely praise.

verses.lat: 146:2 Ædíficans Jerúsalem Dóminus: * dispersiónes Israélis congregábit.
verses.eng: 146:2 The Lord buildeth up Jerusalem: * he will gather together the dispersed of Israel

verses.lat: 146:3 Qui sanat contrítos corde: * et álligat contritiónes eórum.
verses.eng: 146:3 Who healeth the broken of heart, * and bindeth up their bruises.

verses.lat: 146:4 Qui númerat multitúdinem stellárum: * et ómnibus eis nómina vocat.
verses.eng: 146:4 Who telleth the number of the stars: * and calleth them all by their names.

verses.lat: 146:5 Magnus Dóminus noster, et magna virtus ejus: * et sapiéntiæ ejus non est númerus.
verses.eng: 146:5 Great is our Lord, and great is his power: * and of his wisdom there is no number.

verses.lat: 146:6 Suscípiens mansuétos Dóminus: * humílians autem peccatóres usque ad terram.
verses.eng: 146:6 The Lord lifteth up the meek, * and bringeth the wicked down even to the ground.

verses.lat: 146:7 Præcínite Dómino in confessióne: * psállite Deo nostro in cíthara.
verses.eng: 146:7 Sing ye to the Lord with praise: * sing to our God upon the harp.

verses.lat: 146:8a Qui óperit cælum núbibus: * et parat terræ plúviam.
verses.eng: 146:8a Who covereth the heaven with clouds, * and prepareth rain for the earth.

verses.lat: 146:8b Qui prodúcit in móntibus fænum: * et herbam servitúti hóminum.
verses.eng: 146:8b Who maketh grass to grow on the mountains, * and herbs for the service of men.

verses.lat: 146:9 Qui dat juméntis escam ipsórum: * et pullis corvórum invocántibus eum.
verses.eng: 146:9 Who giveth to beasts their food: * and to the young ravens that call upon him.

verses.lat: 146:10 Non in fortitúdine equi voluntátem habébit: * nec in tíbiis viri beneplácitum erit ei.
verses.eng: 146:10 He shall not delight in the strength of the horse: * nor take pleasure in the legs of a man.

verses.lat: 146:11 Beneplácitum est Dómino super timéntes eum: * et in eis, qui sperant super misericórdia ejus.
verses.eng: 146:11 The Lord taketh pleasure in them that fear him: * and in them that hope in his mercy.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: To our God * be joyful and fitting praise.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (2 Cor 1:3-4)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Benedíctus Deus, et Pater Dómini nostri Jesu Christi, Pater misericordiárum, et Deus totíus consolatiónis, qui consolátur nos in omni tribulatióne nostra.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort, who comforteth us in all our tribulation.

capitulum_laudes.label: Capitulum (Rom 13:12-13)
capitulum_laudes.lat: Nox præcéssit, dies autem appropinquávit. Abiciámus ergo ópera tenebrárum, et induámur arma lucis. Sicut in die honéste ambulémus.
capitulum_laudes.eng: The night is passed, and the day is at hand. Let us therefore cast off the works of darkness, and put on the armour of light. Let us walk honestly, as in the day.

versum_tertia.label: Versiculus
versum_tertia.lat: ℣. Adjútor meus, esto, ne derelínquas me.
versum_tertia.eng: ℣. Be Thou my helper, forsake me not.
versum_tertia.latR: ℟. Neque despícias me, Deus, salutáris meus.
versum_tertia.engR: ℟. Do not Thou despise me, O God my Saviour.

versum_sexta.label: Versiculus
versum_sexta.lat: ℣. Dóminus regit me, et nihil mihi déerit.
versum_sexta.eng: ℣. The Lord ruleth me: and I shall want nothing.
versum_sexta.latR: ℟. In loco páscuæ ibi me collocávit.
versum_sexta.engR: ℟. He hath set me in a place of pasture.

versum_nona.label: Versiculus
versum_nona.lat: ℣. Ab occúltis meis munda me, Dómine.
versum_nona.eng: ℣. From my secret ones cleanse me, O Lord.
versum_nona.latR: ℟. Et ab aliénis parce servo tuo.
versum_nona.engR: ℟. And from those of others spare Thy servant.

ant_1.label: Antíphona
ant_1.lat: In Deo salutáre meum * et glória mea: et spes mea in Deo est.
ant_1.eng: In God is my salvation * and my glory: and my hope is in God.

ant_2.label: Antíphona
ant_2.lat: Exsúrgat Deus, * et dissipéntur inimíci ejus.
ant_2.eng: Let God arise, * and let his enemies be scattered.

ant_3.label: Antíphona
ant_3.lat: Salvum me fac, * Deus, quóniam intravérunt aquæ usque ad ánimam meam.
ant_3.eng: Save me, O God * for the waters are come in even unto my soul.

nocturn_1_versum.label: Versicle after Nocturn I
nocturn_1_versum.eng: ℣. God hath not turned away my prayer.

nocturn_2_versum.label: Versicle after Nocturn II
nocturn_2_versum.latR: ℟. Deus Israël dabit virtútem plebi suæ.
nocturn_2_versum.eng: ℣. God is wonderful in his saints.
nocturn_2_versum.engR: ℟. The God of Israel is he who will give power and strength to his people.

nocturn_3_versum.label: Versicle after Nocturn III
nocturn_3_versum.eng: ℣. I will praise the name of God.
nocturn_3_versum.engR: ℟. And I will magnify him with praise.

hymnus_laudes.label: Hymn
hymnus_laudes.title: Lux ecce surgit áurea
hymnus_laudes.lat:
Lux ecce surgit áurea,
Pallens facéssat cǽcitas,
Quæ nosmet in præceps diu
Erróre traxit dévio.

Hæc lux serénum cónferat,
Purósque nos præstet sibi:
Nihil loquámur súbdolum:
Volvámus obscúrum nihil.

Sic tota decúrrat dies,
Ne lingua mendax, ne manus
Oculíve peccent lúbrici,
Ne noxa corpus ínquinet.

Speculátor astat désuper,
Qui nos diébus ómnibus,
Actúsque nostros próspicit
A luce prima in vésperum.

Deo Patri sit glória,
Ejúsque soli Fílio,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
Nunc et per omne sǽculum.
Amen.
hymnus_laudes.eng:
See the golden sun arise!
Let no more our darkened eyes
Snare us, tangled by surprise
In the maze of sin!

From false words and thoughts impure
Let this light, serene and sure,
Keep our lips without secure,
Keep our souls within.

So may we the day-time spend,
That, till life’s temptations end,
Tongue, nor hand, nor eye offend!
One, above us all,

Views in his revealing ray
All we do, and think, and say,
Watching us from break of day
Till the twilight fall.

Unto God the Father, Son,
Holy Spirit, Three in One,
One in Three, be glory done,
Now and evermore.
Amen.

hymnus_vespera.label: Hymn
hymnus_vespera.title: Magnæ Deus poténtiæ
hymnus_vespera.lat:
Magnæ Deus poténtiæ,
Qui fértili natos aqua
Partim relínquis gúrgiti,
Partim levas in áëra.

Demérsa lymphis ímprimens,
Subvécta cælis érigens:
Ut stirpe ab una pródita,
Divérsa répleant loca:

Largíre cunctis sérvulis,
Quos mundat unda Sánguinis,
Nescíre lapsus críminum,
Nec ferre mortis tǽdium.

Ut culpa nullum déprimat:
Nullum éfferat jactántia:
Elísa mens ne cóncidat:
Eláta mens ne córruat.

Præsta, Pater piíssime,
Patríque compar Únice,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito
Regnans per omne sǽculum.
Amen.
hymnus_vespera.eng:
O sovereign Lord of nature’s might,
Who bad’st the water’s birth divide;
Part in the heavens to take their flight,
And part in ocean’s deep to hide;

These low obscured, on airy wing
Exalted those, that either race,
Though from one element they spring,
Might serve thee in a different place.

Grant, Lord, that we thy servants all,
Saved by thy tide of cleansing blood,
No more ’neath sin's dominion fall,
Nor fear the thought of death’s dark flood!

Thy varied love each spirit bless,
The humble cheer, the high control;
Check in each heart its proud excess,
But raise the meek and contrite soul!

This boon, O Father, we entreat,
This blessing grant, Eternal Son,
And Holy Ghost, the Paraclete,
Both now, and while the ages run.
Amen.

ant_laudes.label: Antiphon ad Benedictus
ant_laudes.lat: In sanctitáte * serviámus Dómino, et liberábit nos ab inimícis nostris.
ant_laudes.eng: In holiness * let us serve the Lord, and he will deliver us from our enemies.

ant_vespera.label: Antiphon ad Magnificat
ant_vespera.lat: Fecit Deus * poténtiam in brácchio suo: dispérsit supérbos mente cordis sui.
ant_vespera.eng: God has shown * the power of his arm: he has scattered the proud in the imagination of their hearts.

versum_1.label: Versicle
versum_1.eng: We are filled in the morning with thy mercy.
versum_1.engR: And we have rejoiced, and are delighted.
